For just as the Baptist said above: No one has ever seen God, the Son who is in the bosom of the father, he has declared him to us: so here he denies that they have known the father, because they have not known the Messiah himself. For although human minds know God in some way, because they have the knowledge of the law divinely implanted, and the Jews boasted of singular revelations and the wondrous works of God, published among this people, yet true knowledge of God cannot yet exist where only the law is known, which is a judgment concerning the will of God arguing and condemning sin, it does not show that secret will concerning the saving of the human race, which has only been revealed in the Gospel. For even if the law also says that God is good, merciful, etc., and has promises of bodily and eternal goods, yet it always adds a condition, it promises to the just and those keeping the law, conversely it testifies that God is angry, and wishes to condemn those who do not satisfy the law, it shows nothing of gratuitous mercy, that God wishes to remit sins to the unworthy, deserving wrath and death.

This secret will, or decree of the eternal father, was nowhere shown or brought forth, except by the Son of God himself, first in the promises which were made to Adam and the fathers, and afterwards by his own voice, when the Gospel was openly promulgated. And although in the Prophets there were repeated and declared promises concerning the Messiah, that he would be a future victim for the human race, on account of which God would wish to remit sins, and save those who believe: yet the Pharisees, and the greatest part of the people, did not even care to understand the testimonies of the Prophets, but with a carnal imagination they dreamed that the Messiah would have a bodily empire, would be a king flourishing in power, riches, worldly glory; of the secret counsel of God, that he was sent to abolish sin and death, so that he might restore eternal justice and life, they knew nothing at all. Wherefore Christ rightly says: You neither know me, nor my father, and if you had known me, you would have known my father also. He denies that he is known, because they have not known the promises published concerning the Messiah, nor are they moved by the testimonies of miracles, so that they might believe his voice. Therefore neither can the father be acknowledged by them, because through this Messiah alone the will of the father has been brought forth and revealed, concerning receiving and saving the human race, which when it is not acknowledged, it is necessary that minds remain in eternal darkness and eternal death,

On the other hand, he who knows Christ, that is, he who, having heard the voice of the Gospel, determines by faith that he is received by God on account of this Son the propitiator, and is gifted with eternal life, he now truly knows the Father, that is, he truly determines both things: that God is justly angry at sin, to such an extent that no other sacrifice could have appeased Him except the death of the only-begotten Son, and that the goodness and mercy of God are truly infinite and ineffable, because He freely forgives sins on account of the Son, and grants eternal life, despite the wrath and death that are deserved. This, finally, is to have truly known God, to apprehend with certain confidence the mercy and goodness which lifts up the heart, so that it ceases to flee from God, and is not angry at God, and hates Him—as must necessarily happen when, through the Law, the magnitude of sin and the wrath of God begins to become known to the mind, under which minds are oppressed by despair and rush into eternal death, unless they are recalled by the voice of the Gospel, which commands one to trust that God certainly forgives on account of the Son, and wills to save those who believe; by this voice the Holy Spirit is effective in believers. For once this confidence is conceived, they are freed from terrors, and a new light arises in them, apprehending God, which is the very beginning of eternal life. Therefore, concerning this recognition, Christ says in John 17: This is eternal life, that they may know you the true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus, to be Christ.

Latin:

Dicebant ei Iudaei: Ubi est pater tuus?

Iudaei ut eludant responsionem de testimo- nio, quaerunt de patre ubi sit, quasi dicant: Praeclare vero testimonium patris allegas, qui et abest, et ignotus est, age vero, si tibi credi po- stulas, coram sistas nobis patrem, ut ipsum de te testantem audiamus. Haec est calumniosa et vi- rulenta irrisio, quales sunt impiorum voces, qui odio veritatis impulsi a diabolo, audacter exerunt blasphemas linguas adversus aperta testimonia mi- raculorum, sed Christus de patre graviter respon- det: Si me novissetis, nossetis et patrem meum. Simplicissima sententia haec est, tum demum in- tellecturos esse de patre, quod vere testetur de hoc Messia, si credunt voci ipsius et miraculis, quibus ostendit ac probat se missum esse a patre aeterno, quare hoc dicto revocat eos ad testimo- nium verbi Dei et miraculorum: docet ad hoc, ut agnoscatur Deus, requiri fidem, seu assensum doctrinae traditae divinitus voce Patrum et Pro- phetarum de hoc Messia, nec posse recte iudicari de voluntate Dei, nisi quis prius assentietur huic verbo, propemodum, ut supra dixit: Si quis vo- let facere voluntatem patris mei, cognoscet de doctrina.

Sed hoc dictum complectitur etiam amplio- rem doctrinam de agnitione arcanae voluntatis Dei, de qua et alias dicitur, et infra saepe repe- tetur. Sicut enim supra dixit Baptista: Deum nemo vidit unquam, filius qui est in sinu patris, ipse enarravit nobis: ita hic negat eos patrem no- visse, quia ipsum Messiam non norint. Etsi enim mentes humanae aliquo modo norunt Deum, quia legis noticiam habent divinitus insitam, et Iudaei gloriabantur de singularibus revelationi- bus, et mirandis operibus Dei, editis in hoc po- pulo, tamen nondum potest existere vera noticia Dei, ubi tantum lex cognoscitur, quae est iudi- cium de voluntate Dei arguente et damnante pec- catum, non ostendit illam arcanam voluntatem de salvando genere humano, quae tantum patefacta est in Evangelio. Nam etiamsi et lex ait, Deum esse bonum, clementem etc., et habet promis- siones bonorum corporalium et aeternorum, ta- men semper addit conditionem, promittit iustis et servantibus legem, econtra testatur Deum ira- sci, et damnare velle hos, qui non satisfaciunt legi, nihil ostendit de gratuita misericordia, quod Deus velit remittere peccata indignis, meritis iram et mortem.

Haec arcana voluntas, seu decretum aeterni patris, nusquam ostensum aut prolatum est, nisi ab ipso filio Dei, primum in promissionibus, quae factae sunt Adae et patribus, et postea sua ipsius voce, palam promulgato Evangelio. Etsi autem in Prophetis erant repetitae et enarratae promis- siones de Messia, quod esset victima futurus pro genere humano, propter quam Deus vellet remit- tere peccata, et salvare credentes: tamen Phari- saei, et maxima pars populi ne curabant quidem intelligere Prophetarum testimonia, sed carnali imaginatione somniabant Messiam habiturum im- perium corporale, futurum regem florentem po- tentia, opibus, gloria mundana, de arcano con- silio Dei, quod missus esset ad abolendum pecca- tum et mortem, ut restitueret aeternam iusticiam et vitam, nihil prorsus norant, Quare recte ait Christus: Neque me nostis, neque patrem meum, et si me nossetis, novissetis et patrem. Negat se cognosci, quia promissiones editas de Messia non norint, nec moveantur testimoniis miraculorum, ut credant voci ipsius. Ideo neque patrem ab ipsis posse agnosci, quia per hunc solum Messiam prolata et patefacta est voluntas patris, de reci- piendo et salvando genere humano, quae cum non agnoscitur, necesse est mentes manere in aeternis tenebris et morte aeterna,

Econtra, qui Christum novit, hoc est, qui audita voce Evangelii, fide statuit se propter hunc filium propiciatorem recipi a Deo, et donari vita aeterna, is iam vere novit patrem, hoc est, vere statuit utrumque, et Deum iuste irasci peccato, adeo, ut nulla alia hostia, praeterquam unigeniti filii morte, placari potuerit, et vere esse infinitam et ineffabilem bonitatem et misericordiam Dei, quod gratis propter filium remittat peccata, et reddat vitam aeternam, meritis iram et mortem. Hoc demum est vere novisse Deum, certa fiducia apprehendere misericordiam et bonitatem, quae erigit cor, ut desinat fugere Deum, nec irascatur Deo, et oderit eum, sicut necesse est fieri, cum per legem incipit innotescere menti magnitudo peccati et irae Dei, sub qua opprimuntur mentes desperatione, et ruunt in mortem aeternam, nisi revocentur voce Evangelii, quae iubet confidere, quod certo propter filium Deus ignoscat, et velit salvare credentes, hac voce efficax est Spiritus sanctus in credentibus. Nam concepta hac fidu- cia, liberantur a terroribus, et oritur in eis nova lux, apprehendens Deum, quae est ipsa incoatio vitae aeternae. Ideo de hac agnitione ait Chri- stus Ioan. 17.: Haec est vita aeterna, ut cogno- scant te verum Deum, et hunc quem misisti Ie- sum esse Christum.

## 8:20
He spoke these words to them in the treasury.

It was said above about the snares laid for Christ by the Pharisees, which, although they were frustrated, nevertheless they did not for that reason cease to lay snares, especially since He was now increasing the offenses, because He continues to teach and openly refutes the opinions of the Pharisees. It is signified, therefore, that they, now more irritated, had absolutely decided to seize Christ, and that the opportunity for this matter had come from the convenience of the place, where He could easily be seized, as He was teaching at the treasury, which place, as Josephus writes, was not in the inner or more sacred temple, but at the very entrance, under the porticoes, and it was permitted to be approached indiscriminately by the whole multitude. And yet the attempt of the Pharisees is in vain, and Christ is defended without any human protection, nor is power given to them to do harm when they wish, and the reason is added: Because His hour had not yet come, which teaches that the pious who are doing their duty are defended by God, and that there are miraculous deliverances by which the counsels of adversaries are made void, and however certain and prepared the snares may be, they are frustrated for as long as God wills the pious to perform their duty. Just as He miraculously saved Daniel when he was exposed to the lions, and David is snatched away from Saul several times, as if from his very jaws. Let these examples confirm us also, so that we may not be deterred by the fear of enemies from confession or other struggles, nor flee from similar dangers, but let us ourselves also expect defense from God; as Christ teaching is not seized, so let us know that God will also defend us while we are doing our duty, until we finish the course of our vocation, and that the attempts of the adversaries will not succeed as long as God wills us to perform the duty of our vocation.

Latin:

Haec verba locutus est eis in gazophylacio.

Supra dictum est de insidiis structis Christo a Pharisaeis, quae tametsi erant frustratae, tamen non ideo desinebant insidiari, praesertim cum iam augeret offensiones, quia pergit docere, et palam refutat Pharisaeorum opiniones. Significa- tur igitur illos iam magis irritatos, prorsus con- stituisse Christum prehendere, et ad hanc rem accessisse occasionem ex commoditate loci, ubi facile potuit prehendi, cum doceret ad gazophy- lacium, qui locus, ut scribit Iosephus, erat non in interiore seu sacratiore templo, sed in ipso ingressu, sub porticibus, ac licebat promiscue ab omni multitudine adiri. Et tamen frustra est Pharisaeorum conatus, et defenditur Christus, sine ullo humano praesidio, nec datur illis pote- stas nocendi, cum volunt, et additur ratio: Quia nondum venit hora eius, quae docet, divinitus defendi pios facientes suum officium, et esse mi- randas liberationes, quibus irrita fiunt consilia adversariorum, et quantumvis certae ac paratae insidiae, frustrantur tam diu, dum Deus vult pios fungi suo munere. Sicut mirabiliter serva- vit Danielem obiectum leonibus, et David aliquo- ties eripitur Sauli, tanquam ex faucibus. Haec exempla confirment et nos, ne deterreamur metu hostium a confessione, aut aliis certaminibus, nec defugiamus similia pericula, sed et ipsi a Deo ex- pectemus defensionem, ut Christus docens non prehenditur, ita sciamus Deum et nos defensu- rum esse facientes officium, donec absolvamus cursum nostrae vocationis, nec successuros esse conatus adversariorum, quamdiu Deus vult nos fungi munere vocationis.

## 8:21
Jesus therefore said again: I am going.

It is a sad and horrible threat concerning the punishment of the neglected and despised Gospel, such as many are read everywhere. He spoke of His benefit, He exhorted the people to receive this light, which frees them from errors and eternal death, and brings perpetual life and happiness; He also alleged testimonies concerning His vocation and His office, that He was sent by the Father, but when He sees these things being despised and mocked by the Pharisees, who were swelling with the persuasion of their own wisdom and justice, He adds a prediction concerning the punishments, namely, because they despise the doctrine and the heavenly benefit, greater darkness and everlasting destruction will follow; He says that He is going away because they do not wish to hear Him and receive the offered liberation: this is the first degree of punishments, to lose the voice of the Gospel, which alone is salutary and life-giving; afterwards, being destitute of this light or recognition of Christ, He says they will remain in darkness and errors, and will seek consolation in vain, and finally that punishments will follow which will submerge them into destruction. Nothing can be said more horrible than this voice: You will seek me, and you will die in your sin. For it signifies especially this sin, namely, the neglect of the Gospel and the contempt of the benefits which the Son of God brings, draws with it blindness and extreme destruction, just as in the Prophets these punishments are described in the saddest words, Psalm 109: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and pour out your wrath upon them, let their house be desolate, let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and let them not be written with the righteous. And experience testifies in all ages that the contempt of the Gospel has been punished in the same ways with extreme devastation and destruction, just as the fury and stubbornness of the Jews against Christ destroyed the whole nation most miserably. Afterwards also in the Church, the neglect of pure doctrine and εἰδωλομανίαι were punished are by the horrible devastation of Mahometan cruelty and fury.

Let us therefore learn to acknowledge how great a benefit it is to have the doctrine of the Gospel and the knowledge of Christ, and let us take care that we do not, by our own fault, lose this light and bring punishments upon ourselves, but let us pray to God that He may preserve this heavenly gift. For these sentences testify that it is impossible to avoid darkness and errors, nor to be freed from punishments, except for those who retain by faith the knowledge of Christ, which the doctrine of the Gospel delivers.

Will he kill himself? etc.

See what obstinate impiety does? They receive such a sad warning, which ought to be deprecated with tears and true repentance, with jeers and bitter sarcasm. Will he kill himself? etc., as if they were saying: What tricks is he preparing, since he wants to hide himself in such a way that we cannot follow him; namely, is he going to kill himself so that he may not appear anywhere? These are the poisonous voices of the enemies of Christ, so that through mockery they even insult Him hanging on the cross for the human race: If he is the Son of God, let him save himself, let him come down from the cross. Thus, they mock Him who is exhorting to repentance and faith with virulent words: Let him go indeed where he wants, let him kill himself, let him perish, let us see if anyone is going to look for him. Thus the flock of the chief priests and Pharisees responds to the Messiah sent by God, who do not bear being stripped of the glory of their own righteousness, do not want to be accused of blindness for being ignorant of how one arrives at God; they see the title of the Church and the people of God being attributed to them, and proud of this glory, they securely mock the voice of the Gospel, which convicts their unbelief and predicts the judgment of God and punishments.

The chief cause of hatred is against the Gospel, and this voice of Christ has always produced the sharpest offenses: Where I go, you cannot come. For it detracts from the glory of wisdom and righteousness of those who have the doctrine of the law, who have worship and governance in the Church or the people of God, when it denies that men are righteous and please God on account of the law, just as now the pontifical assembly rages that the reputation of righteousness is being detracted from them on account of the worship of traditions, and that the power of establishing laws and traditions is being taken away. Therefore, when they hear such voices, that we are not justified by the law, that traditions are not worship pleasing to God, they furiously persecute the pious and curse the Gospel. But

The example of Christ admonishes the pious not to be deterred by such reproaches, curses, and jeers from the confession of sound doctrine, according to that of Isaiah 52: Do not fear the reproaches of men.

Latin:

Dixit igitur iterum Iesus: Ego vado.

Tristis et horrenda comminatio est de poena neglecti et contemti Evangelii, quales multae pas- sim leguntur. Dixit de suo beneficio, hortatus est populum, ut accipiant hanc lucem, quae libe- rat eos ab erroribus et morte aeterna, et affert perpetuam vitam et felicitatem, allegavit et testi- monia de vocatione et munere suo, quod sit mis- sus a patre, sed cum videt haec contemni et rideri a Pharisaeis, tumentibus persuasione sapientiae et iusticiae, addit praedictionem de poenis, vide- delicet, quia contemnant doctrinam et beneficium coeleste, secuturas esse maiores tenebras et exi- tium sempiternum, ait se abire, quia nolint ipsum audire et accipere oblatam liberationem: hic primus gradus est poenarum, amittere vocem Evangelii, quae una est salutaris et vivifica, postea destitutos hac luce seu agnitione Christi, ait hae- suros esse in tenebris et erroribus, et frustra quaesituros consolationem, et tandem secuturas esse poenas, quae demergant ipsos in exitium. Nihil potest dici horribilius hac voce: Quaeritis me, et in peccato vestro moriemini. Significat enim praecipue hoc peccatum, videlicet neglectio- nem Evangelii et contemtum beneficiorum, quae affert filius Dei, trahere secum caecitatem et ex- tremum exitium, sicut in Prophetis tristissimis verbis hae poenae describuntur, Psalm. 109.: Ob- scurentur oculi eorum, ne videant, et funde super eos iram tuam, fiat domus eorum deserta, de- leantur de libro viventium, et cum iustis non scribantur. Et experientia testatur omnibus aeta- tibus iisdem modis punitum esse contemtum Evan- gelii extrema vastitate et exitio, sicut Iudaeorum furor et pertinacia contra Christum totam gentem miserrime perdidit. Postea etiam in Ecclesia ne- glectio purae doctrinae et εἰδωλομανίαι punitae sunt horribili vastatione immanitatis et furoris Mahometici.

Discamus ergo agnoscere, quantum sit bene- ficium habere doctrinam Evangelii et noticiam Christi, ac caveamus, ne nostro vitio hanc lucem amittamus, et accersamus nobis poenas, sed ore- mus Deum, ut servet hoc munus coeleste. Nam hae sententiae testantur non posse vitare tenebras et errores, nec liberari a poenis, nisi hos, qui fide retinent noticiam Christi, quam tradit do- ctrina Evangelii.

Nunquid interficiet seipsum? etc.

Vide, quid faciat obstinata impietas? tam tristem comminationem lacrymis et vera poeniten- tia deprecandam, excipiunt sannis, et amarulento sarcasmo. Nunquid interficiet seipsum etc., quasi dicant: Quas praestigias parat, cum ita se occul- tare vult, ut non possimus eum sequi, videlicet, seipsum interfecturus est, ne usquam appareat? Hae sunt venenatae voces hostium Christi, ut per ludibrium etiam insultent pendenti in cruce pro genere humano: Si filius Dei est, salvet semet- ipsum, descendat de cruce. Ita hic hortantem ad poenitentiam et fidem, irrident virulentis di- ctis: Eat sane, quo vult, interficiat seipsum, pe- reat, videat nunquis ipsum quaesiturus sit. Sic respondet Messiae misso a Deo grex Pontificum et Pharisaeorum, qui non ferunt se exui gloria pro- priae iusticiae, nolunt accusari caecitatis, quod ignorent quomodo perveniatur ad Deum, vident sibi deferri titulum Ecclesiae et populi Dei, hac gloria superbientes secure irrident vocem Evan- gelii, quae arguit ipsorum incredulitatem, et praedicit de iudicio Dei ac poenis.

Praecipua odii causa est adversus Evange- lium, ac semper acerrimas offensiones peperit haec vox Christi: Quo ego vado, vos non potestis venire. Derogat enim gloriam sapientiae et iusti- ciae, his, qui habent doctrinam legis, habent cultus et gubernationem in Ecclesia seu populo Dei, cum negat homines iustos esse, et placere Deo, propter legem, sicut nunc coetus pontificius fremit sibi detrahi existimationem iusticiae pro- pter cultus traditionum, adimi potestatem con- dendi leges et traditiones. Ideo cum audiunt ta- les voces, quod non iustificemur lege, quod tra- ditiones non sint cultus placentes Deo, furenter, persequuntur pios, et maledicunt Evangelio. Sed

Christi exemplum admonet pios, ne talibus con- viciis, maledictis, sannis, deterreantur a con- fessione sanae doctrinae, iuxta illud Esaiae 52.: Convicia hominum nolite metuere.

## 8:23
You are from below, I am from above.

He adds the reason for His statement. I rightly said: where I am going, you cannot follow, and it is no wonder that you are not moved to repentance and faith, but rather are hardened when you hear my sermons; there is a huge difference between you and me; you are from the infernal regions, or as He Himself interprets, from this world, that is, you only know, approve, and follow those things which the world and reason judge to be wisdom and righteousness, and when you perform some discipline or worship of works, which reason understands and can accomplish, you think you have performed excellently and are already righteous before God; you do not know the will of God concerning the magnitude of sin, which clings to human nature, on account of which it is subject to the wrath of God and eternal punishments, nor concerning mercy, how He wishes to save the human race.

On the contrary, I am from above, sent by God; I bring heavenly doctrine, I reveal the secret will of God, unknown to reason, concerning the remission of sins, concerning the restoration of eternal life, etc. Because you do not accept this, I rightly judge that you are not from above, but are from the world, that is, without spiritual light, without the knowledge of God, or wisdom discerning and glorifying God, without righteousness, and finally, that you remain in darkness and in death. For although reason has some knowledge of the law and performs some political virtues, nevertheless this very wisdom and carnal righteousness, such as it is, is subject to the wrath of God and eternal death, nor are men freed unless they believe this voice which the Son of God brings from heaven, which testifies that He was sent by the Father and took on human nature so that He might become a victim for sin, which would appease the wrath of God and abolish eternal death. Reborn by this faith, they themselves are also no longer of this world, because they have been freed through Christ. The rest, because they do not believe the Gospel, are not freed from sin and from death, but remain guilty and condemned before God. Therefore, Christ repeats the previous conclusion.

Latin:

Vos deorsum estis, ego de supernis sum.

Addit rationem sui dicti. Recte dixi: quo ego abeo, vos non posse sequi, nec mirum est, vos non flecti ad poenitentiam et fidem, sed ma- gis indurari, cum auditis meas conciones, ingens discrimen est inter vos et me, vos de infernis estis, seu ut ipse interpretatur, de hoc mundo, hoc est, ea tantum nostis, probatis, sectamini, quae mundus et ratio iudicat esse sapientiam, iu- sticiam, et cum praestatis aliquam disciplinam, aut cultus operum, quae ratio intelligit, et effi- cere potest, putatis vos praeclare defunctos esse, et iam esse iustos coram Deo, non nostis volun- tatem Dei, de magnitudine peccati, quod haeret in natura humana, propter quod subiecta est irae Dei et poenis aeternis, nec de misericordia, quo- modo velit salvare genus humanum.

Econtra ego de supernis sum missus a Deo, affero doctrinam coelestem, patefacio arcanam voluntatem Dei, ignotam rationi, de remissione peccatorum, de restitutione vitae aeternae etc. Hanc quia non accipitis, recte iudico vos non esse de supernis, sed esse de mundo, hoc est, sine luce spirituali, sine agnitione Dei, seu sa- pientia cernente et glorificante Deum, sine iusti- cia, denique manere in tenebris et in morte. Nam etsi ratio habet aliquam noticiam legis, et praestat aliquas virtutes politicas, tamen haec ipsa qualiscunque sapientia et iusticia carnalis, est subiecta irae Dei et morti aeternae, nec liberan- tur homines, nisi credant huic voci, quam affert filius Dei e coelo, quae testatur ipsum esse mis- sum a patre, et induisse humanam naturam, ut fieret victima pro peccato, quae placaret iram Dei, et aboleret mortem aeternam. Hac fide renati etiam ipsi iam non sunt de hoc mundo, quia per Christum liberati sunt. Reliqui, quia non cre- dunt Evangelio, non liberantur a peccato et a morte, sed manent rei et damnati coram Deo. Ideo Christus repetit superiorem conclusionem.

## 8:24
Unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sin.

He declares clearly that there is no way, no remedy for emerging from eternal death, except faith, which establishes that we, on account of this mediator sent by God, are received and saved, not the law, not the worship of works, not human virtues deliver from sin and from external punishments, even if some excellent and heroic men have remarkable decorations, even if a Pharisee excels many others, yet, because he is without faith, he does not please God, he is not delivered from eternal death; on the contrary, a miserable sinful woman, or a thief hanging on the cross, although they do not bring merits, yet because in repentance they flee by faith to this Lord, they truly obtain the remission of sins and eternal life. In others, where there is no recognition or faith of the reconciliation promised on account of this mediator, it is necessary that eternal wrath follow, because otherwise the whole human race is oppressed by sin, and guilty before God, as Paul says: We were by nature children of wrath. Likewise: All have sinned, or are guilty, and furthermore unbelief is added, which accumulates sin, and hinders the reconciliation or remission from being able to be received. For in those who believe, sin has already been remitted, and what remains clinging to nature is governed by faith, so that it does not condemn, as was said above: He who believes in the Son is not judged. On the contrary, as it is said there: He who does not believe is already judged, because he does not believe in the Son of God. Thus he says here: If you do not believe that I am, you will die in your sin.

Latin:

Nisi credideritis, quod ego sum, moriemini in peccato vestro.

Clare pronunciat, nullam esse viam, nullum remedium emergendi ex morte aeterna, nisi fidem, quae statuit nos propter hunc propiciatorem mis- sum a Deo, recipi et salvari, non lex, non cul- tus operum, non virtutes humanae liberant a pec- cato et a poenis externis, etiamsi aliqui excellen- tes et heroici viri habent egregia decora, etiamsi Pharisaeus praestat multis aliis, tamen, quia est sine fide, non placet Deo, non liberatur a morte aeterna, econtra misera mulier peccatrix, aut la- tro pendens in cruce, etsi non afferunt merita, tamen quia in poenitentia fide confugiunt ad hunc dominum, vere consequuntur remissionem pec- catorum et vitam aeternam. In aliis, ubi non est agnitio seu fides reconciliationis promissae propter hunc mediatorem, necesse est sequi aeter- nam iram, quia et alioqui universum genus hu- manum oppressum est peccato, et reum coram Deo, sicut Paulus inquit: Eramus natura filii irae. Item: Omnes peccaverunt, seu rei sunt, et prae- terea accedit incredulitas, quae cumulat peccatum, et impedit, quo minus reconciliatio, seu remissio accipi possit. Nam in his, qui credunt, pecca- tum iam remissum est, et quod reliquum haeret in natura, regitur fide, ut non damnet, sicut su- pra dictum est: Qui credit in filium, non iudica- tur. Econtra, ut illic dicitur: Qui non credit, iam iudicatus est, quia non credit in filium Dei. Ita hic ait: Si non credideritis, quod ego sum, moriemini in peccato vestro.

## 8:25
They said therefore: Who are you?

The Pharisees understand that Christ speaks magnificently about himself; they had heard what he said, that he was sent by the Father. Likewise, that he is from above, finally when he says: Unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sin. This, however, they judge to be an unbearable arrogance, because he openly prefers himself to all the remaining teachers, Prophets, nay even to Moses himself and the fathers. And although they judge the utterance to be blasphemous, yet they think it should rather be exploded with laughter and jeers. Wherefore, to his most grave sermon, as if unworthy of a response, they submit nothing else than this utterance: Who are you? And this very utterance is nothing else than a sign of mocking by those who deride, as if they were saying: What do you take upon yourself? Are you not ashamed of your arrogance? Or do you really dare to demand that you be believed when saying such absurd things? These are jeers not unlike those of the men who, spitting upon Christ, afterwards salute him as king.

Latin:

Dicebant igitur: Tu quis es?

Intelligunt Pharisaei Christum magnifice de sese loqui, audierant quod dixit, se missum a patre. Item, esse de supernis, denique cum in- quit: Nisi credideritis, quod ego sum, moriemi- ni in peccato vestro. Hanc vero iudicant non fe- rendam esse arrogantiam, quia sese palam ante- ferat omnibus reliquis doctoribus, Prophetis, imo ipsi Mosi et patribus. Etsi autem iudicant vocem esse blasphemam, tamen potius ducunt risu et cachinnis esse explodendam. Quare ad eius gra- vissimam concionem, quasi indignum responso nihil aliud subiiciunt, quam hanc vocem: Quis es tu? Estque haec ipsa vox nihil aliud, nisi significatio per ludibrium irridentium, quasi di- cant: Ecquid tibi sumis? non pudet te arrogan- tiae? an vero audes postulare, ut tibi credatur tam absurda dicenti? Hi sunt cachinni non dis- similes illorum, qui conspuentes Christum, postea salutant regem.

## 8:25
In the beginning, that which I also speak to you.

The interpretation of the word 'principle' in this place, concerning the divinity of Christ, is foreign, having arisen from a not sufficiently learned version. For the text does not mean this, that Christ calls himself the principle, but in Greek it is a customary phrase in the expression τὴν ἀρχὴν, which is wont to be used as an adverb, as we say: 'in the beginning' or 'first of all', or 'before all things', or 'altogether'; so here also let it be accepted as 'in the beginning', I am this very thing which I speak, as if he were saying: You may indeed laugh, yet I affirm to you that I am this very one whom I have said: This must be done by you before all things, that you recognize me to be a teacher sent by the Father, bringing the word and command of the Father, so that you may believe me. This word must first be heard, and received by faith, then finally you will know who I am.

This is, in my judgment, the simplest meaning of this saying, 'I am altogether what I speak', that is, I am the person speaking, bringing the word of the eternal God, which indeed delivers useful doctrine. Christ recalls us to the word, and teaches that he is known in this way, if we believe this voice, which has been brought by the Son of God, and is propagated through the ministry of the Gospel. He does not want us to follow human imaginations, or the judgment of rational wisdom, concerning the will and works of God, nor to seek other revelations, or illuminations outside the word, but he binds us to the voice of the Gospel concerning Christ, which has certain and firm testimonies of the universal Church, from then on from the beginning of the world, of the Fathers, Prophets, Christ, and the Apostles. Finally, it is confirmed by the testimonies of the miracles of the sent Holy Spirit, etc. To these testimonies God wants the pious to look, and thus finally he is apprehended and recognized, when we believe this word, which the Son of God brings, through which the Holy Spirit is effective in minds, kindles a new light, and instructs pious minds concerning both things, namely, concerning the wrath of God against sin, and again concerning his immense mercy, when they contemplate the admirable counsel of God, who willed that his Son become a victim for the sins of the human race. This is the true and spiritual knowledge of God, and this faith in true struggles brings firm consolation, and raises up minds, so that they shake off doubt, and overcome terrors, and hearts, having conceived this light and consolation, now begin truly to call upon God, and perform true spiritual worship.

On the contrary, where minds, having neglected this voice of the Gospel, wander with their own imaginations, and either from reason, or from the doctrine of the law judge concerning God, it is necessary to be entangled in many ways in darkness and errors. For they either rush securely into manifest profanity and Epicurean frenzies, or if they retain the doctrine of the law, they dream that they are righteous by some simulation of obedience toward the law. Afterwards, when they fall into terrors, they cannot struggle out, but are oppressed by doubt, which brings other horrible sins, despair, hatred of God, blasphemies. Finally, outside of this word, true light and knowledge of God cannot exist, nor do they ever understand or experience true consolation in terrors, and true spiritual movements, except for those who receive by faith this voice of the Gospel brought forth by the Son of God. Wherefore Scripture warns everywhere that we should not allow ourselves to be led away from the word by the snares of the devil, or by other illusions which can be cast in our way, so that we might trust in human wisdom or seek other secret revelations outside the word, just as it is commanded in Deut.: Do not say, who ascends into heaven, the word is near, in your mouth. Likewise, Isa. 8: To the law and to the testimony, but if they do not speak according to this word: There will be no morning light for them. And the Psalm: Your word is a lamp to my feet, etc.

Latin:

Principio, quod et loquor vobis.

Aliena est hoc loco interpretatio vocabuli principium, de divinitate Christi, orta ex non satis erudita versione. Nam textus non hoc vult, quod Christus se vocet principium, sed Graece est usitata phrasis in voce τὴν ἀρχὴν, quae solet pro adverbio usurpari, ut nos dicimus: principio aut inprimis, seu ante omnia, seu prorsus, ita hic quoque accipiatur principio, hoc ipsum sum quod loquor, quasi dicat: Rideatis sane, ego ta- men affirmo vobis me esse hunc ipsum, quem dixi: Hoc ante omnia vobis agendum est, ut me agnoscatis esse doctorem missum a patre, afferen- tem verbum et mandatum patris, ut mihi creda- tis. Hoc verbum primum audiendum est, et ac- cipiendum fide, ita demum cognoscetis quis sim.

Haec est meo iudicio simplicissima sententia huius dicti, prorsus sum, quod loquor, id est, sum persona loquens, afferens verbum aeterni Dei, quod quidem tradit utilem doctrinam. Re- vocat nos Christus ad verbum, et docet ita se co- gnosci, si huic voci credamus, quae est allata a filio Dei, et propagatur per ministerium Evange- lii. Non vult nos sequi humanas imaginationes, aut iudicium sapientiae rationalis, de voluntate et operibus Dei, nec quaerere alias revelationes, aut illuminationes extra verbum, sed alligat nos ad vocem Evangelii de Christo, quae habet certa et firma testimonia universae Ecclesiae, inde us- que ab initio mundi, Patrum, Prophetarum, Christi et Apostolorum. Denique confirmata est testimoniis miraculorum missi Spiritus sancti etc. Ad haec testimonia vult Deus respicere pios, et ita demum apprehenditur et agnoscitur, cum cre- dimus huic verbo, quod affert filius Dei, per quod efficax est Spiritus sanctus in mentibus, ac- cendit novam lucem, et erudit pias mentes de utraque re, videlicet, de ira Dei adversus pecca- tum, et rursus de immensa misericordia, cum in- tuentur admirandum consilium Dei, quod filium voluit victimam fieri pro peccatis generis humani. Haec est vera et spiritualis noticia Dei, et haec fides in veris certaminibus affert firmam consola- tionem, et erigit mentes, ut excutiant dubitatio- nem, et vincant terrores, et corda, concepta hac luce et consolatione, iam incipiunt vere invocare Deum, et praestant veros cultus spirituales.

Econtra ubi mentes neglecta hac voce Evan- gelii vagantur suis imaginationibus, et vel ex ratione, vel ex doctrina legis iudicant de Deo, necesse est multipliciter implicari tenebris et erroribus. Aut enim securae ruunt in manifestam profanitatem et furores epicureos, aut si retinent doctrinam legis, somniant se iustos qualicunque simulatione obedientiae erga legem. Postea cum incidunt in terrores, non possunt eluctari, sed opprimuntur dubitatione, quae affert alia horribilia peccata, desperationem, odium Dei, blasphemias. Denique extra hoc verbum non potest existere vera lux et noticia Dei, nec unquam intelligunt, aut experiuntur veram consolationem in terroribus, et veros motus spirituales, nisi hi, qui hanc vocem Evangelii prolatam a filio Dei fide accipiunt. Quare passim monet scriptura, ne sinamus nos abduci a verbo insidiis diaboli, aut aliis praestigiis, quae obiici possunt, ut confidamus humana sapientia aut quaeramus alias arcanas revelationes extra verbum, sicut in Deut. praecipitur: Ne dicas, quis ascendit in coelum, prope est verbum, in ore tuo. Item, Esai. 8.: Ad legem et ad testimonium, quod si non dixerint, iuxta verbum hoc: Non erit eis matutina lux. Et Psalmus: Lucerna pedibus meis verbum tuum, etc.

## 8:26
I have many things to say and to judge concerning you.

With a brief response he refuted the insulting questions of the Pharisees. He confessed that he was the Son of God, sent by the Father, according to the promises, and that he brought heavenly doctrine, and the word handed down by the Father, and thus revealed this will of God, that not on account of the law, but only on account of this Son, he wishes to save those who believe, and that men are not otherwise freed from eternal death, except by faith in this Lord, sent by the eternal Father, so that through him the Church might be gathered and saved; now he repeats the threat: I have many things to say and to judge concerning you, as if he were saying: Although you are convinced by the manifest testimonies of my calling, and by my own voice, by which I prove that I am sent by the Father, and that I bring his word, yet you knowingly resist the truth, and you do not wish to believe, and you continue to hate me, and you treat me with insult. But this obstinacy will not deter me from continuing to perform my duty. Indeed, the more you oppose me, the more I will continue to defend the office handed down to me by the heavenly Father, namely, to propagate the voice of the Gospel, and to accuse and condemn your unbelief. Nor do I take this judgment upon myself, just as you justly and without cause condemn me, indeed against manifest divine testimonies, but by the command and authority of the Father I perform this office, so that by the word I may argue and judge all who do not believe the Gospel; it is necessary that all men be subjected to this word, just as he says elsewhere: The Holy Spirit will convict the world of sin, because they do not believe in me. Wherefore do not think that you will bear this contempt with impunity, or that my sermons will be in vain; the sentence has already been passed, and by my ministry it will be promulgated to the whole world, which declares that all who do not believe this voice of mine are judged and condemned by God, nor will your boasting, by the confidence of which you persecute me, profit you, that you are the people of God, that you have been gifted with the chief benefits of miracles, of the given law, of promises, of the priesthood, of the temple, etc. Indeed, because you continue to rage against the Gospel, it will come to pass that you will not even retain these things, but will lose them, and this polity of yours and eternal goods.

In this way he answers the contemners concerning his office, with the addition of a threat concerning the effect; he said that he was the person speaking, bringing the word of the eternal Father, and he says that this word will be effective against the contemners, namely, that by it those who do not believe the Gospel are judged, or condemned and punished. For he signifies that not by human or bodily force, but by divine power he will propagate the word and will cause it to be effective against the power and frenzies of the enemies of the Gospel. To this statement he adds an occupation.

But he who sent me is truthful, and what I have heard from him, I speak, etc.

As if he were saying: Although I am now mocked by you, and am not heard speaking about the Father, yet he himself will testify that I have spoken the truth; my voice will be effective, both for saving those who believe, and for condemning the contemners. You will not make him a liar, even if you continue to contemn my voice, because I know that I bring his word, and that I perform this office by his command; wherefore you will experience that the voice was not in vain, when I argue and judge your unbelief, because it is brought forth not by my sentence and command, but by the Father's. By this statement he not only comforts himself against those who proudly and securely contemn the Gospel, but also confirms the pious, so that they may know that God will certainly be effective through the ministry of this voice, because it has been produced and brought forth by the Son of God himself at the command of the eternal Father.

Latin:

Multa habeo de vobis loqui, et iudicare.

Brevi responsione refutavit contumeliosas percontationes Pharisaeorum. Fassus est se esse filium Dei, missum a patre, iuxta promissiones, et afferre doctrinam coelestem, et verbum traditum a patre, adeoque patefacere hanc voluntatem Dei, quod non propter legem, sed tantum propter hunc filium velit salvare credentes, nec aliter liberari homines a morte aeterna, nisi fide huius domini, missi ab aeterno patre, ut per ipsum colligatur, et salvetur Ecclesia, nunc repetit comminationem: Multa habeo de vobis loqui et iudicare, quasi dicat: Etsi convincimini manifestis testimoniis meae vocationis, et mea ipsius voce, qua probo me missum esse a patre, et afferre ipsius verbum, tamen scientes repugnatis veritati, nec vultis credere, et pergitis me odisse, et contumelia afficitis. Verum haec obstinatio non deterrebit me, quo minus pergam facere meum officium. Imo quo magis vos adversabimini, eo magis pergam tueri munus mihi traditum a patre coelesti, videlicet, propagare vocem Evangelii, et accusare et damnare incredulitatem vestram. Nec ipse sumo mihi hoc iudicium, sicut vos iuste et sine causa me damnatis, imo contra manifesta testimonia divina, sed mandato et autoritate pa- tris fungor hoc munere, ut verbo arguam et iu- dicem omnes, qui non credunt Evangelio, huic verbo necesse est subiici omnes homines, sicut alibi ait: Spiritus sanctus arguet mundum de peccato, quia non credunt in me. Quare nolite cogitare, vos impune laturos esse hunc contem- tum, aut meas conciones irritas fore, iam lata est sententia, et meo ministerio promulgabitur in universum orbem, quae pronunciat iudicari et damnari a Deo omnes, qui non credunt huic meae voci, nec proderit vobis gloriatio, cuius fiducia me persequimini, quod sitis populus Dei, quod sitis donati praecipuis beneficiis miraculorum, da- tae legis, promissionum, sacerdotii, templi, etc. Imo quia pergitis contra Evangelium furere, fu- turum est, ut ne haec quidem retineatis, sed amittatis, et hanc politiam vestram et aeterna bona.

Hoc modo respondet contemtoribus de suo officio, addita comminatione de effectu, dixit se esse personam loquentem, afferentem verbum aeterni patris, et hoc verbum ait efficax fore ad- versus contemtores, videlicet, ut eo iudicentur, seu damnentur et puniantur non credentes Evan- gelio. Significat enim non vi humana seu corpo- rali, sed divina potentia se propagaturum esse verbum et facturum, ut sit efficax contra poten- tiam et furores hostium Evangelii. Huic dicto addit occupationem.

Sed qui me misit, verax est, et quae audivi ex eo, loquor, etc.

Quasi dicat: Etsi iam rideor a vobis, nec au- dior de patre loquens, tamen ipse testabitur me vera dixisse, erit efficax mea voce, et ad salvan- dos credentes, et damnandos contemtores. Hunc non facietis mendacem, etiamsi pergitis contem- nere meam vocem, quia scio me afferre ipsius verbum, et eius mandato fungi hoc munere, quare experiemini non fuisse irritam vocem, cum arguo et iudico vestram incredulitatem, quia non mea, sed patris sententia et mandato profertur. Hoc dicto non solum sese solatur adversus hos, qui superbe et secure contemnunt Evangelium, sed etiam confirmat pios, ut sciant Deum certo per ministerium huius vocis efficacem fore, quia mandato aeterni patris ab ipso filio Dei prodita et prolata est.

## 8:26
As he was saying these things, many believed.

Although the greater multitude despises the Gospel, especially the Pharisees, yet it produces some fruit, nor is it preached entirely in vain, but in these struggles some assent to the truth, moved by the words of Christ who so often alleges the heavenly testimony. This example warns pious teachers not to be deterred from delivering the doctrine of the Gospel, or from confession, by the poisonous calumnies of adversaries, but to know that it is God's command that they should issue a confession of true doctrine, and that he himself is present with the word, so that it may be effective in some, according to that of Isaiah 55: The word which goes forth from my mouth shall not return to me empty, etc.

But Christ instituted a new discourse to those who had begun to believe, he urges them to persevere in faith, and to strive to know the truth, lest, deterred by carnal judgments or scandals, they relapse. For he sees that these hearers are not sufficiently firm, as the event showed a little later, when new offenses are cast in their way from the words of Christ. He warns them gravely, therefore, that they will truly be disciples of his doctrine if they have remained in his word, that is, if faith perseveres, simply assenting to his word, and does not allow itself to be overturned by carnal judgments and opinions, such as were those of the Pharisees and the multitude in this people concerning the Messiah, that he was to be a worldly king, flourishing in glory, power, and riches, who would liberate the people from foreign domination, and would conserve and propagate this Mosaic polity and these rites. He wishes these opinions to be cast aside, and for judgment to be made concerning himself from his own word, namely, that he was sent by the Father, not to establish or restore a worldly kingdom in this people, but to liberate those who believe from sin and eternal death, as he said above: Unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sins.

He therefore distinguishes his hearers, or disciples; he does not acknowledge those who seek such a teacher who, because of the law and Mosaic rites, promises or brings them bodily liberty and the empire of the world, but he requires such disciples who by faith assent to his word, which testifies that this is the Messiah, the Son of God, sent by the Father, so that he might become a victim for the sins of all men, for the sake of which God wills to receive those who believe, and to grant eternal life. To these he promises these goods, namely, the knowledge of the truth, which is a new light, kindled in minds by the Holy Spirit, truly acknowledging and apprehending God, rightly judging concerning the will of God. Then he promises true liberty, which is to be freed from sin and eternal death, to be truly received by God, and to be gifted with perpetual righteousness and life, just as will be said a little later concerning liberty. These things do not happen to those who only know the law, and dream that they are righteous by that carnal discipline, or observation of Mosaic rites, and that they, on account of the law, will have a kingdom and corporal liberty, by which they may shake off foreign masters, and they themselves may enjoy the empires of the world.

Latin:

Haec eo loquente, multi crediderunt.

Etsi maior multitudo contemnit Evangelium, praesertim Pharisaeorum, tamen parit aliquem fructum, nec prorsus frustra praedicatur, sed in his certaminibus aliqui assentiuntur veritati, moti dictis Christi toties allegantis testimonium coe- leste. Hoc exemplum monet pios doctores, ne propter adversariorum venenatas calumnias abs- terreantur a tradenda doctrina Evangelii, aut a confessione, sed sciant Dei mandatum esse, ut edant confessionem verae doctrinae, et ipsum adesse verbo, ut sit efficax in aliquibus, iuxta il- lud Esaiae 55.: Verbum, quo egreditur de ore meo, non revertetur ad me vacuum, etc.

Sed Christus ad hos, qui coeperant credere, instituit novam concionem, hortatur eos, ut per- severent in fide, et studeant veritatem cognoscere, ne deterriti carnalibus iudiciis, aut scandalis, re- labantur. Videt enim non satis firmos esse hos auditores, ut paulo post eventus ostendit, cum obiiciuntur novae offensiones ex dictis Christi. Graviter igitur monet, sic vere discipulos fore suae doctrinae, si manserint in sermone eius, hoc est, si fides perseveret simpliciter assentiens ipsius verbo, nec sinat se everti carnalibus iudiciis et opinionibus, quales erant Pharisaeorum et multitudinis in hoc populo de Messia, quod esset futurus rex mundanus, florens gloria, potentia, opibus liberaturus populum ab aliena domina- tione, conservaturus et propagaturus hanc poli- tiam Mosaicam et hos cultus. Has opiniones vult abiici, et de sese iudicari ex suo verbo, videlicet, quod sit missus a patre, non ut constituat aut in- stauret regnum mundanum in hoc populo, sed ut liberet credentes a peccato et morte aeterna, sicut supra dixit: Nisi credideritis, quod ego sum, moriemini in peccatis vestris.

Discernit igitur auditores, seu discipulos, non agnoscit hos, qui quaerunt talem doctorem, qui propter legem et cultus Mosaicos promittat aut afferat eis libertatem corporalem, et imperium orbis terrarum, sed tales discipulos requirit, qui fide assentiantur verbo ipsius, quod testatur hunc esse Messiam filium Dei missum a patre, ut fiat victima pro peccatis omnium hominum, propter quam Deus velit recipere credentes, et donare vi- tam aeternam. His promittit haec bona, videli- cet cognitionem veritatis, quae est nova lux, ac- censa in mentibus a Spiritu sancto, vere agno- scens ac apprehendens Deum, recte iudicans de voluntate Dei. Deinde promittit veram liberta- tem, quae est liberari a peccato et a morte ae- terna, vere recipi a Deo, et donari perpetua iu- sticia et vita, sicut paulo post de libertate dicetur. Haec non contingunt his, qui tantum legem no- runt, et somniant se iustos esse illa disciplina carnali, seu observatione Mosaicorum rituum, et se propter legem habituros regnum et libertatem corporalem, qua excutiant alienos dominos, et ipsi fruantur imperiis mundi.

## 8:27
They did not know that he was speaking about the Father.

own wisdom or righteousness, they are so far removed in their whole hearts from the doctrine of the Gospel that they neither allow themselves to be taught, nor can they understand, just as it is predicted concerning them in the Prophets: The heart of this people has become dull, and they have heard heavily with their ears, lest perhaps they understand and be converted.

Nothing could be said more clearly than what he has already inculcated: that he was sent by the Father, that he is this very Son of God for whose sake God chose the Church from the beginning and wishes to save those who believe, and likewise that he brings the voice of the Gospel from the Father and speaks and judges by his command. Since there is nothing obscure in these words, and the Father is so often mentioned by name, it is added as a surprising thing that they did not know that he was speaking to them about the Father: The slowness and stupidity of their intellect is not being accused; they understood these voices when he said that he was not of this world, but sent from the Father from above, etc., but such is the contempt for this teacher, which they have put on, fascinated by the persuasion of the righteousness of the law and that glory that this was the people of God, having the law, the polity, and the worship handed down by God, that nothing enters their minds less than that this is the true teacher sent by God, let alone the Messiah or the Son of God, since he brings a new kind of doctrine and seems to preach arrogantly about himself without mention of the law and Mosaic rites. This was in itself a great offense, so that they turned away from this teacher, and the contempt for his person was added, because an unknown man, needy, without studies and the support of the powerful, the wise, etc., took upon himself the office of teaching among the people of God, against the authority of the highest order, which held the government; wherefore they thought of nothing less than that he was sent by God, and indeed the Son of God, even if he had repeated these voices about the Father a thousand times.

Latin:

Non cognoverunt, quod de patre diceret.

priae sapientiae aut iusticiae, ita procul totis ani- mis abhorrent a doctrina Evangelii, ut nec patian- tur se doceri, nec possint intelligere, sicut de his in Prophetis praedicitur: Incrassatum est cor populi huius, et auribus graviter audierunt, ne forte intelligant et convertantur.

Nihil potuit dici clarius, quam quod iam in- culcavit, se missum a patre, esse hunc ipsum filium Dei, propter quem Deus ab initio elegit Ecclesiam, et vult salvare credentes, item, se a patre afferre vocem Evangelii, et eius mandato loqui et iudicare. In his verbis cum nihil insit obscuri, et toties nominatim allegetur pater, tan- quam res mira additur, illos non cognovisse, quod patrem eis diceret: Non accusatur ingenii tarditas et stupor, intelligebant has voces, cum dixit, se non esse ex hoc mundo, sed ex supernis missum a patre etc., sed tantus est comtemtus hu- ius doctoris, quem induerunt fascinati persuasio- ne iusticiae legis et illius gloriae, quod hic esset populus Dei, habens legem, politiam, cultum a Deo traditum, ut nihil minus subeat ipsorum animos, quam hunc esse verum doctorem missum a Deo, nedum Messiam aut filium Dei, cum affe- rat novum genus doctrinae, et sine mentione legis et cultuum Mosaicorum de sese arroganter videa- tur concionari. Haec erat per sese magna offen- sio, ut aversarentur hunc doctorem, et accedebat personae comtemtus, quod homo ignotus, egens, sine studiis et suffragatione potentum, sapientum, etc. sumeret sibi munus docendi in populo Dei, contra autoritatem summi ordinis, qui tenebat gubernationem, quare nihil minus cogitabant, quam hunc esse missum a Deo, et quidem filium Dei, etiamsi millies has voces de patre iterasset.

## 8:28
When you have lifted up the Son of Man.

They do not understand nor do they accept what he said, that he was sent by the eternal Father and would judge those who do not believe by divine power. Although they are not moved by this statement, nor do they care to know either him or the Father, he nevertheless continues to say how he wishes to be acknowledged. And this is a completely unheard-of and absurd discourse to the Pharisees, nor is it any better understood than that which he has said hitherto: He says that it will come to pass that he is acknowledged to be the Son of God only when he has been lifted up, that is, raised on the cross and subjected to the most terrible punishment, as if he were saying: You do not hear nor acknowledge me now speaking and bringing heavenly testimony that I have been sent by the Father, so that you might believe my voice, but offended by a kind of doctrine alien to your judgment, and by this humble appearance of mine, you do not even deem me worthy to be heard. But it is not enough now that I, held in contempt and spurned by you, am rejected; rather, this remains, that you should also lift me up on the cross, and then indeed you will establish me as a blasphemer and cursed by God, now silent, most shamefully oppressed, and that what I have now said about myself was completely vain and false: But then at last it will come to pass that I am openly acknowledged in the world, when, having been made a victim for the human race and resurrected from death, I will reign by divine power, and I will spread and propagate this word, which will testify that I am the Son of God, and through this very thing I will be effective, the Holy Spirit having been given; then for the first time you will hear me publicly and openly preached and acknowledged as the Son of God, and you will experience that I am effective, about to save those who believe by the word, and to punish those who do not obey.

Furthermore, the imaginations of the Pharisees concerning the Messiah were far different; they dreamed of nothing else than that some prince would come from a noble and powerful family, surrounded by crowds of nobles, fortified with arms and power, who, having shaken off foreign domination, would restore liberty to the people and widely propagate the empire to other nations. They received nothing of this, that the Son of God was to come, who would put on human nature so that he might become a victim for the human race, who was to bring a new and perpetual righteousness and life. Although these things were also predicted clearly enough in the scriptures, they nevertheless heard them with completely alien minds and ears, nor did they allow themselves to be persuaded so that they might assent. The example therefore teaches: That it is not to be wondered at that the doctrine of the Gospel is not understood by many who are judged to excel in wisdom, intellect, etc. Indeed, that they cannot even be brought to want to know it. The impious are always thus demented by the persuasion of their own righteousness. This is a grave discourse, encompassing an arcane doctrine, unknown to reason and carnal wisdom, concerning that admirable counsel of God, which both willed the Son to become a victim having put on flesh, and which in this arcane way wills itself to be acknowledged, which the Gospel has revealed, which shows both the wrath of God against the sin of the human race, which could be appeased by no other sacrifice than the death of the only-begotten Son, and again shows the ineffable mercy, that the eternal Father willed the Son to sustain the whole weight of sin, that is, the universal damnation to be paid for the human race, so that he might save those who believe. He says that he will reveal this secret counsel of God, but only then, when he has been exalted, that is, made a victim and a curse, hanging on the cross, and that only then will it come to pass that it is made known how God wishes to be acknowledged, namely when the voice of the Gospel will sound openly, that not because of the law or Levitical worship, but because of this son, God wishes to receive and save those who believe.

This is the sum of this saying: To the offense of the Pharisees regarding the person of Christ and the kind of doctrine, which they judge to be openly absurd, he opposes this very thing, that God does not wish to be acknowledged otherwise than under this very form of the cross, that the son of God, sustaining the wrath of God and death on account of the sin of the human race, and having been raised again, will spread this word, that because of this crucified son, God truly receives those who believe. To this sentiment corresponds the saying of Paul concerning the efficacy of the Gospel, 1 Cor. 1, when he says: Because through wisdom the world did not know God in wisdom, it pleased God through the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe. He teaches that the immutable decree of the eternal Father is to be preferred to the Gospel, in that he wishes to save the human race, not in that way which the wisdom of reason judges, namely the justice of the law, or by the performing of new and prodigious deeds or miracles in certain outstanding men who especially excel among humans, but that all who believe the Gospel are saved by faith in this word, which is therefore mocked by the wise because it teaches these things absurd to reason and human judgment, that the son of God was made a victim, or an expiation, or a curse, and that men are pronounced righteous by God, not because of the effort of performing the law, and however excellent their virtues, but because of the obedience of the son of God, who sustained the wrath of God and death, if only they believe that they are forgiven for his sake.

This doctrine cannot but seem absurd to the wise, who in some way understand the law, and rightly judge that there is nothing more beautiful in this whole nature of things than the pursuit of virtue and the diligence of performing the law. But let the pious believe the word of God, which convicts the uncleanness of the heart, shows the wrath of God against the sin of the whole human race, and judges that the law is by no means satisfied by that diligence, whatever it may be, which reason provides, and let them know that it is in truth the eternal and immutable decree of the wisdom of God, which judged that it was necessary for the son of God to be sent into the flesh, and to be made a victim on the cross, which would please and take away eternal wrath, and because of which, having been received by God, we would be gifted with righteousness and eternal life.

Moreover, it is to be observed in this place the testimony concerning the person of Christ, for he says both: He says that he is the son of man, that is, truly having a human nature, and indeed destined by God to be made a victim, that is, to sustain death and the wrath of God on account of the sin of the human race, but he adds concerning his divine nature and power: Then you will know that I am, clearly as he said above: If you do not believe that I am, you will die in your sins. For by these words he does not only signify this, that he is called or sent by God, like other Prophets and teachers, Moses, the Baptist, but he wishes his person to be distinguished from all other governors and ministers, he wishes himself to be acknowledged to be that very Lord who has existed from eternity, and from then on from the beginning has revealed himself, having issued the word or promises, who has always been present to the Church, and has brought forth wondrous works and deliverances, and always preserves the Church, just as it is said in John 1, that all things were made through him. Likewise, as the Baptist says: He who was before me, and was made before me, that is, he for whose sake God chose the Church from the beginning, and wishes to save it, and who is not only a teacher and minister like the others, but he himself is the Lord and founder and savior of the Church, he himself performs miracles, gives the Holy Spirit and eternal life. All these things are signified by this saying, when he says: You will know that I am, he clearly makes a distinction, he wishes himself to be acknowledged in a much different way than Moses or the Prophets, who indeed were ministers sent by God, and had testimonies of their calling. But this Messiah demands it be believed that he himself is the Lord, for whose sake God receives and saves the Church, not because of the law, or the merits of any men, because for his sake alone the promises were given, and he alone is the propitiator, who abolishes sin and death, and restores eternal life.

Therefore he adds fearful threats: Unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sins. He wishes us to know that the Church is saved and preserved for his sake, and he predicts to the Jews that this whole Mosaic polity, however flourishing, and indeed divinely constituted, is therefore going to perish, because they do not acknowledge and receive this Lord, and therefore he signifies that he was not sent by God to constitute a political or worldly dominion, but to bring this heavenly command that all may believe his word, and know that God wills, for his sake, to save those who believe, and to take vengeance upon those who do not believe, so that they may be condemned and perish, with the entire polity of this people overturned, which had been established by God only for the sake of this Messiah, so that the promises concerning Christ might exist in this people, and he himself might be acknowledged as Lord and propitiator.

The same thing is also signified by these words: When you have lifted up the Son of Man, you will know that I am, that is, when I have performed this work for which I was sent, namely, that I should become a victim, then I will gather the Church, having given the Holy Spirit, and having performed miraculous works, which will testify that I reign by divine power, you will experience this in such a way that either you will be saved by believing the Gospel, or if you do not wish to obey, you yourselves will perish, and this entire polity of yours will be overturned, which you dream will be perpetual, and that the Messiah, when he comes, will fortify it and amplify it with far greater glory and bodily power. This will happen then for the first time, when you, having seen me lifted up on the cross and now dead, will think that I am utterly oppressed, nay, even rejected and condemned by God, but immediately after this death and weakness it will appear that I am the victor over sin, and the Lord of death, and the giver of eternal life. Thus you will know that I am, and that I do nothing of myself, that is, you will know that I do not reign by human, but by divine power, and that I perform truly divine works, give the Holy Spirit, hear and save those who call upon me, and punish those who do not obey the Gospel.

Latin:

Cum exaltaveritis filium hominis.

Non intelligunt nec accipiunt quod dixit, se esse missum ab aeterno patre, et iudicaturum di- vina potentia non credentes. Hoc dicto etsi nihil moventur, nec curant cognoscere aut ipsum aut patrem, tamen pergit dicere, quomodo velit agnosci. Estque haec prorsus inaudita, et ab- surda concio Pharisaeis, nec magis intellecta, quam ea quam hactenus dixit: Ita demum ait fore, ut agnoscatur esse filius Dei, cum exaltatus fuerit, hoc est, sublatus in crucem et teterrimo supplicio affectus, quasi dicat: Non auditis nec agnoscitis me nunc loquentem, et afferentem testimonium coeleste, quod missus sim a patre, ut credatis meae voci, sed offensi genere doctrinae alieno a vestro iudicio, et ista humili specie mea, ne di- gnum quidem existimatis, quem audiatis. Sed non satis est nunc me comtemtum et spretum a vobis explodi, verum hoc restat, ut etiam me tollatis in crucem, tum vero statuetis me tan- quam blasphemum et maledictum a Deo, iam ta- cere turpissime oppressum, et prorsus vana ac falsa fuisse, quae nunc de me dixi: At tunc de- mum fiet, ut palam agnoscar in mundo, cum factus victima pro genere humano, et resuscitatus ex morte regnabo divina potentia, et spargam ac propagabo hoc verbum, quod testabitur me esse filium Dei, et per hoc ipsum ero efficax dato Spi- ritu sancto, tunc primum audietis me publice et palam praedicari et agnosci filium Dei, et expe- riemini esse efficacem, salvaturum credentes ver- bo, et puniturum non obtemperantes.

Deinde de Messia longe aliae erant Phari- saeorum imaginationes, nihil aliud somniabant, quam venturum ex nobili et potente familia ali- quem principem, stipatum catervis procerum, munitum armis, potentia, qui excussa aliena do- minatione, restitueret populo libertatem, et late propagaret imperium in alias nationes. Nihil ho- rum recipiebant, quod venturus esset filius Dei, qui indueret naturam humanam, ut fieret victima pro genere humano, qui esset allaturus novam et perpetuam iusticiam et vitam. Haec etsi erant etiam in scripturis satis clare praedicta, tamen prorsus alienis animis et auribus audiebant, nec sinebant se persuaderi, ut assentirentur. Docet igitur exemplum: Non esse mirandum, non in- telligi doctrinam Evangelii a multis, qui iudican- tur excellere sapientia, ingeniis, etc. Imo ne posse quidem adduci, ut velint eam cognoscere. Semper sic sunt impii dementati persuasione pro- Haec est gravis concio, complectens arcanam doctrinam, ignotam rationi et sapientiae carnali, de illo admirando consilio Dei, quod et voluit filium fieri victimam induta carne, et quod hoc arcano modo vult se agnosci, quem patefecit Evangelium, quod ostendit et iram Dei adversus peccatum humani generis, quod nulla alia hostia potuerit placari, nisi morte unigeniti filii, et rur- sus monstrat misericordiam inenarrabilem, quod aeternus pater voluerit filium sustinere totam mo- lem peccati, hoc est, universam damnationem luendam generi humano, ut salvaret credentes. Hoc arcanum consilium Dei ait se patefacturum esse, sed tum primum, cum fuerit exaltatus, hoc est, factus victima et maledictum, pendens in cruce, et ita demum fore, ut innotescat, quo- modo Deus velit agnosci, videlicet cum palam sonabit vox Evangelii, quod non propter legem aut cultus leviticos, sed propter hunc filium Deus velit recipere et salvare credentes.

Haec summa est huius dicti: Offensioni Pha- risaeorum de persona Christi et genere doctrinae, quod iudicant palam absurdum, opponit hoc ipsum, quod Deus non aliter velit agnosci, quam sub hac ipsa forma crucis, quod filius Dei susti- nens iram Dei et mortem, propter peccatum ge- neris humani, et rursus resuscitatus sparget hoc verbum, quod propter hunc filium crucifixum, Deus vere recipiat credentes. Ad hanc sententiam congruit dictum Pauli de efficacia Evangelii, 1. Cor. 1. cum ait: Quia per sapientiam mundus non cognovit Deum in sapientia, placuit Deo per stultitiam praedicationis salvare credentes. Docet Evangelio praeferri immutabile decretum aeterni patris, quod velit salvare genus humanum, non illo modo, quo iudicat sapientia rationis, videli- cet iusticia legis, aut efficiendis novis et prodigio- sis factis seu virtutibus in aliquibus praestantibus viris, qui praecipue excellunt inter homines, sed fide huius verbi salvatos esse omnes, qui credunt Evangelio, quod ideo ridetur a sapientibus, quia docet haec absurda rationi et iudicio humano, filium Dei factum esse victimam, seu piaculum, seu maledictum, et homines iustos pronunciari a Deo, non propter studium faciendae legis, et quantumvis excellentes virtutes, sed propter obe- dientiam filii Dei, qui sustinuit iram Dei et mor- tem, si tamen credant sibi propter hunc ignosci.

Haec doctrina non potest non videri absurda sapientibus, qui aliquo modo intelligunt legem, et recte iudicant nihil esse pulcrius in hac tota natura rerum, quam studium virtutis, et diligen- tiam faciendae legis. Sed pii credant verbo Dei, quod arguit immunditiem cordis, ostendit iram Dei adversus peccatum totius generis humani, ac iudicat nequaquam satisfieri legi illa qualicunque diligentia, quam praestat ratio, et sciant, revera esse aeternum, et immutabile decretum sapientiae Dei, quae iudicavit, oportere filium Dei mitti in carnem, et in cruce fieri victimam, quae placeret et tolleret aeternam iram, et propter quam re- cepti a Deo donaremur iusticia et vita aeterna.

Est autem hoc loco observandum testimo- nium de persona Christi, utrunque enim dicit: Ait, se esse filium hominis, hoc est, vere haben- tem naturam humanam, et quidem destinatum a Deo, ut fiat victima, hoc est, sustineat mortem et iram Dei propter peccatum humani generis, sed addit de divina natura et potentia: Tunc cogno- scetis quod ego sum, plane ut supra dixit: Si non credideritis quod ego sum, moriemini in peccatis vestris. Nam his verbis non tantum hoc signifi- cat, se esse vocatum aut missum a Deo, sicut alii Prophetae et doctores, Moses, Baptista, sed vult discerni personam ab omnibus aliis gubernatori- bus et ministris, vult se agnosci, esse illum ipsum dominum, qui ab aeterno extiterit, et inde usque ab initio sese patefecerit, edito verbo seu promissionibus, qui semper affuerit Ecclesiae, et ediderit miranda opera et liberationes, et semper conservet Ecclesiam, sicut Ioann. 1. dicitur, Omnia per ipsum facta esse. Item, ut Baptista ait: Qui prior me fuit, et ante me factus est, hoc est, is propter quem Deus ab initio elegit Eccle- siam, et eam vult salvare, et qui non tantum est doctor et minister ut caeteri, sed ipse est domi- nus et conditor et servator Ecclesiae, ipse edit miracula, dat Spiritum sanctum et vitam aeter- nam. Haec omnia significantur hoc dicto, cum inquit: Cognoscetis quod ego sim, clare facit dis- crimen, multo aliter vult agnosci sese, quam Mosen aut Prophetas, qui quidem erant ministri missi a Deo, et habebant testimonia vocationis. Sed hic Messias postulat credi, quod ipse sit do- minus, propter quem Deus recipiat et servet Ec- clesiam, non propter legem, aut merita ullorum hominum, quia propter hunc solum datae sunt promissiones, et hic solus est propiciator, qui abolet peccatum et mortem, et restituit vitam ae- ternam.

Ideo addit metuendas minas: Nisi credideri- tis, quod ego sum, moriemini in peccatis vestris. Vult nos scire, propter ipsum salvari et conser- vari Ecclesiam, et praedicit Iudaeis, hanc totam politiam Mosaicam, quantumvis florentem, et quidem divinitus constitutam, ideo interituram esse, quia non agnoscant et recipiant hunc do- minum, ideoque significat se non missum esse a Deo, ut constituat politicam seu mundanam do- minationem, sed afferre hoc mandatum coeleste, ut omnes ipsius verbo credant, et sciant Deum velle propter ipsum salvare credentes, et sumtu- rum poenas de non credentibus, ut damnentur et pereant, eversa tota politia huius populi, quae tantum propter hunc Messiam a Deo constituta erat, ut in hoc populo extarent promissiones de Christo, et ipse agnosceretur dominus et propi- ciator.

Idem et his verbis significatur: Cum exalta- veritis filium hominis, cognoscetis quod ego sum, hoc est, cum praestitero hoc opus, propter quod missus sum, videlicet ut fiam victima, tunc colli- gam Ecclesiam, dato Spiritu sancto, et editis mi- randis operibus, quae testabuntur, me regnare divina potentia, hanc experiemini vos ita, ut aut credentes Evangelio salvemini, aut si non voletis obedire, et ipsi pereatis, et haec tota politia ve- stra evertatur, quam vos somniatis perpetuam fore, et Messiam ubi venerit, muniturum esse eam, et amplificaturum longe maiore gloria et po- tentia corporali. Hoc tum primum fiet, cum me exaltatum in crucem et mortuum iam, existimabi- tis prorsus oppressum esse, imo etiam abiectum et damnatum a Deo, sed statim post hanc mortem et infirmitatem apparebit, me esse victorem pec- cati, et mortis dominum, et datorem vitae aeter- nae. Sic cognoscetis quod ego sum, et a meipso facio nihil, id est, cognoscetis me non humana, sed divina potentia regnare, et edere vere divina opera, dare Spiritum sanctum exaudire, et sal- vare invocantes, punire non obedientes Evan- gelio.

## 8:28
And as the Father taught me, so I speak.

That is, according to this very word which I bring and will scatter into the Church, so that it may appear that this is truly the immutable decree and command of the eternal Father.

And he adds the reason: He who sent me is with me, and does not leave me, as if he were saying: I know that the Father wills this, and that through me he will perform these miraculous works in the Church, against the power of Satan and the world, and that this alone pleases him, to be thus celebrated by the voice of the Gospel, and to be acknowledged himself, because for my sake he wills to save those who believe, because he wills to hear me, and that I be believed, because for my sake he has chosen and receives the Church, just as he testified with his own voice: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear him, as the Baptist also says: The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand.

Latin:

Et sicut me docuit pater, ita loquor.

Id est, iuxta hoc ipsum verbum, quod affe- ro, et spargam in Ecclesiam, ut appareat, hoc vere esse immutabile decretum et mandatum ae- terni patris.

Et addit rationem: Qui me misit, mecum est, et non relinquit, quasi dicat: Scio hoc velle patrem, et per me effecturum esse haec miranda opera in Ecclesia, adversus potentiam Satanae et mundi, et hoc tantum ei placere, sic celebrari voce Evangelii, et agnosci ipsum, quod propter me velit servare credentes, quod velit me audire, et mihi credi, quod propter me elegerit et reci- piat Ecclesiam, sicut testatus est sua voce: Hic est filius meus dilectus, quo delector: hunc audite, ut et Baptista ait: Pater diligit filium, et omnia dedit in manu eius.

## 8:33
We are the seed of Abraham.

They submit a response entirely foreign to the most weighty sentiments of Christ, which testifies that those, some of whom had begun to believe, so that they might agree that this is the Messiah, nevertheless still hold fixed in their minds an imagination concerning a corporal kingdom, still dreaming that, if indeed this is the Messiah, he is going to be a powerful king, flourishing in wealth, surrounded by throngs of nobles and the multitude, and that in these things they too would be blessed. Led by this hope, they were more easily agreeing. Now when he begins to preach concerning the acknowledgment of truth and faith, and says: Only then will they be happy, and have liberty, if they hold his word by faith, and persevere in it, offended they recoil, and argue in return, they deny that they are slaves, subject to a foreign power, as far as the profession, or doctrine of religion pertains, but that they are the seed of Abraham, always from the beginning having been the people of God, never having been idolaters, after the manner of the nations, but having held the doctrine of religion, the law, circumcision, and other rites indeed handed down by Moses, but received by hand from the fathers from then all the way to Abraham. Thus here a new struggle arises for Christ, and indeed a much harder one than the previous.

And so that the altercations of this whole chapter may be more rightly understood, let us look at the heads of the controversies. The struggle in these questions, which are agitated concerning the Messiah, is chiefly about three things. First, it is disputed about the polity, second about the worships, third about the person of the Messiah.
