Let us each diligently inculcate in ourselves these sayings and similar ones distinguishing the true Church from other nations, and true invocation from fictitious. For they both piously instruct minds about necessary matters, and kindle faith and invocation.

Latin:

Qui me odit, et patrem meum odit.

Si et supra cap. 5. dixit: Qui non honorat filium, non honorat patrem. Hae duae senten- tiae diligentissime observandae sunt. Monstrant enim discrimen verae religionis et commentitia- rum, et verae invocationis et falsae. Iudaei et Mahometistae gloriantur se unum et verum Deum invocare, conditorem coeli et terrae, et homi- num et omnium aliarum creaturarum. Imo et Platonis et similium virorum mentes unum ali- quem Deum conditorem universae naturae cogi- tabant. Sed haec dicta Christi reiiciunt illam Iu- daicam, Mahometicam et Ethnicam cogitationem, qui negant hunc vere esse Deum conditorem, qui misit filium suum Iesum Christum. Illi non agno- scunt, non invocant verum Deum, sed sculpunt sibi novum simulacrum Dei, et a vero Deo aber- rant. Teneamus igitur discrimen religionum, nec concedamus Iudaeis et Mahometistis, coli ab eis Deum conditorem coeli et terrae, sed fingunt illum esse Deum, qui missurus sit alium Messiam, vel qui misit Mahometum. Ac certissimum est, Mahometum a diabolo missum esse, quia Maho- meti doctrina recens est, pugnans cum Prophetis et Apostolis, ut manifestum est. Quare certum est impiam et diabolicam esse.

Semper etiam in invocatione compellantes Deum, cogitemus hunc Deum conditorem coeli et terrae, qui misit filium suum Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, et per illum se patefecit dato Evangelio. Ita primum cogitemus, quem Deum, ubi et quomodo patefactum alloquamur, deinde etiam promissiones nobis proponamus, in quibus affirmat se exauditurum esse invocantes, propter filium mediatorem. Has cogitationes et hanc fidem afferre nos ad precandum oportet. Ac ta- lis invocatio discernit veram Ecclesiam ab Ethni- cis, Iudaeis, Turcis invocantibus, et est ef- ficax.

Ac Psalm. 16. sic discernitur Ecclesia a cae- teris gentibus. Discernitur et invocatio vera et efficax, a falsa et damnata, cum dicitur: San- ctis qui sunt in terra, et admirandis, omnis vo- luntas mea in eis, id est, Ego Christus perpetuo diligo.iustos, id est, coetum qui me audit, his consulo hac mea passione, omnes mei labores, omnia mea officia ad hoc destinata sunt, ut illis opem ferant. Nos stulte cogitamus Christum otio- sum alicubi sedere, ac sibi beatum esse. Hic cla- mitat se pro suo coetu solicitum esse, laborare, interpellare, regere eum, defendere et servare. Econtra addit, se damnare libationes et invoca- tiones aliorum, qui ipsum audire nolunt. Non libabo, inquit, libationes eorum, nec sumam nomina eorum in labiis meis, id est, non nomi- nabo eos, non interpellabo pro eis apud patrem. Haec dicta et similia discernentia veram Eccle- siam ab aliis gentibus, et veram invocationem a commentitia, diligenter inculcemus nobis singuli. Nam et pie docent mentes de rebus necessariis, et accendunt fidem et invocationem.

## 15:25
That the word written in the law might be fulfilled.

John is accustomed to speak in this way, as in chapter 12: They did not believe in him, that the scripture might be fulfilled. These things are not to be taken so stoically, as if he wishes God to be the cause of evil, or as if wills were compelled by some fate, but let such things be understood concerning the necessity of consequence, that is, they were predicted because they were going to happen, and now the event shows God to be truthful: Just as the truth of God is seen in other divine predictions.

But the sentence is cited from Psalm 68: Save me, O God, in which Psalm there is a long description of the passion of Christ and his members. And we are warned by this saying that we should suffer, as Peter says: Not as murderers, or thieves, but as Christians, that is, on account of the confession of the Gospel. And there is a remarkable πάθος in the passage of thanks: They hate me, not only as guilty of no crime, nor as harming them, but even as most ardently desiring to do them good, serving with the utmost humility, transferring to myself the punishments which they themselves deserve, not seeking any vengeance, but rather with immense grief lamenting their stubbornness and destruction, offering them the highest and eternal goods. For this best will, and one full of sorrow and mourning on their account, and most desirous of doing them good, I receive hatred.

Let doctors consider this image, who often incur hatreds, but others for other causes. Let not the filth of life, rapine, excessively unjust πλεονεκτήματα, tyrannical harshness, and other vices bring upon us just hatreds. Furthermore, let the good, who are far from these vices, know that ingratitude is a common disease of almost the entire human race. And let them bear calmly that for their best will and immense benefits, bad thanks, hatreds, insults, and other evils are returned to them, just as all histories are full of examples of ingratitude. The Attic state kept Miltiades in prison almost until his death. It expelled Aristides, Themistocles, and Cimon, who had deserved the best. Finally, the catalog of such people is infinite, whose examples should admonish us that we should strive to do right for the sake of God, not for the sake of human reward, nor should we be broken in spirit when the efforts and duties of men do not respond to our will and our merits.

Latin:

Ut impleatur sermo scriptus in lege.

Consuevit ita loqui Ioannes ut cap. 12.: Non credebant in eum, ut impleretur scriptura. Haec non sunt ita stoice accipienda, quasi velit causam mali Deum esse, aut quasi fato aliquo sint coactae voluntates, sed intelligantur talia de ne- cessitate consequentiae, id est, praedicta sunt, quia eventura fuerunt, et nunc ostendit eventus Deum esse veracem: Sicut veritas Dei conspicitur in aliis praedictionibus divinis.

Citatur autem sententia ex Psalm. 68.: Sal- vum me fac Deus, in quo Psalmo longa descriptio est passionis Christi et membrorum eius. Ac mo- nemur hoc dicto ut patiamur, sicut Petrus ait: Non ut homicidae, aut fures, sed ut Christiani, id est, propter confessionem Evangelii. Estque insigne πάθος in particula Gratis: Oderunt me non solum nullius sceleris reum, nec nocentem ipsis, sed etiam ardentissime cupientem eis bene- facere, servientem summa humilitate, transfe- rentem in me poenas, quas ipsi merentur, non quaerentem ullam vindictam, imo ingenti dolore deplorantem ipsorum pertinaciam, et exitium, offerentem eis summa et aeterna bona. Pro hac optima voluntate, et plena moeroris et luctus propter ipsos, et maxime cupida benefaciendi eis, reporto odium.

Hanc imaginem considerent doctores, qui saepe incurrunt in odia, sed alii propter alias cau- sas. Non accersant nobis iusta odia, turpitudo vitae, rapinae, πλεονεκτήματα nimis iniqua, ty- rannicae asperitates, et alia vitia. Deinde boni, qui alieni sunt ab his vitiis, sciant communem morbum esse fere totius generis humani, ingrati- tudinem. Et placide ferant sibi pro optima vo- luntate et ingentibus beneficiis reddi malam gra- tiam, odia, contumelias, et alia mala, sicut omnes historiae plenae sunt exemplorum, ingra- titudinis. Attica civitas Miltiaden in carcere pene ad mortem usque detinuit. Aristiden, Themi- stoclem, Cimonem optime meritos expulit. De- nique catalogus infinitus est talium, quorum exempla nos admoneant, ut studeamus propter Deum recta facere, non propter mercedem huma- nam, nec frangamur animis, cum non respon- dent hominum studia et officia nostra voluntati et nostris meritis.

## 15:26
But when the paraclete has come.

Christ taught many things above concerning the sum of the Gospel, concerning himself, concerning the true Church, concerning the Holy Spirit, and concerning the ministry of the Gospel. He comforted his hearers, and as one about to depart, he gave certain commands. Now he repeats the discourse concerning the Holy Spirit and the ministry of the Gospel.

But first let us learn the description of the Holy Spirit, which shows who and what kind he is, and testifies that he is a distinct person from the Father and the Son; but as I have often warned elsewhere, the testimonies of any article are firmer and more illustrious when the principal ones are joined together at the same time, and add light, as it were, to one another. Wherefore, let other sayings be added to this place, which teach who the Holy Spirit is, and testify that he is a person distinct from the Father and his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. Moreover, the distinction of persons is shown clearly in the revelation of the three persons, which took place at the baptism of Christ, as has been said in another place.

But above I recited what παράκλητος signifies, namely, an advocate. But just as an advocate in court sustains many duties—he advises, he directs his side with counsel, he is an encourager and a comforter, he speaks for him for whom he is an advocate—so the Holy Spirit has similar duties privately in believers, and publicly in the Church in the ministry; he kindles light in hearts so that they may understand the Gospel, he moves them so that they may assent, he confirms the assent which is attacked in various ways, he shows counsel, he raises up the terrified, he speaks for us, that is, he impels hearts to invocation; he is also our orator openly in confession, and he helps those who speak. Thus also in the public ministry he is present and preserves the public voice of the Gospel, and through it he is effective, so that many may be converted to the true knowledge of God. These benefits, signified by the title of paraclete, are more expressed when he is named the spirit of truth, that is, a truthful spirit and one that makes others truthful. He is spirit, providing light and an agitator. Truthful, that is, agreeing with the divine mind, not dissenting from the eternal Father and from Christ, nor from the word delivered through the Father and through Christ. Furthermore, he is also one who makes others truthful and agreeing with the will and word of God, and interpreting, proposing, and defending the truth in the public ministry.

Here also let a comparison be considered. The opinions of other nations concerning God are full of errors, as the Gentiles invented new gods with immense audacity, and cults without end—one Bacchus, another Proserpina, another Priapus, another something else. Thus now the Jews, the Mahometans, and the Monks invent foul frenzies, but there is one true doctrine, written by the Prophets and Apostles, which the Holy Spirit sounds, and of which the Holy Spirit testifies, just as he said clearly here and above: He will teach you all things, and will bring to your memory all things which I have said. The Spirit is therefore the preserver of the evangelical ministry, and through this ministry he is effective. Furthermore, let this comparison also be considered. The minds of individuals are full of errors, doubts, and confusions, thinking about God without the light of the Holy Spirit, just as Simonides truly said: The longer he sought the nature and will of God, the more he doubted; that happens when minds are not directed by the voice of the Gospel and the Holy Spirit illuminating the Gospel and confirming assent in minds. These things must often be pondered, and it must be requested that God may rule and confirm us with the Holy Spirit. For this reason, this promise has been repeated so often in this final discourse, so that we may know that Christ wishes this benefit to be requested, and that he will give it, just as he clearly asserts here: whom I will send to you from the Father. And above: I will not leave you orphans: I will ask the Father, and he will give you the Spirit, the Paraclete. The human mind by itself is full of darkness, and easily slips, and wanders, and the devil throws up many specters, and in various ways leads men away from God. No one can avoid these dangers without the Holy Spirit. Therefore, let us ask that this Paraclete be given to us with true and ardent prayers, and he is truly given to those who ask, as Christ affirms: How much more will your Father who is in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask.

Latin:

Cum autem venerit paracletus.

Multa docuit supra de summa Evangelii, de seipso Christus, de vera Ecclesia, de Spiritu san- cto, de ministerio Evangelii. Consolatus est au- ditores suos, et dedit tanquam discessurus certa mandata. Nunc repetit concionem de Spiritu sancto, et de ministerio Evangelii.

Primum autem discamus descriptionem Spi- ritus sancti, quae ostendit quis et qualis sit, et testatur distinctam personam esse a patre et filio, sed ut saepe alias monui, firmiora et illustriora sunt cuiuslibet articuli testimonia, cum praeci- pua simul coniunguntur, et alia aliis quasi lumen addunt. Quare ad hunc locum adiungantur cae- tera dicta, quae docent, quis sit Spiritus sanctus, et testantur personam a patre, et filio eius Domi- no nostro Iesu Christo distinctam esse. Ostendi- tur autem perspicue distinctio personarum in re- velatione trium personarum, facta in baptismo Christi, ut alio loco dictum est.

Supra autem recitavi, quid significet παρά- κλητος, scilicet advocatum. Ut autem advocatus in iudicio multa officia sustinet, monet, regit suam partem consilio, est hortator et consolator, dicit pro eo, cui est advocatus. Ita Spiritus san- ctus similia habet officia privatim in credentibus, et publice in Ecclesia in ministerio, accendit lu- cem in cordibus, ut Evangelium intelligant, mo- vet ut assentiantur, confirmat assensionem, quae oppugnatur variis modis, monstrat consilium, perterrefactos erigit, pro nobis loquitur, id est, impellit corda ad invocationem, palam etiam in confessione noster orator est, et adiuvat dicentes. Ita et in publico ministerio adest et servat publi- cam Evangelii vocem, et per eam est efficax, ut multi convertantur ad veram Dei agnitionem. Haec beneficia significata appellatione paracleti, magis expressa sunt, cum nominatur spiritus ve- ritatis, id est, spiritus verax et efficiens veraces. Spiritus est, lucem praebens, et agitator. Verax, id est, menti divinae congruens, non dissentiens ab aeterno patre, et a Christo, nec a verbo tra- dito per patrem et per Christum. Deinde etiam efficiens veraces, et congruentes voluntati et verbo Dei, et veritatem in publico ministerio in- terpretans, proponens, et propugnans.

Hic et collatio consideretur. Aliarum gen- tium opiniones de Deo sunt plenae errorum, ut Ethnici finxerunt immani audacia novos deos, et cultus sine fine, alius Bacchum, alius Proserpi- nam, alius Priapum, alius alia. Sic iam Iudaei, Mahometistae, Monachi comminiscuntur tetros furores, sed una est vera doctrina, scripta per Prophetas et Apostolos, quam sonat Spiritus sanctus, et de qua Spiritus sanctus testificatur, sicut hic et supra clare dixit: Ille docebit vos omnia, et rediget vobis in memoriam omnia, quae dixi. Est igitur Spiritus conservator mini- sterii evangelici, et per hoc ministerium est effi- cax. Deinde et haec collatio consideretur. Ple- nae sunt errorum, dubitationum, et confusio- num mentes singulorum, cogitantes de Deo sine luce Spiritus sancti, sicut vere dixit Simonides: Quo diutius naturam et voluntatem Dei quaereret, eo se magis dubitare, id fit, cum mentes non re- guntur voce Evangelii, et Spiritu sancto illu- strante Evangelium, et confirmante assensionem in mentibus. Haec saepe cogitanda sunt, et petendum, ut Deus regat et confirmet nos Spiritu sancto. Nam ideo toties haec promissio in hac postrema concione repetita est, ut sciamus Christum velle peti hoc beneficium, et daturum esse, sicut hic clare asseverat, quem ego mittam vobis a patre. Et supra: Non relinquam vos orphanos: Ego rogabo patrem, et dabit vobis spiritum paracletum. Mens humana per sese plena est caliginis, et facile labitur, et aberrat, et diabolus obiicit multa spectra, et variis modis abducit homines a Deo. Haec pericula nemo sine Spiritu sancto cavere potest. Ideo hunc paracletum veris et ardentibus votis dari nobis petamus, et vere datur petentibus, ut affirmat Christus: Quanto magis pater vester qui in coelis est, dabit Spiritum sanctum petentibus.

## 15:26
Who proceeds from the Father.

Although the article concerning the essence of God, and concerning the three persons, the eternal Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, is unsearchable, and profane men, such as Samosatenus, the Jews, the Mahometans, and countless others, cry out that the things which the Church professes are absurd opinions—that the Son was born from the substance of the eternal Father, coeternal, ὁμοούσιον, and that the Holy Spirit proceeds from both—nevertheless, because God himself has revealed himself thus by clear and certain testimonies, and has willed that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit be distinguished, it is necessary for us to embrace this doctrine, and reverently assent, even if the wisdom of devils and men, raging, is offended by the absurdity.

Why, you will ask, does God propose to us articles whose words, even if we imitate them in some way, we can nevertheless conceive no images of the things themselves? I hear the Son called λόγος, but what kind of λόγος is that, since he is a person? I hear there is a distinction between being born and proceeding; I recognize the different words, but I would wish to see the thing more closely. These questions torment the human mind, but although there ought to be a manner of these descriptions and thoughts, let us nevertheless know that it is God's will that the divinity be acknowledged in this way. The Son was made redeemer and victim; the eternal Father certainly wishes him to be acknowledged as such. Indeed, he declares men to be thus righteous, and heirs of eternal life, if on account of this Son they believe that the remission of sins and eternal life are given to them.

He also sent the Holy Spirit in a visible form, so that we may distinguish him from the Father and the Son, and believe that he is sent into our hearts, so that he may rule us, and begin in us light, righteousness, and eternal life. The proper benefit of the Son is that he is the redeemer; the proper benefit of the Holy Spirit is to be sent into the hearts of believers. Since these immense goods have been attributed to the persons with a certain distinction, the eternal Father certainly wishes the persons to be acknowledged and invoked. Indeed, Christ says: He who does not honor the Son, does not honor the Father.

Let us know, therefore, that the doctrine concerning the three persons is not to be neglected, nor buried in silence, but let us ponder and recite it reverently, and let us seek only as much concerning it as God has revealed. He has revealed, however, those things which he willed to be exercised in invocation; as often as we invoke, he wishes us to look upon the Son, and on account of him to seek the remission of sins; he wishes it also to be requested that we be governed by the Holy Spirit. Let these distinctions always come into the mind and before the eyes in invocation.

Then let us piously ponder how the doctrine of the Gospel distinguishes the Father, the eternal Son, and the Holy Spirit. And it is known that these distinctions are taught: The Father, from eternity looking upon himself, begets the Son, who is the image of the eternal Father. The Son is begotten, and is the image of the eternal Father. The Holy Spirit proceeds from the eternal Father and from the Son.

Here now it is asked, what is the difference between being born and proceeding? Or what does that 'proceeding' signify at all? These things are declared thus for the sake of teaching. If the nature of men were uncorrupted, its consideration would have instructed us more about God. But let us nevertheless take examples in some way from the nature of men. There are two faculties of the soul: the faculty of understanding, and the faculty of willing. The understanding begets images by thinking; the will has impulses, just as the heart begets spirits, feels love, joy, and other affections. From these examples the explanation is taken. Since the Son is called λόγος, he is begotten by thinking. But thought is an image of the thing thought; therefore the Son is called λόγος, because the Son is the image of the Father.

But the Holy Spirit is said to proceed, because he is the love of the will. Therefore, the Father, looking upon the Son, wills and loves him, and in turn the Son, looking upon the Father, wills and loves him. By this mutual love, which is properly of the wills, the Holy Spirit proceeds, who is the agitator from the eternal Father, and from the Son, the coe- ternal image of the Father. Just as, therefore, to the intelligent faculty it is attributed to beget: so we say that procession is from the will. Because the will is the seat of love and of agitation, concerning which, so that we may think of some shadow of them, however slight, let us contemplate ourselves, let us recognize that images are begotten by thought, but that the will, or the heart, has impulses and love. In us, essence is not transfused into any images, or into any love, or impulse, even if our nature is vehemently seized with love, or joy, and migrates as it were into the beloved object, but the image of the eternal Father, which is the Son, and is the substance of the eternal Father, and to the Holy Spirit the essence of the Father and the Son is communicated.

Here also the forms of speech must be observed. Sometimes it is spoken of the eternal procession, by which the Holy Spirit is the third person of the divinity, as it is said here: Who proceeds from the Father, and this is properly called procession. Sometimes it is spoken of the mission, by which the Holy Spirit is sent into the hearts of men who are reborn by faith. Some sometimes call this a temporal procession, but it is more usually called Mission. Just as it is also named here in the text: Whom I will send from the Father, and they inquire concerning the mission, whether the person of the Holy Spirit is present in the hearts of the reborn, or whether only gifts are kindled in the mind and heart, such as light in the mind and trust and love of God in the will and heart. But it is rightly answered that both are true. Both that the person of the Holy Spirit is present in the hearts of the reborn, and that gifts are kindled in the mind, will, and heart itself. Thus it is written in the Prophet Joel: I will pour out of my spirit upon all flesh, and to the Romans 8: If indeed the spirit of God dwells in you, these things are said concerning the person. But concerning the gifts themselves or effects, or qualities, as they call them in the schools, these sayings and similar ones speak clearly, to the Galatians 5: The fruit of the spirit is love, joy, peace, faith, goodness, continence, etc.

I have recited these things for this reason, that some questions in the Sentences of Lombard might be more easily judged and explained, which I willingly pass over, whether love kindled in the heart is some effect which is not the person of the Holy Spirit himself. I said that both must be affirmed, that the Holy Spirit is present in the hearts of the reborn, and that love is an effect, or quality, kindled in the heart by the Holy Spirit, with the will assenting and obeying. But I willingly break off these questions, about which there is unlearned and cold disputation in the commentaries of Lombard.

There remains also this question, about which it is enough to warn the studious. The more recent Greek Churches are said to have stirred up a contest: Whether the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, that is, whether he is from the essence of the Father and the Son, and they contended that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father, that is, is from the essence of the Father: And through the Son, as if sent carnally, and is not from the essence of the Son. Concerning this question, let us determine, as the Latin Churches feel, that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the eternal Father and the Son, that is, is from the essence of the eternal Father and the Son, just as Christ expressly says, John 16: He will glorify me, because he will receive from me, and Christ says here: I will send, he does not only say: He will be sent through me, as through a conduit. Now I return to the text, which again preaches concerning the effects of the Holy Spirit, and concerning the ministry of the Gospel.

Latin:

Qui a patre procedit.

Etsi articulus de essentia Dei, et de tribus personis, aeterno patre, et filio, et Spiritu sancto impervestigabilis est, et homines profani, ut Samosatenus, Iudaei, Mahometistae, et alii innumerabiles clamant absurdas opiniones esse, quod profitetur Ecclesia, filium natum esse ex substantia patris aeterni, coaeternum, ὁμοούσιον, et Spiritum sanctum ab utroque procedere. Tamen quia Deus claris et certis testimoniis ipse sese sic patefecit, ac voluit discerni Patrem, Filium, et Spiritum sanctum, necesse est nos hanc doctrinam amplecti, et reverenter assentiri, etiamsi diabolorum et hominum sapientia fremens absurditate offenditur.

Cur inquies, proponit nobis Deus articulos, quorum verba etiamsi utcunque imitamur, tamen rerum nullas imagines cogitare possumus? Audio filium dici λόγον, sed qualis est ille λόγος, cum sit persona? Audio discrimen esse inter nasci et procedere, agnosco diversa verba, sed rem propius videre cuperem. Excruciant hae quaestiones humanam mentem, sed quanquam modus esse harum descriptionum, et cogitationum debet, tamen sciamus Dei voluntatem esse, ut sic agnoscatur divinitas. Filius est factus redemtor et victima, hunc certe pater aeternus vult agnosci. Imo pronunciat homines ita iustos, et haeredes vitae aeternae, si propter hunc filium credant sibi donari remissionem peccatorum et vitam aeternam.

Misit et Spiritum sanctum visibili specie, ut dis- cernamus eum a patre et filio, et credamus eum mitti in pectora nostra, ut nos regat, et lucem, iusticiam et vitam aeternam in nobis incoët. Proprium filii beneficium est, quod est redemtor, proprium Spiritus sancti mitti in pectora creden- tium. Cum haec immensa bona quodam discri- mine personis attributa sint, vult certe personas aeternus pater agnosci et invocari. Imo Chri- stus dicit: Qui non honorat filium, non honorat patrem.

Sciamus ergo non negligendam esse, nec si- lentio obruendam doctrinam de tribus personis, sed reverenter eam cogitemus et recitemus, et tantum de ea quaeramus, quantum Deus patefe- cit. Patefecit autem ea quae in invocatione exer- ceri voluit, quoties invocamus, vult nos filium intueri, et propter eum petere remissionem pec- catorum, vult item peti, ut gubernemur Spiritu sancto. Haec discrimina semper in invocatione incurrant in mentem et in oculos.

Deinde pie cogitemus, quomodo patrem, aeternum filium et Spiritum sanctum doctrina Evangelii discernat. Ac notum est haec discri- mina tradi: Pater ab aeterno intuens sese gignit filium, qui est imago aeterni patris. Filius est genitus, et est imago aeterni patris. Spiritus sanctus procedit a patre aeterno et a filio.

Hic iam quaeritur, quid interest inter nasci et inter procedere? aut quid omnino significat il- lud procedere? Haec ita declarantur docendi cau- sa. Si hominum natura incorrupta esset, consi- deratio eius magis nos erudiisset de Deo. Sed sumamus tamen aliquo modo exempla ab homi- num natura. Duae sunt facultates animae, facul- tas intelligens, et facultas volens. Intelligens gignit imagines cogitando, volens habet impetus, sicut cor gignit spiritus, sentit amorem, laetitiam, et alios affectus. Ab his exemplis sumitur decla- ratio. Cum filius vocetur λόγος, gignitur cogi- tando. Est autem cogitatio imago rei cogitatae, λόγος igitur dicitur filius, quia filius est imago patris.

At Spiritus sanctus dicitur procedere, quia voluntatis est amor. Intuens igitur Pater Filium, vult et amat eum, ac vicissim filius intuens pa- trem, vult et amat eum. Hoc mutuo amore, qui proprie est voluntatum, procedit Spiritus sanctus, qui est agitator ab aeterno patre, et filio coae- terna imagine patris. Sicut igitur intelligenti fa- cultati tribuitur gignere: sic a voluntate dicimus processionem. Quia voluntas est sedes amoris et agitationis, de quibus ut aliquam qualemcunque umbram cogitemus, nos ipsos intueamur, agno- scamus cogitatione gigni imagines, voluntatem vero, aut cor habere impetus et amorem. In nobis non transfunditur essentia in imagines ul- las, aut in ullum amorem, seu impetum, etsi na- tura nostra vehementer cum amore, seu laetitia rapitur, et quasi in amatum obiectum migrat, sed aeterni patris imago, quae est filius, et est sub- stantia aeterni patris, et Spiritui sancto commu- nicatur essentia patris et filii.

Hic et formae sermonis observandae sunt. Alias de processione aeterna dicitur, qua Spiritus sanctus est persona tertia divinitatis, ut hic dici- tur: Qui a patre procedit, et haec proprie voca- tur processio. Alias de missione dicitur, qua Spiritus sanctus mittitur in corda hominum, qui fide renascuntur. Hanc interdum vocant aliqui processionem temporalem, sed usitatius dicitur Missio. Sicut et hic in textu nominatur: Quem ego mittam a patre, et de missione quaerunt, an Spiritus sancti persona adsit in cordibus rena- scentium, an vero tantum dona in mente et corde accendantur, ut lux in mente et in voluntate et corde fiducia, et dilectio Dei. Sed recte respon- detur, utrunque verum esse. Et personam Spi- ritus sancti adesse in cordibus renascentium, et in ipsa mente, voluntate et corde dona accendi. Ita scriptum est in Propheta Ioël: Effundam de meo spiritu super omnem carnem, et ad Roma- nos 8.: Siquidem spiritus Dei habitat in vobis, haec de persona dicuntur. De ipsis vero donis seu effectibus, seu qualitatibus, ut in scholis vocant, clare loquuntur haec dicta, et similia, ad Galat. 5.: Fructus spiritus est dilectio, gaudium, pax, fides, bonitas, continentia, etc.

Haec ideo recitavi, ut quaestiones aliquot in sententiis Longobardi facilius diiudicentur et ex- plicentur, quas volens praetereo, an sit effectus aliquis dilectio in corde accensa, qui non sit ipsa persona Spiritus sancti. Dixi utrunque affirman- dum esse, quod adsit in cordibus renatorum Spi- ritus sanctus, et quod dilectio sit effectus, seu qualitas accensa in corde per Spiritum sanctum, assentiente et optemperante voluntate. Sed liben- ter abrumpo has quaestiones, de quibus inerudite et frigide in commentariis Longobardi disputatur.

Restat et haec quaestio, de qua satis est mo- nere studiosos. Graecae Ecclesiae recentiores di- cuntur movisse certamen: An Spiritus sanctus procedat a patre et filio, id est, an sit ex essentia patris et filii, et contenderunt Spiritum sanctum a patre procedere, id est, ex patris essentia esse: Ac per filium, tanquam carnalem mitti, nec esse ex essentia filii. De hac quaestione statuamus, ut latinae Ecclesiae sentiunt, Spiritum sanctum ab aeterno patre et filio procedere, id est, esse ex es- sentia aeterni patris et filii, sicut Christus ex- presse inquit, Ioannis 16.: Ille me glorificabit, quia ex me accipiet, et Christus hic inquit: Ego mittam, non tantum ait: Per me mittetur, ut per canalem. Nunc ad textum redeo, qui de effecti- bus Spiritus sancti, et de ministerio Evangelii rursus concionatur.

## 15:26
He will testify of me, and you will testify.

Generally, when it is spoken of the effects of the Holy Spirit, both benefits must be embraced, that the ministry of the Gospel is preserved publicly, and true doctrine in the ministry, and that through the ministry the Holy Spirit is effective.

Then, however, privately in the hearts of those hearing the Gospel, he kindles faith, and other new motions consistent with the law of God, as it is said in Romans 8: You have received the spirit of adoption of sons, by which we cry Abba Father. Thus let the testimony be understood here, concerning both benefits, concerning the public ministry, and concerning faith privately in the hearts of individuals. This doctrine concerning both effects of the Holy Spirit has often been recited, and will soon be repeated more copiously.

He adds consolation, however, to confirm the Apostles. And you, he says, will be witnesses, because you are with me from the beginning. Why does he call teachers in the Church witnesses? First, this signifies that they do not beget a new kind of doctrine, but are witnesses of the doctrine received from Christ. Then he predicts concerning their constancy: If they will be witnesses, they will please God, and with great strength will gather the Church for God, having taxed impious opinions and crimes, and having abolished idols. But what he adds, because you are with me from the beginning, signifies what kind of witnesses he wants his own to be, who are not rude in doctrine, or novices, but who have already been hearers for a long time, and have become more learned and firmer by use.

Latin:

Ille testabitur de me, et vos testabimini.

Plerunque cum de effectibus Spiritus sancti dicitur, utrunque beneficium complectendum est, quod publice ministerium Evangelii servatur, et in ministerio vera doctrina, et quod per ministe- rium Spiritus sanctus est efficax.

Deinde vero privatim in cordibus audientium Evangelium accendit fidem, et alios novos motus congruentes legi Dei, ut dicitur Rom. 8.: Acce- pistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum, per quem cla- mamus Abba pater. Ita hic intelligatur testifi- catio, de utroque beneficio, de publico ministe- rio, et de fide privatim in singulorum cordibus. Haec doctrina de utrisque effectibus Spiritus sancti saepe recitata est, et mox copiosius repetetur.

Consolationem vero addit ad confirmandos Apostolos. Et vos, inquit, eritis testes, quia ab initio mecum estis. Quare vocat doctores in Ec- clesia testes? Primum, hoc significat, non gi- gnere eos novum doctrinae genus, sed testes esse doctrinae a Christo acceptae. Deinde praedicit de constantia eorum: Si erunt testes, placebunt Deo, et magno robore colligent Deo Ecclesiam, taxatis impiis opinionibus et sceleribus, et aboli- tis idolis. Quod vero addit, quia ab initio me- cum estis, significat quales esse suos testes velit, qui non sint rudes doctrinae, aut tyrones, sed qui iam diu fuerint auditores, et sint usu erudi- tiores et firmiores facti.

## 16:1 Argument
Chapter XVI.

Latin:

Caput XVI.

## 16:1
These things I have spoken to you.

When mention is made of the ministry, immediately the preaching concerning the cross is attached, which accompanies the profession of the Gospel. But lest minds be broken, it is necessary that they be forewarned and confirmed. This is what Christ intends when He says: That He says these things, lest, overcome by scandals, they fall away from the Gospel. Nor does Christ simply say here: That the Church will undergo huge calamities, but He makes mention of the chief crime which is objected; that species increases the grief. Two crimes, however, are objected to the Church, of which one is lighter, the other heavier. Either this species is used as a pretext for cruelty, that the disciples of Christ are the authors of public discords, and they are called seditious. This crime is objected to them by Maxentius, Diocletian, and the like. Although this calumny increases grief for the prudent, yet because the refutation is easy, and many openly see that those who defend foul errors with immense cruelty are the ones to be accused, those who are dragged to punishments are less moved by this crime. The other crime is more atrocious, which is objected to the disciples of Christ in that very assembly which is called the Church of God, namely, that they are the authors of impious dogmas, heretics, harming and destroying the glory of God. Here, since few understand the true doctrine, the greatest part necessarily judges that they must be removed, as offscourings, hostile and hateful to God, and pestiferous to the whole human race. This reproach is difficult to bear, namely, by the judgments of the powerful, in that very assembly which is called the Church of God, to be seen as an enemy of God, because they boast of the promises made to the Church, that it does not err. And it is true that great reverence is owed to the Church. Wherefore it is hard to oppose that assembly which has authority confirmed by many centuries and by the examples of great men.

Concerning this temptation Christ says here: Everyone who kills you will think he is offering a sacrifice to God. To leave behind property, spouse, children, life is difficult, but it is much more difficult to undergo this reproach, that you are an enemy of God and the Church. Therefore Christ forewarns us, and forbids us to cast away the Gospel, broken by this crime, and opposes this saying: They do not know the Father, nor me. It is an atrocious crime to be called seditious, but it is much more atrocious to be called an enemy of God and a blasphemer against

God, but because of these crimes the confession of the Gospel is not to be cast away, according to that: Whoever shall deny me before men, I also will deny him before my heavenly Father. This command is a rule which the Church ought to follow, however great the dangers and punishments proposed.

Latin:

Haec locutus sum vobis.

Cum mentio facta est ministerii, mox attexitur praedicatio de cruce, quae comitatur Evangelii professionem. Ne autem frangantur animi, praemoneri et confirmari eos necesse est. Id Christus vult, cum ait: Se haec dicere, ne scandalis victi deficiant ab Evangelio. Nec simpliciter hic dicit Christus: Ecclesiam subituram esse ingentes aerumnas, sed mentionem facit praecipui criminis, quod obiicitur, illa species auget dolorem. Duo autem crimina obiiciuntur Ecclesiae, quorum alterum levius, alterum gravius est. Aut praetexitur saevitiae haec species, quod discipuli Christi sint autores publicarum discordiarum, et dicuntur seditiosi. Hoc crimen obiiciunt eis Maxentius, Diocletianus, et similes. Etsi autem haec calumnia auget prudentibus dolorem, tamen quia facilis est refutatio, et multi palam vident eos accusandos esse, qui tetros errores defendunt immani crudelitate, minus hoc crimine moventur illi, qui ad supplicia rapiuntur. Alterum crimen atrocius est, quod obiicitur discipulis Christi in illo ipso coetu, qui vocatur Ecclesia Dei, videlicet, quod sint autores impiorum dogmatum, haeretici, laedentes et delentes gloriam Dei. Hic cum pauci intelligant veram doctrinam, maxima pars necessario eos tollendos censet, tanquam catharmata, inimica et invisa Deo, et pestifera toti generi humano. Hoc probrum difficile est sustinere, videlicet iudiciis potentum, in illo ipso coetu, qui vocatur Ecclesia Dei, videri hostem Dei, quia illi iactitant promissiones Ecclesiae factas, quod non erret. Et verum est, magnam reverentiam Ecclesiae deberi. Quare illi coetui, qui habet autoritatem multis seculis, et magnorum hominum exemplis confirmatam, adversari durum est.

De hac tentatione Christus hic inquit: Omnis qui vos interficit, putabit se offerre sacrificium Deo. Facultates, coniugem, liberos, vitam relinquere difficile est, sed multo difficilius subire hoc probrum, quod sis hostis Dei et Ecclesiae. Ideo Christus nos praemonet, et vetat abiicere Evangelium, fractos hoc crimine, et opponit hoc dictum: Non norunt patrem, nec me. Atrox crimen est, dici seditiosum, sed multo atrocius est, dici hostem Dei et blasphemum adversus

Deum, sed propter haec crimina non abiicienda est confessio Evangelii, iuxta illud: Qui negaverit me coram hominibus, negabo et ego eum coram patre meo coelesti. Hoc mandatum regula est, quam sequi Ecclesia debet, quantacunque pericula et supplicia proponuntur.

## 16:8
He will convict the world of sin.

To the forewarning concerning the cross He again adds consolation, and doctrine concerning the evangelical ministry. I go to the Father, that is, through the cross I will come to glory, but my death will bring you huge sadness and mourning, yet know that it will be profitable to you. He opposes, therefore, to the sad spectacle of death, the fruit and goods which will follow, and again He promises the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, and concerning His efficacy in the ministry publicly, and privately in the hearts of believers, He proposes a distinguished and most memorable discourse. And this narrative of the text is therefore to be looked at and considered more diligently, which has been greatly obscured by the insipid interpretations of many writers, who have hallucinated for this reason, because they understood neither the doctrine of the righteousness of faith, nor the distinction between Law and Gospel, nor did they consider the phrase. Now let us give thanks to God, that these great matters have been somewhat illustrated, and let us be more studious, lest this light be extinguished again.

Latin:

Arguet mundum de peccato.

Praemonitioni de cruce rursus addit consolationem, et doctrinam de ministerio evangelico. Ego ad patrem abeo, id est, per crucem veniam ad gloriam, sed vobis ingentem moesticiam, et luctum mea mors afferet, verum scitote vobis profuturam esse. Opponit igitur tristi spectaculo mortis, fructum et bona, quae sequentur, et rursus promittit consolatorem Spiritum sanctum, et de eius efficacia in ministerio publice, et privatim in cordibus credentium, insignem et maxime memorabilem concionem proponit. Et haec narratio textus ideo diligentius aspicienda et consideranda est, qui multorum scriptorum insulsis interpretationibus valde obscurata est, qui ideo hallucinati sunt, quia nec doctrinam de iusticia fidei, nec discrimen legis et Evangelii intellexerunt, nec phrasin consideraverunt. Nunc gratias Deo agamus, quod hae res tantae aliquantulum illustratae sunt, et simus studiosiores, ne haec lux rursus extinguatur.

## 16:8
He will convict the world.

What, therefore, does the Holy Spirit do when He comes? Will He establish a new polity, as Moses established, or will He tame the nations with arms, as the Jews dream of the empire of the Messiah? He commands these imaginations to be removed, and expressly says what He is about to do. He will convict, He says, the world. Let this word be understood first concerning the ministry of the Gospel, afterwards concerning the efficacy in the hearts of individuals. He will convict, that is, not with iron, not with arms, but by voice and by teaching He will accuse, convince, and condemn not a few, not only the lowest rabble, but the world, that is, the whole human race, and this word clearly, when He says: He will convict, testifies that repentance is to be preached in the Church, and it is greatly to be observed that He expressly says: The Holy Spirit will convict. Therefore, human reproof is not instituted by human counsel, as when Socrates reproves the vices of his fellow citizens, nor is it a vain voice, but an efficacious one that will penetrate into minds and hearts, and will kindle the recognition of sin and of the wrath of God, likewise of the promised of mercy, so that horrendous terrors may be stirred up, and in turn, in consolation, a new and eternal justice and life may be begun.

Let there be added, therefore, to this saying of Christ similar sentences which preach about the efficacy of the evangelical ministry, as in Romans 1: The Gospel is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth, that is, by this voice sounding the Gospel, men truly become heirs of eternal life who embrace that voice by faith. This seems ridiculous to human wisdom, to promise eternal life, or to say that it is begun in a man by some human voice. But the Prophets, Christ, and the Apostles inculcate this article so often, that they may confirm this sentence in us. So also in 2 Corinthians 3 it is said: He made us fit ministers of the new testament, not of the letter, but of the spirit: For the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life. That whole passage testifies without any ambiguity that the evangelical ministry is efficacious, and that by the voice of the Gospel believers become heirs of eternal life. Let the pious reader also remember this, when it is said: The Holy Spirit will convict, it signifies not only those sins which reason convicts are accused in this ministry, but many hidden evils, which it will recount afterwards. Reason does not judge the darkness born with us from God, and depraved inclinations, to be sins, or that ignorance of Christ, or unbelief, is a sin. But these evils are both condemned by the voice of the evangelical ministry, and hearts are moved by the Holy Spirit so that they may acknowledge that these evils are displeasing to God, and may tremble because of the judgment of God.

Of sin indeed, because they do not believe in me.

Although there are various interpretations of many, yet let us be hearers and disciples of Christ, let us follow the words which are sufficiently clear to those instructed in the Church, and let us not attach foreign meanings. This says clearly and simply: The Holy Spirit will convict this sin in the whole human race, namely the ignorance and contempt of the Son of God, because men neither know the promise concerning the Son, nor believe, but with horrible fury have forgotten this promise in the whole world, and have fashioned gods and cults with immense audacity; indeed, even among those who have heard the promise or the Gospel, like the people of Israel: yet few assent and believe, and some who do assent experience their own doubt and diffidence; the Holy Spirit will convict this very sin, which is the source of all other sins, and while it remains, no virtues please God. This is the native meaning which the words produce.

Many wise men dispute what is to be thought about Aristides, about Scipio, about Pomponius, or similar men, whether such men did not please God, since their most beautiful virtues were truly gifts of God? I answer: We must judge about them from the word of God; it is a sin not to acknowledge this Son of God as mediator, nor to believe that on account of him God receives and hears us, and in those in whom sin clings, in them many other horrendous evils remain. Because they cannot establish anything about the remission of sins, they flee from God, they do not call upon him, they never truly expect help from him, they rage against him, as if he cruelly burdens this nature. This confusion of many vices follows where there is no acknowledgment of Christ, and that true faith apprehending the remission of sins on account of Christ.

I have reviewed the examples of the Gentiles so that we may compare them to ourselves. We each grieve when we are polluted with homicide or adultery. But we do not grieve that trust in Christ does not burn in the heart. And yet it should have been thought that it is no less a sin not to believe in the Son of God than it is homicide or adultery.

But let someone ask whether the Holy Spirit will not also accuse other sins, or will he accuse only unbelief? The customary answer is: That unbelief is the source of sins, therefore by the accusation of this sin he includes the others. For the impious remain in other sins for this reason, because they do not return to God by faith and the acknowledgment of Christ, and sin remains as long as one does not believe in Christ; therefore it is necessary that unbelief be accused first, and when hearts are kindled with true faith in Christ, sins are taken away, and man is received, even if remnants of sin remain. It does not follow, however, on the contrary, that a man is received if other virtues are present and faith is lacking. This customary answer does not displease me, but it seems to me to be aptly answered if we say that Christ is preaching about that sin which is properly condemned by the voice of the Gospel, and is revealed in the Gospel; the others were previously condemned by the voice of the law, and yet it is true that, while unbelief remains, other sins remain. But when the acknowledgment of Christ shines forth, other sins are taken away and forgiven.

Latin:

Arguet mundum.

Quid igitur agit Spiritus sanctus veniens? num constituet novam politiam, ut Moses constituit, aut domabit gentes armis, ut somniant Iudaei Messiae imperium? Has imaginationes removeri iubet, et diserte dicit, quid acturus sit. Arguet, inquit, mundum. Haec vox primum de ministerio Evangelii, postea de efficacia in singulorum cordibus intelligatur. Arguet, id est, non ferro, non armis, sed voce ac docendo accusabit, convincet et damnabit non paucos, non infimam tantum plebeculam, sed mundum, id est, totum genus humanum, et clare haec vox, cum inquit: Arguet, testatur poenitentiam in Ecclesia praedicandam esse, ac valde observandum est, quod diserte inquit: Spiritus sanctus arguet. Non igitur humana reprehensio est instituta humano consilio, ut cum Socrates arguit vitia suorum civium, nec est vox irrita, sed efficax penetratura in mentes et corda, accensura agnitionem peccati et irae Dei, item promissae misericordiae, ut horrendi pavores excitentur, et rursus in consolatione incoëtur nova et aeterna iusticia et vita.

Adiungantur ergo ad hoc dictum Christi si- miles sententiae, quae de ministerii evangelici efficacia concionantur, ut Rom. 1.: Evangelium est potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti, id est, hac voce sonante Evangelium, vere homines fiunt haeredes vitae aeternae, qui eam vocem fide am- plectuntur. Ridiculum hoc videtur humanae sa- pientiae, polliceri vitam aeternam, aut dicere humana aliqua voce eam in homine incoari. Sed Prophetae, Christus et Apostoli inculcant hunc articulum toties, ut confirment in nobis hanc sen- tentiam. Ita et 2. Corinth. 3. dicitur: Fecit nos idoneos ministros novi testamenti, non literae, sed spiritus: Litera enim occidit, spiritus autem vivificat. Totus ille locus sine ulla ambiguitate testatur ministerium evangelicum esse efficax, et voce Evangelii credentes fieri haeredes vitae ae- ternae. Meminerit pius lector et hoc, cum dici- tur: Spiritus sanctus arguet, significat non tan- tum ea peccata, quae ratio arguit accusari in hoc ministerio, sed multa arcana mala, quae postea recensebit. Ratio non iudicat caliginem de Deo nobiscum nascentem, et pravas inclinationes pec- cata esse, aut ignorationem Christi, seu incredu- litatem peccatum esse. Sed haec mala et damnan- tur voce ministerii evangelici, et per Spiritum sanctum moventur corda, ut agnoscant haec mala displicere Deo, et expavescant propter iudicium Dei.

De peccato quidem, quia non credunt in me.

Etsi variae sunt multorum interpretationes, tamen simus auditores et discipuli Christi, sequa- mur verba quae satis perspicua sunt institutis in Ecclesia, nec peregrinas sententias affingamus. Hoc clare et simpliciter dicit: Spiritus sanctus ar- guet hoc peccatum in toto genere humano, scilicet ignorationem et contemtum filii Dei, quod homi- nes nec norunt promissionem de filio, nec cre- dunt, sed horribili furore obliti sunt in toto mundo hanc promissionem, et finxerunt deos et cultus immani audacia, imo inter hos qui audie- runt promissionem seu Evangelium, ut populus Israël: tamen pauci assentiuntur et credunt, et aliqui assentientes experiuntur suam dubitationem et diffidentiam, hoc ipsum peccatum, quod est fons omnium aliorum peccatorum, et quo ma- nente, non placent ullae virtutes Deo, arguet Spiritus sanctus. Haec est nativa sententia, quam gignunt verba.

Multi sapientes disputant, quid sentiendum est de Aristide, de Scipione, de Pomponio, aut similibus, an non placuerunt tales viri Deo, cum pulcerrimae eorum virtutes vere dona Dei fuerint? Respondeo: Nobis ex verbo Dei de ipsis iudicandum est, peccatum est non agnoscere hunc filium Dei mediatorem, nec credere quod propter eum Deus nos recipiat et exaudiat, et in quibus haeret peccatum, in his manent alia multa horrenda mala. Quia non possunt statuere de remissione peccatorum, fugiunt Deum, non invocant, nunquam vere ab ipso expectant auxilium, fremunt adversus eum, quasi crudeliter oneret hanc naturam. Haec confusio multorum vitiorum sequitur, ubi non est agnitio Christi, et illa vera fides apprehendens remissionem peccatorum propter Christum.

Recensui Ethnicorum exempla, ut ad nos ea conferamus. Singuli nos dolemus cum homicidio aut adulterio polluimur. Sed non dolemus, quod non ardet fiducia Christi in corde. Atqui sic sentiendum erat, non minus peccatum esse non credere in filium Dei, quam sit homicidium aut adulterium.

Quaerat autem aliquis, an non accusabit Spiritus sanctus etiam caetera peccata, aut solam accusabit incredulitatem? Usitata responsio est: Fontem esse peccatorum incredulitatem, ideo accusatione huius peccati comprehendit caetera. Nam ideo manent impii in caeteris peccatis, quia non redeunt ad Deum fide et agnitione Christi, et tamdiu manet peccatum, donec non creditur in Christum, ideo necesse est primum accusari incredulitatem, et cum corda accensa sunt vera fide in Christum, peccata tolluntur, et recipitur homo, etiamsi manent reliquiae peccati. Non autem sequitur econtra recipi hominem, si adsint aliae virtutes, et desit fides. Haec usitata responsio mihi non displicet, sed mihi videtur apte responderi, si dicamus Christum concionari de eo peccato, quod proprie damnatur voce Evangelii, et in Evangelio revelatur, caetera prius damnata sunt voce legis, et tamen verum est, manente incredulitate, manere caetera peccata. Illucescente vero agnitione Christi, tolli et condonari caetera peccata.

## 16:10
Of righteousness, because I go to the Father.

This member has seemed obscure to many interpreters. For what is this new definition of righteousness, that our righteousness is the transition of Christ to the Father? For the law says far otherwise, that our righteousness is obedience according to all the commandments. But I said above, to those who are ignorant of the distinction between the law and the Gospel, this passage is mere darkness. But those rightly instructed in the Gospel understand what is being said. It is true that the righteousness of the law is our virtues, but the righteousness which is given in the Gospel is the transition and kingdom of Christ. For on account of the transition, that is, the death of Christ, the remission of sins and reconciliation are given to us: or the transition and death of Christ are given to us, so that on account of this sacrifice we may be accepted. And because Christ sits at the right hand of the Father, and intercedes for us, we are the inheritance of Christ, and are gifted with the Holy Spirit, eternal righteousness, and life. This simplest interpretation is true and native, just as it is evident that Paul speaks often, as in 1 Cor. 1: From him you are in Christ Jesus, who was made for us wisdom from God, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption. He says that Christ is our righteousness, which is to be understood in both ways: both because his righteousness is given to us, that is, on account of him we are righteous and accepted, and because he effects in us new and eternal righteousness and life. You should think, therefore, that your righteousness is not your virtues and your purity, but look upon the Son of God, the mediator who suffered and was resurrected for you, and who is now interceding for you. This righteousness is given to you, so that you may be righteous and accepted on account of him, and so that it may not be merely an imputation while sin and death remain, he effects righteousness and eternal life in us here.

Wherefore when it is said: The Holy Spirit will convict the world of righteousness, he affirms that he will accuse this very opinion of human reason, which feigns that men are righteous, that is, having the remission of sins, and accepted, on account of their own honest exercises, virtues, worship, and discipline. Just as the Jews, Mohammedans, Anabaptists, monks, and all hypocrites, fascinated by the admiration of their own exercises, most stubbornly defend this opinion, that they are righteous on account of their exercises and that certain severity of discipline, and they execrate this voice of the Gospel, which says: That we are righteous on account of Christ who suffered for us, and was resurrected and is reigning, not on account of our own exercises or our purity, as a corruption of good morals and a loosening of discipline, as the struggles of Paul show, which he had with the defenders of the righteousness of the law, and similar huge struggles have arisen in our age.

Latin:

De iusticia quia ad patrem vado.

Hoc membrum multis interpretibus obscurius visum est. Quae est enim haec nova definitio iusticiae, iusticia nostra est transitus Christi ad patrem? Longe enim aliter lex inquit, iusticiam nostram esse obedientiam iuxta omnia praecepta. Sed dixi supra, iis qui ignorant discrimen legis et Evangelii, hunc locum meras tenebras esse. Sed recte instituti in Evangelio intelligunt quid dicatur. Verum est legis iusticiam esse nostras virtutes, sed iusticia, quae in Evangelio donatur, est Christi transitus et regnum. Nam propter transitum, id est, mortem Christi, dantur nobis remissio peccatorum, et reconciliatio: seu transitus et mors Christi donantur nobis, ut propter hoc sacrificium simus accepti. Et quia Christus sedet ad dextram patris, et interpellat pro nobis, sumus haereditas Christi, et donamur Spiritu sancto, aeterna iusticia et vita. Haec simplicissima interpretatio vera et nativa est, sicut constat saepe loqui Paulum, ut 1. Cor. 1.: Ex ipso vos estis in Christo Iesu, qui factus est nobis sapientia a Deo, et iusticia, et sanctificatio, et redemtio. Ait Christum esse nostram iusticiam, quod utroque modo intelligatur, et quia ipsius iusticia nobis donatur, hoc est, propter eum iusti et accepti sumus, et quia efficit in nobis novam et aeternam iusticiam et vitam. Cogites igitur iusticiam tuam esse, non virtutes tuas, et tuam munditiem, sed intuere filium Dei mediatorem pro te passum et resuscitatum, ac nunc pro te interpellantem. Huius iusticia tibi donatur, ita, ut sis propter eum iustus et acceptus, et ne sit tantum imputatio manente peccato et morte, hic iusticiam et vitam aeternam in nobis efficit.

Quare cum dicitur: Spiritus sanctus arguet mundum de iusticia, hanc ipsam rationis humanae opinionem accusaturum esse affirmat, quae fingit homines esse iustos, id est, habentes remissionem peccatorum, et acceptas, propter propria honesta exercitia, virtutes, cultus, disciplinam. Sicut Iudaei, Mahometistae, Anabaptistae, Monachi, et omnes hypocritae fascinati admiratione suorum exercitiorum, pertinacissime propugnant hanc opinionem, quod sint iusti propter sua exercitia, et illam qualemcunque severitatem disciplinae, et hanc vocem Evangelii, quae dicit: Nos iustos esse propter Christum passum pro nobis, et resuscitatum et regnantem, non propter propria exercitia, aut munditiem nostram, execrantur, tanquam corruptelam bonorum morum, et disci- plinae laxationem, ut certamina Pauli ostendunt, quae ei cum defensoribus iusticiae legis fuerunt, et extiterunt nostra aetate similia certamina in- gentia.

## 16:11
Of judgment, because the prince of this world has already been judged.

The first two parts embrace the sum of the doctrine concerning sin and righteousness, concerning the ignorance of God, concerning unbelief fleeing from God, concerning faith in Christ the mediator, crucified, resurrected, sitting at the right hand of the Father, interceding for us, concerning the governance by which Christ, sitting at the right hand of the Father, gives the Holy Spirit, excites the ministers of the Gospel, gathers the Church, and begins in it new light, righteousness, and eternal life. This is the sum of the Gospel, which he said the Holy Spirit would propagate through the ministry. When this voice sounds and the Church begins to be gathered, then indeed struggles arise, and huge discords of judgments. The Church affirms that the voice of the Gospel is true, and a firm and immovable sentence of God, concerning the true worship of God and the salvation of men. But the Epicurean and hypocritical judgments of those who despise God cry out in opposition. Tyrants and other Epicureans clamor that the Gospel is a monstrous and empty fable. Hypocrites, who defend false worship, complain that ceremonies and exercises pleasing to God are being abolished, and the rein of discipline is being loosened, and public harmony is being disturbed. Therefore, in order to oppress the voice of the Gospel, they exercise cruelty against the professors of the Gospel.

Concerning this diversity of judgments, Christ consoles us when he says: The Holy Spirit will convict the world of judgment, namely, the world condemning the Gospel, and raging with horrible cruelty for the sake of destroying the Gospel, that is, the Holy Spirit will accuse the world condemning the Gospel and attempting to destroy it. How will he accuse it? He will excite teachers so that they may confess, and he will confirm the hearts and minds of those confessing and hearing against the furies of tyrants, so that they do not allow themselves to be deterred by the magnitude of the most atrocious punishments, and he will invite many more to the Gospel. Therefore, a manifold consolation is proposed to us, the Holy Spirit is promised, so that he may rule our minds, so that they may judge rightly, so that they may confess bravely, so that they may know that confession will be effective, will invite and confirm many, and the Gospel cannot be destroyed, and a testimony is proposed, by which Christ affirms that the confession of the Gospel is pleasing to God, and that the furies of the Epicureans and hypocrites, who hate the Gospel and attempt to destroy it, are condemned, and that their attempts will be in vain, and that God will take vengeance in this life and after this life upon the enemies of the Gospel, just as Judas, Herod, Agrippa, and many others perished by manifest miracles. This consolation the martyrs proposed to themselves in the time of Diocletian and in similar times, thinking thus: although we are weak and the emperor's power is great, which seems as if it will utterly destroy the Church of God, yet we know that the Holy Spirit has been promised to us. Let us ask that our hearts be kindled and confirmed by this, so that, not broken by the fear of punishments, we may fail from the Gospel, but may constantly confess. And although the judgments of the world are sought to disturb concord in empires by confession, yet let us know that this worship is pleasing to God, and that these are not merely empty and foolish contentions, as many say, but in these struggles the Holy Spirit is truly effective, calls and confirms others, and gathers the eternal Church. Some time later God will refute the judgments of the world, will destroy tyrants, and will bring forth testimonies which will show that the confession of the Gospel is true, just as the Holy Spirit confirmed the witnesses of the Gospel with many miracles, and punished the enemies, as in Acts 13, Elymas the Sorcerer is punished with sudden blindness. And Diocletian, after he had long exercised cruelty, brought death upon himself, and many miracles of the martyrs confirmed the pious and increased the Church.

We have need of this same consolation at this time also. Our weakness is great, there are many everywhere to whom the Gospel has shone in some way, and who have begun to call upon God more rightly, and have the beginnings of faith and true obedience, but the strength of few is such that they dare to confess; let us therefore ask to be kindled and confirmed by the Holy Spirit. Furthermore, many are deterred by this reproach, that we are called the authors of discords. Against this calumny, oppose this word: Whoever shall have confessed me before men, I will confess him before my heavenly Father. And here it is said that the Holy Spirit himself convicts the world. Therefore, whether discords or the tearing apart of kingdoms follow, one must obey the Holy Spirit, who commands and exercises confession. Finally, let us not be moved by that mockery of the Epicureans, who say that these struggles of ours are useless. Nay, since the Holy Spirit convicts the world, this work will be effective, the Church will be gathered, it will not be destroyed, and those very tyrants who rage most atrociously will truly be punished. Let us often think upon these consolations, so that we may learn and perform true worship.

Moreover, a reason is added to this consolation: Because the prince of this world has been judged, that is, condemned. When the devil rages so cruelly through tyrants and other impious men, so that he seems as if he will utterly destroy the Church of God, in this sad spectacle let us raise ourselves with these consolations, that the Church of God is to remain, as it is said in Matthew 16: And the gates of hell shall not prevail against it, and John 10: My sheep hear my voice, and no one shall snatch them from my hands, and here it is said: The prince of the world has been condemned, that is, although he still lies in wait for the Church and wounds many members, yet he will not conquer; those who believe in Christ will struggle out of the snares in this way, both because Christ himself covers and defends the Church, and because those who believe in Christ seek help by faith in all dangers, there they experience the victories of Christ.

But let someone ask, where, by what sentence, by what saying has the devil been condemned? I answer: First, he has been condemned by the express voice of God, Genesis 3, immediately at the restoration of the Church: The seed of the woman shall crush the head of the serpent, and the serpent shall lie in wait for his heel. Here God affirms that the seed of the woman, that is, the coming deliverer born of a woman, will repress the power of the devil and will take vengeance upon the devil. For to crush the head does not signify only a struggle with the devil, but signifies the overthrow of diabolical power, and the oppression and punishment of the devils; on the contrary, the devil will hurt the heel of Christ and the Church, that is, he will indeed atrociously wound Christ and the Church. Just as David was horribly wounded, when, having committed adultery, he impelled him to kill the husband of the woman he had seized, and afterwards incited his son to stir up sedition. These were horrible bites, and in the hearts of individual pious people the devil makes some savage wounds, so that they are almost overwhelmed by despair, but yet the promise of God consoles us; we hear that not the head, but the sole of the foot is wounded; Christ remains the victor, and he heals these our wounds, when we flee to him.

Add to this many sayings from the Gospel, which preach about the condemnation of the devil, as in Matt. 25: Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire, which is prepared for the devil and his angels, and in Luke 20 it is said: I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven. And the condemnation of the devil is described in Coloss. 2: Christ confidently led in triumph the powers stripped by himself, etc.

But profane men, secure and given over to pleasures, think this whole doctrine about these struggles, about the snares of the devil, about the victory of Christ, about our victories, to be feigned terrors and old wives' tales; therefore it is difficult to speak about this matter. But it is useful for sane men to contemplate the power and furies of the devil in the whole history of the world. See how immediately from the beginning he arms the impious brother against Abel. Afterwards he filled the world with idols, and demented men to such a degree that they thought the slaughter of children and lusts were the worship of God. Then what sad spectacles there are, the destructions of so many cities, in which mothers cooked the flesh of their children, and legions were decimated to feed the remaining soldiers; when Brutus had surrounded the city of the Xanthians in Lycia with a siege, the citizens themselves burned the city and destroyed themselves, others stabbing themselves with the sword: and a woman was seen who had hanged herself from the roof of her house, and had hung her strangled infant from her own neck, and in her right hand was holding a torch, with which she was setting the house on fire. Let us not pass by these horrible spectacles with idle minds, but let us deplore the horrible wrath of God against the sins of the human race, and let us confess that the devil truly rages against men, and oppresses those who have been deserted by God with a huge mass of miseries. Although examples of diabolical furies are nowhere lacking, just as recently a miserable mother in this neighborhood killed her children, nevertheless those who are in those regions where Turkish armies exercise their cruelty see more diabolical spectacles.

Let us be moved by the thought of these such great miseries, so that we may not be secure, nor forget the threats of Christ, and in this thought let us invoke the Son of God, who conquered, so that he might help us, and bring us aid in our dangers, and conquer that dire enemy; by faith and invocation, let us flee in our miseries to the Son of God our champion, which if we do, we shall experience that we are truly helped and liberated. Unless the devil had been judged, that is, condemned, so clearly that he cannot rage as he desires, the individual members of the Church would be entangled in such horrible evils that they could not struggle free, but because he is restrained by the Son of God, they emerge, just as Adam, having fallen, was restored, and afterwards raised up in many huge sorrows: and David escaped from so many sins and scandals. Let us look upon these examples, and compare to them our dangers and miseries inexplicable by human counsels, and let us propose this consolation to ourselves: the devil has been judged and condemned, so that he may not conquer the Son of God and those fleeing to him. Let us therefore invoke the Son of God, and seek defense and liberation, and let us not think this invocation to be in vain, but let faith burn, and await the help of Christ, which when we do, we shall truly experience liberation.

These exercises of faith must be learned by practice, but for the most part men entangled in dangers, when they are destitute of human counsels, and see that they are not helped by secondary causes and by those means which human reason can foresee, become weakened and lose faith, and consider invocation to be an empty murmur, and finally, they either fall into Epicurean furies, or, oppressed by grief, perish, like Saul and Judas. Against these most sad temptations Christ consoles us in this text. Wherefore let us fix this saying in our minds, and think of it assiduously. This meditation will illustrate this sermon of Christ more than any prolix explanations. Although it also profits the hearer to be reminded to compare his own dangers to the consolation, and to oppose it to the fiery darts of the devil, who strives especially for this, that he may impel weakened minds to rush into contempt of God, or into despair. Against these extreme evils let us be intent, and let us fortify ourselves with these promises of Christ so often repeated.

Latin:

De iudicio, quia princeps mundi iam iudi- catus est.

Priores duae partes complectuntur summam doctrinae de peccato et de iusticia, de ignora- tione Dei, de incredulitate fugiente Deum, de fide in Christum mediatorem, crucifixum, resus- citatum, sedentem ad dextram patris, interpel- lantem pro nobis, de gubernatione, qua Christus sedens ad dextram patris, dat Spiritum sanctum, excitat ministros Evangelii, colligit Ecclesiam, incoat in ea novam lucem, iusticiam, et vitam aeternam. Haec est summa Evangelii, quam di- xit Spiritum sanctum per ministerium propaga- turum esse. Haec vox cum sonat et coepit colligi Ecclesia, tum vero oriuntur certamina, et ingen- tes discordiae iudiciorum. Ecclesia affirmat vo- cem Evangelii veram esse, et firmam et immotam Dei sententiam, de veris cultibus Dei, et de sa- lute hominum. At iudicia contemnentium Deum epicurea et hypocritica reclamant. Tyranni et alii Epicurei clamitant Evangelium esse porten- tosam et inanem fabulam. Hypocritae, qui fal- sos cultus defendunt, quaeruntur aboleri ceremo- nias, et exercitia Deo placentia, et laxari frenum disciplinae, et concordiam publicam turbari. Ideo ut opprimant Evangelii vocem, saevitiam exercent adversus Evangelii professores.

De hac diversitate iudiciorum Christus con- solatur nos, cum ait: Spiritus sanctus arguet mundum de iudicio, videlicet condemnante Evan- gelium, et horribili saevitia grassante, delendi Evangelii causa, id est, Spiritus sanctus accusa- bit mundum condemnantem Evangelium, et de- lere conantem. Quomodo accusabit? Excita- bit doctores, ut confiteantur, et adversus tyran- norum furores confirmabit pectora et animos con- fitentium et audientium, ne deterreri se sinant magnitudine atrocissimorum suppliciorum, et multo plures ad Evangelium invitabit. Proponi- tur ergo nobis multiplex consolatio, promittitur Spiritus sanctus, ut regat nostras mentes, ut recte iudicent, ut fortiter confiteantur, ut sciant con- fessionem efficacem fore, multos invitaturam et confirmaturam, nec posse deleri Evangelium, et testimonium proponitur, quo affirmat Christus Deo placere confessionem Evangelii, et damnari furores Epicureorum et hypocritarum, qui Evan- gelium oderunt, et delere conantur, et conatus eorum irritos fore, et Deum poenas in hac vita et post hanc vitam de hostibus Evangelii sumturum esse, sicut perierunt Iudas, Herodes, Agrippa, et alii multi manifestis miraculis. Hanc conso- lationem sibi martyres tempore Diocletiani et si- milibus temporibus proponebant, sic cogitantes, etsi sumus imbecilles et imperatoris magna est po- tentia, quae videtur penitus deletura esse Eccle- siam Dei, tamen scimus nobis promissum esse Spiritum sanctum. Hoc accendi et confirmari pectora nostra petamus, ne fracti metu suppli- ciorum, deficiamus ab Evangelio, sed constanter confiteamur. Et quanquam mundi iudicia quae- runtur turbari confessione concordiam in impe- riis, tamen sciamus Deo placere hunc cultum, nec esse tantum inanes et fatuas contentiones, ut multi dicunt, sed his certaminibus Spiritus san- ctus vere est efficax, vocat et confirmat alios, et colligit aeternam Ecclesiam. Aliquanto post Deus refutabit mundi iudicia, delebit tyrannos, et te- stimonia edet, quae ostendent Evangelii confes- sionem veram esse, sicut multis miraculis Spiri- tus sanctus confirmavit testes Evangelii, et puni- vit hostes, ut Act. 18. Elymas Magus subita caecitate punitur. Et Diocletianus postquam diu exercuit saevitiam, sibi ipsi mortem conscivit, et miracula multa martyrum confirmaverunt pios, et Ecclesiam auxerunt.

Hac eadem consolatione nobis et hoc tem- pore opus est. Magna est imbecillitas nostra, multi sunt ubique, quibus aliquo modo illuxit Evangelium, et qui rectius coeperunt invocare Deum, et initia fidei et verae obedientiae habent, sed paucorum tantum est robur, ut confiteri au- sint, petamus ergo nos accendi et confirmari Spi- ritu sancto. Deinde multi deterrentur hoc pro- bro, quod dicimur autores discordiarum. Ad- versus hanc calumniam opponito hanc vocem: Qui confessus fuerit me coram hominibus, con- fitebor eum coram patre coelesti. Et hic dicitur, Spiritus sanctus ipse arguere mundum. Sive igi- tur discordiae, sive dilacerationes regnorum se- quantur, Spiritui sancto obediendum est, qui confessionem praecipit et exercet. Postremo nec illa Epicureorum subsannatione moveamur, qui dicunt haec nostra certamina inutilia esse. Imo cum Spiritus sanctus arguat mundum, erit id opus efficax, colligetur Ecclesia, non delebitur, vere etiam punientur illi ipsi tyranni, qui atro- cissime grassantur. Has consolationes saepe cogi- temus, ut veros cultus discamus et praestemus.

Est autem addita ratio huic consolationi, Quia princeps mundi huius iudicatus est, id est, condemnatus. Cum diabolus adeo crudeliter gras- satur per tyrannos et alios impios homines, ut videatur funditus deleturus esse Ecclesiam Dei, in hoc tristi spectaculo nos erigamus his consola- tionibus, quod Ecclesia Dei sit mansura, sicut Matth. 16. dicitur: Et portae inferorum non prae- valebunt adversus eam, et Ioan. 10.: Oves meae vocem meam audiunt, et nemo rapiet eas de ma- nibus meis, et hic dicitur: Princeps mundi con- demnatus est, id est, etsi adhuc insidiatur Ec- clesiae, et multa membra sauciat, tamen non vin- cet, eluctabuntur ex insidiis credentes in Chri- stum, hoc modo, et quia ipse Christus tegit et defendit Ecclesiam, et quia credentes in Christum fide petunt auxilium in omnibus periculis, ibi ex- periuntur victorias Christi.

Quaerat autem aliquis, ubi, qua sententia, quo dicto condemnatus sit diabolus? Respondeo: Primo expressa voce Dei condemnatus est, Ge- nes. 3. statim in Ecclesiae instauratione: Semen mulieris conteret caput serpentis, et serpens in- sidiabitur calcaneo eius. Hic affirmat Deus se- men mulieris, id est, venturum liberatorem na- tum ex muliere, potentiam diaboli repressurum esse, et sumturum poenas de diabolo. Nam con- terere caput non significat tantum certamen cum diabolo, sed significat eversionem potentiae dia- bolicae, et oppressionem et poenas diabolorum, econtra diabolus laedet calcaneum Christi et Ec- clesiae, hoc est, atrociter quidem vulnerabit Chri- stum et Ecclesiam. Sicut David horribiliter vul- neratus est, cum facto adulterio, impulit eum ad necandum maritum raptae mulieris, et postea in- citavit filium ad movendam seditionem. Hi fue- runt horrendi morsus, et in singulorum piorum cordibus diabolus aliqua saeva vulnera facit, ut pene opprimantur desperatione, sed tamen pro- missio Dei nos consolatur, audimus non caput, sed plantam pedis sauciari, manet victor Christus, et sanat haec nostra vulnera, cum ad eum con- fugimus.

Huc adde multa dicta ex Evangelio, quae de condemnatione diaboli concionantur, ut Matth. 25.: Discedite a me maledicti in ignem aeternum, qui paratus est diabolo et angelis eius, et Lu- cae 20. dicitur: Videbam satanam ut fulgur ex coelo cadere. Et condemnatio diaboli describi- tur ad Coloss. 2.: Duxit Christus confidenter in triumpho exutas potestates per seipsum, etc.

Sed hanc totam doctrinam de his certamini- bus, de insidiis diaboli, de victoria Christi, de nostris victoriis, homines profani, securi, et dediti voluptatibus, putant esse ficta terricula- menta, et aniles fabulas, ideo difficile est de hac re loqui. Sed potentiam et furores diaboli con- templari homines sanos utile est in tota mundi historia. Vide ut statim ab initio armat impium fratrem adversus Abel. Postea mundum comple- vit idolis, ac dementavit homines adeo, ut ma- ctationes liberorum, et libidines putarent esse cultus Dei. Deinde quam tristia spectacula sunt, tot urbium excidia, in quibus matres coxerunt carnes liberorum, et legiones decimatae sunt ad alendos reliquos milites, cum Brutus cinxisset obsidione urbem Xanthiorum in Lycia, cives ipsi urbem incenderunt, et sese perdiderunt, alii sese fodientes ferro: et conspecta est mulier, quae sese suspenderat de tecto suae domus, et de suo collo strangulatum infantem suspenderat, et in dextra tenebat facem, qua domum inflammabat. Haec horrenda spectacula non praetereamus otiosis ani- mis, sed deploremus horrendam iram Dei, ad- versus peccata generis humani, et fateamur dia- bolum vere grassari adversus homines, et eos qui deserti sunt a Deo, ingenti mole aerumnarum opprimere. Etsi nusquam desunt exempla furo- rum diabolicorum, sicut nuper misera mater in hac vicinia suos liberos interfecit, tamen qui sunt in iis regionibus, ubi Turcici exercitus suam sae- vitiam exercent, vident plura spectacula diabolica.
