It is to be lamented that human wisdom generally imagines in all men that the snares of the devil and grave falls can be avoided by our own diligence. But let the saying of Jeremiah be in our sight: I know, O Lord, that the way of man is not his own. Nothing is easier for man than to hallucinate, to be deceived, and to err. Therefore, let us often think of this saying of Christ; he commands both, vigilance and prayer; Christ wants us to be intent and circumspect. But because he commands us to pray, he signifies that not all falls can be avoided by our own circumspection, but that there is need of divine governance, and let us know that great consolation is proposed to us as often as prayer is commanded. For it follows that prayer is not empty, as all Epicureans think, for it is not commanded in vain. Confirmed by this consolation, let us be more ardent in praying, and let us ask God to rule our minds, our dangers, and the outcomes of our dangers.

Then in the same place follows the kiss of the traitor, which signifies that many lie in wait for the teachers of the Gospel with the simulation of friendship, and the chief part of this act is the seizing of Christ, in which let the divine power itself be considered, so that we may acknowledge that Christ suffers not compelled by human power, but willingly, as it is written in Isaiah: He was offered, because he willed it. For the soldiers fall prostrate at one word of Christ. To this act also pertains the fight of Peter, in which let the error of the Apostles be considered again, who were still dreaming of an earthly empire. And here a notable voice is uttered, which testifies that the Apostles do not bear the sword, that is, that the ministry of the Gospel is not the power of the sword, as they call it. It teaches likewise that it is the ordinance of God that all who use the sword without laws and against their calling should be punished by the sword. For when it is said: Everyone who takes the sword will perish by the sword, let those be understood to take the sword who attempt to exercise the power of the sword not given by laws or magistrates, as do all who commit unjust homicides, and all seditious persons. Moreover, the saying of Christ is taken from chapter 9 of Genesis: Whoever sheds human blood, by man shall his blood also be shed. Nor is this law repeated without grave cause in this very final agony of Christ, perhaps so that all posterity may be warned not to seize empires under the pretext of the Gospel, as the Roman Pontiffs have done, and the Anabaptists, and often others have sought empires for no legitimate cause, but only under the pretext of the Gospel. Let us therefore be cautious, lest we aid seditious counsels. There are also significations in the act itself; Peter cuts off the right ear of the servant of the High Priest. Ambitious teachers cut off the ear, that is, they pour false interpretations into the right ear, by which they confirm seditious counsels, as when the Roman Pontiffs moved wars against the German Emperors, the Henrys; they feigned that they were defending the freedom of suffrage in electing Bishops; the appearance was honest, but yet it was not a just cause for waging wars. The final part of this act in the garden is the flight of all the Apostles, which is an example of the common infirmity of men. Thus far has been spoken briefly about the first act: in which there are very many parts, the doctrine of which cannot be exhausted, namely the very dread and sorrow of Christ, the confirmation of Christ, the betrayal of Judas, the testimony of divine power in Christ, who prostrated the cohort with a single word, the prohibition of the fight, the healing of the wounded, the weakness of the Apostles.

Let the second act be the confession of Christ, first in the house of Annas, then in the house of Caiaphas, and the accusations, insults, and condemnations, and Peter's denial and repentance. The main question, however, is whether he is the Messiah, and whether Christ is the Son of God; he answers clearly, and affirms both: I am the Messiah, and I am the Son of God. I believe, however, that these were distinct questions for them: because the Pharisees did not think the Messiah was by nature the Son of God, and they rage most of all when this confession is heard, and they shout that it is blasphemous, and they boldly pass sentence, he is guilty of death, and immediately they add many insults.

But first, let the responses of Christ be observed here, when the high priest asks about his doctrine, he is rebuked by Christ, and referred to the hearers: Why, he says, do you ask me? Ask those who have heard me. These words are not those of one prevaricating or avoiding confession, but Christ maintains the distinction between the condemnation of manifest crimes and the investigation of non-manifest ones. One should not be questioned about manifest things, as to what the accused confesses or does not confess. But the crime must be clearly objected, and confirmed by the true authority of witnesses, especially concerning doctrine, so that it may be expressly shown what impious opinion someone has spread. On the other hand, in the investigation of secret matters, a fraternal admonition should first precede, if suspicion has provided the occasion. Then let an investigation be made, if the suspicions are confirmed, and there is no doubt that this very order of the court was customary in the synagogue, because Christ also follows this form, Matt. 18. Justly, therefore, does Christ rebuke the High Priest, because in a manifest case he does not observe the order, or if the case is not yet manifest, it was not just to seize the accused with an armed cohort. Therefore, let the reader first consider here the order of judgment, and distinguish the condemnation of manifest cases from the investigation of secret ones, in which a fraternal admonition must necessarily precede.

And the priest's servant understood that the interrogation was being rebuked, therefore he gives blows to Christ, saying: Do you answer the High Priest so? Christ refutes him also, and from this the unlearned argue about tolerance, and allege the saying of Christ: If anyone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other to him. This, they say, Christ does not observe, because he does not remain silent, but expostulates and disputes with the servant; I will clear up this quibble for the sake of the simpler ones. It is a precept of both: to defend the true cause, especially of doctrine, with a clear confession, and at the same time to be prepared in mind to endure violence. Thus in this place Christ affirms that he answered rightly, or if I have not answered rightly, he says: Show the cause, but you are exercising unjust cruelty against me; therefore it is useful to remember this example. It is not tolerance to be silent, and to confirm by silence the false and unjust cause of an adversary. Indeed, especially the confession of doctrine must be clear, as it is written: Whoever shall have confessed me before men, I also will confess him before my heavenly Father. Then, when you have spoken about the cause as much as it is necessary to be said, let the mind be prepared to endure the lacerations of the body, whatever may threaten, as Christ here sustains various insults and tortures. Nor should that saying: If anyone strikes you on the right cheek, be understood superstitiously concerning silence, or the very gesture of turning the other cheek. Because Peter says: Being patient when there is need, that is, when the fury of enemies rushes upon us, let the heart provide tolerance, which what it is, is often said elsewhere: We do not order enemies to rage against us. It is useful to know and follow this rule in many affairs of life. If someone harms your reputation, it is not necessary for you to be silent, but you should modestly excuse yourself, and refute the adversary; if he does not yield when refuted, and the judges do not defend you, as they ought. Christ by his word and example consoles you, so that you may know why tolerance should be provided, and how it pleases God.

After Christ's expostulation with the servant, Peter's fall is described. In this history, manifold doctrine is contained. First, an admonition is proposed concerning our weakness. Second, an example of repentance is handed down, and testimony concerning the receiving of those who have fallen. Third, a distinction is to be considered here between the denial of Peter and blasphemies.

First, concerning our weakness.

It is certain that Peter was sanctified by the Holy Spirit, just as it is said to him in Matt. 16: Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood has not revealed it to you, but my Father, who is in heaven, and his faith had been confirmed, having watched the resuscitation of the dead, of Lazarus and others, he had also done the miracles themselves. Therefore there was in Peter a good intention, as these words testify, Luke 22: I am ready to go with thee into death. It seemed therefore that there was a mediocre strength of faith in Peter, and yet, disturbed by the slight terrors of a maidservant and servants, he casts away his confession. Such was David, gifted with the Holy Spirit and confirmed by many of his own and others' miracles. Indeed, he had even been a spectator of the most sad end of Saul, which example God set forth for succeeding kings, that they might fear God more. And yet David is overcome by the flames of adultery, and immediately heaps up great sins. Reminded by these examples of infirmity, let us amend our security, and lay aside confidence in ourselves, let us learn to fear God, and to seek help and divine governance. Let us keep in readiness also the sayings concerning this doctrine, John 15: Without me you can do nothing. Matthew 16: Watch and pray, that you enter not into temptation: The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak. 1 Peter last: Watch, because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about, seeking whom he may devour. 2 Cor. 10: He that thinketh himself to stand, let him take heed lest he fall. Matthew 12: Coming he findeth the house empty, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first. To the Phil. 2: With fear and trembling work out your salvation. 2 Cor. 3: We are not sufficient to think anything of ourselves, as of ourselves. By these and similar sayings let us excite ourselves to the recognition of our infirmity, to the fear of God, to the petition of help, just as the whole Psalm 119 is such a doctrine and prayer: Deal with thy servant according to thy mercy, and teach me thy justifications. Likewise: Direct my steps according to thy word, and let no injustice have dominion over me. Secondly, let us consider the example of repentance. In Luke chapter 22 these words are read: And immediately, while he was yet speaking, the cock crew, and the Lord turning looked on Peter, and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, and going out, he wept bitterly. In these words are described contrition and the cause of contrition. Bitter tears signify the sorrow in the heart of Peter recognizing his sad and great fall. The cause of contrition moving the heart of Peter was that Christ, looking upon him, kindled the recognition of this so great a fall and the sorrow. Thus contrition is made, the Holy Spirit moving hearts through the word of God.

Although it is not written where Peter was during these two days, or what he did, yet it is consistent that he was in great mourning, but he sustained himself with this voice: I have prayed for thee, Peter, that thy faith fail not; this spark of faith consoled him for the time being, until afterwards the resurrected Lord confirmed him more, saying: Peter, lovest thou me? Feed my sheep. There exists therefore a testimony that even the reborn can fall, and that the fallen can be converted again to God, and that they are truly received. Let this testimony be always in our sight, not only for refuting the Novatians, but also for confirming ourselves, so that we may establish that we are truly received, even if we have been polluted by many and great crimes, and let such histories admonish us concerning the promises: Grace abounds over sin. Likewise: As I live, saith the Lord, I desire not the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live.

Thirdly, let the magnitude of the fall be considered: Peter denies three times, and to the denial he knowingly adds perjury, as Mark 14 expressly says: He began to curse and to swear. Here it is usually asked what difference there is between blasphemy and this fall; although others take the distinction from the causes of the fall, because Peter was overcome by the fear of punishment and was not moved by hatred of Christ, as Judas was, yet let us judge from the result. Peter's repentance is seen, which indeed followed the fall immediately. But it is not blasphemy against the Holy Spirit when true repentance follows. And thus we ought to judge universally; although it is true that some sins are more atrocious than others, yet all are great, and far too sad for their magnitude to be comprehended by us. Furthermore, although all are great, yet let us know that the command of God is immutable, so that we do not despair, but return to God through repentance and confidence in the mediator Christ. Let the Son of God be believed to be far more powerful than the whole kingdom of sin; let us establish that those who return to God with this faith do not have the sin against the Holy Spirit.

Therefore Peter's fall was not blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, but the furies of Judas, Caiaphas, and the like, who did not return to God, were blasphemies against the Holy Spirit. Therefore, in such a temptation, the commands concerning repentance and the promises concerning faith are to be looked at more than the causes of the offense are to be subtly sought. The fall is huge, and it horribly offends God, even if it arose from the fear of the cross, not from hatred of Christ. For although it must be confessed that there are degrees of sins, yet Our lapses ought not to be minimized by us. Because all offend God horribly, and the conscience in a true struggle, when it feels the wrath of God, argues about its sins in a far different way than idle minds. How great was the sin of Adam and Eve, by which they understood that the whole human race had fallen into the eternal wrath of God, nor did they see then that example of the remission of sins, nor could they determine anything else, except that they were utterly cast off by God, like the devils, until they were raised up again, the promise of remission having been given on account of the Son of God.

The opinion which I stated must therefore be retained: that the command of God is immutable, however great sins may be, that we who are doing penance should return to God, with confidence of reconciliation on account of Christ, and that we should not despair on account of the magnitude of our lapse, but should determine that the power of the Son of God is to be preferred by far to all the sins of men. Nor let us add to the remaining lapses also blasphemy, which accuses God of lying, and denies that sins are remitted, just as Saul and Judas are condemned for this reason, because they do not believe that sin is remitted to them on account of the Son of God. And Cain is accused of this blasphemy, because he did not return to God, but added also the blasphemous utterance: My sin is greater than that I can obtain pardon.

Let this be enough to have said briefly about this passage, which is one of the chief ones in the history of the passion, and delivers a doctrine especially useful, which warns us of our infirmity, and proposes a necessary consolation, that God does not wish us to despair, however horribly we have fallen, because Christ, looking upon Peter even when he was denying Him with perjury and execration of himself, calls him back to penance, and reminds him of the sweetest voice which He had spoken: I have prayed for thee, Peter, that thy faith fail not. Let pious minds propose this voice to themselves, and know that the Son of God has prayed for individuals who, doing penance, flee to Him by faith, just as He said clearly above: I pray not for these only, but for all who shall believe, and indeed in that very discourse to Peter He commands him that, being converted, he should confirm his brethren. I have spoken about the passages which are described in this second act, in which the confession of Christ must be diligently considered, which is a testimony about the Son of God; He openly and clearly confesses Himself to be both the Messiah and the Son of God, having a divine nature, and indeed He preaches clearly about the resurrection and about divine power: Ye shall see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of majesty, and let the Pontiffs themselves, who execrate this utterance as the highest blasphemy, and judge that it is not even to be heard any longer, but pronounce sentence without hesitation as against a manifest blasphemer: He is guilty of death, understand that this very thing is said by Christ, that He is truly and by nature God. Here let it be considered what horrendous darkness there was in that assembly which is called the people of God. The chief doctors and governors are so ignorant of the promises and prophetic testimonies about Christ that they judge it to be an execrable blasphemy to say of the Messiah that He is the Son of God, just as elsewhere on account of this very utterance they judge that He is to be stoned. It is less to be wondered at, but equally horrendous, that in these last times the Church has been oppressed by such great darkness, just as the predictions are depicted in this very history, which shows that the enemies of Christ in the Church are always especially the Pontiffs, who fight for their own authority and power, with the light of the true doctrine of the Gospel about the Son of God oppressed.

Let us take the beginning of the third act from the rising of the Sun. For at night in the houses of Annas and Caiaphas, before the Pontiffs and Priests, the confession was made amidst many insults. Now in the morning Christ is led to the political magistrate, where a new crime is cast against Him, plausible before a Gentile governor, namely that this captive had been the author of seditions, and was aspiring to a kingdom. The other crime is also repeated, that this captive had made Himself the Son of God. Two crimes, therefore, the sum of all, are brought against Christ, blasphemy and sedition, of which the one overturns the first table of the decalogue, the other the second.

But let us recite briefly the chief parts of this act: for no one will be able to narrate them all even in the longest work. The first passage is an example of punishment, of betrayal, when Judas horribly condemns himself, and brings death upon himself, so that he may break off his immense torments. The second, an example of hypocrisy, that the Jews do not wish to be defiled by entry into the praetorium, while in the meantime they defile themselves with the impious counsel of killing the Messiah. The third, a double accusation, that this captive is a blasphemer and a seditious person; thus from the very beginning of the struggles of the Church, with empires and Pontiffs, the Prophets, Apostles, and the hearers of these have been burdened with these two most atrocious crimes, the thought of which torments moderate men much more harshly than all the most cruel tortures by which bodies are lacerated. The fourth, the Confession of Christ concerning both article. He confesses that he is the Son of God, and he confesses that he is a King, and he declares his kingdom, saying: My kingdom is not of this world, and thus he delivers the distinction between the kingdom of the Messiah, which is eternal, and the political kingdom, which is to cease. Fifth, Why the Jews say: It is not lawful for us to put any man to death, where the horrible misery of the human race is to be lamented, because not only the Jews, but also the Gentiles put Christ to death, so that it may be signified that all men are guilty of the death of Christ, that is, that Christ suffered for the sins of all men in the whole human race. Sixth, Herod treats Christ with insults, mocking him in the manner of the Epicureans, when nevertheless he wished to be called a king among the people of God. Seventh, The confession of Pilate, that this prisoner is innocent, and again the injustice of Pilate is described here, who, in order to dismiss the Jews appeased in some way, orders the innocent Christ to be beaten with scourges and crowned with thorns. Eighth, Pilate is overcome by fear, when the Jews threaten that they will accuse him before Caesar, because he releases an enemy of Caesar. Ninth, The condemnation of Christ made by Pilate, and the release of Barabbas. These are the principal parts of the third act, in which six hours are consumed.

On the first.

Since Judas represents the heretics of all times, likewise the deserters of the Gospel, likewise the counselors of the powerful, who by an artificial appearance alienate the minds of princes from the Gospel, or confirm them when alienated, and inflame hatreds in them, let all men fear the wrath of God in the punishment of Judas, and avoid the causes of this so horrible punishment. Arius perished with his bowels poured out, like Judas; the prefect of Julian perished with dung poured out through his mouth, and innumerable others, nor are examples lacking in our age. For many impious preachers have been suddenly extinguished in the very sermons. Let us therefore fear the judgment of God, and let us be constant in the true meaning of the Gospel, nor let us allow ourselves to be corrupted by money, or by the simulation of the benevolence of princes, or by the hope of goods, or of power, so that we may aid the furies of those who hate the Gospel.

On the fourth article, namely on the confession of Christ before a Gentile magistrate, the first charge is that he seditiously calls himself a king. Here Christ expressly confesses that he is a king, and yet he adds an interpretation: My kingdom is not of this world. Here let us learn to refute the papal imagination, and that of many political men, who think that the Church is a polity similar to a kingdom, in which it is necessary that there be some one visible head, armed with power, and with the authority of establishing laws and interpreting, of loosening and binding divine and human laws. And this head they wish to be bound to a certain place, and to the election of a certain college, as in other kingdoms. Since by nature men understand political things, they willingly transform the Church into such a human polity. But this imagination is to be refuted because of the many inconveniences that follow, because a tyrannical power is constituted under this pretext, such as the papal one was, which established many impious cults and idols: furthermore, the doctrine of the cross and spiritual promises are obscured. For eyes intent on political goods, when these are lost, think that the Church has been cast off by God.

Therefore let us hold the true and learned definition of the kingdom of the Son of God. The kingdom of Christ is the government of Christ gathering to himself the Church through the ministry of the Gospel, in all times of the world, and freeing it from sin and eternal death, and sanctifying it by the given Holy Spirit, so that it may be his eternal inheritance, and miraculously defending and ruling it in this life, so that it may truly call upon him, and acknowledge that its prayers are heard, and celebrate God, and raising it from death to life and eternal glory.

In this description it is said that Christ is not idle, as is imagined in political κακοζηλίᾳ, but is truly effective, and thus Paul often defines this kingdom, as in Ephesians 1: He gave him as head over all things to the Church, which is his body and fullness, that is, the entire body of Christ, perfecting all things in all. He openly affirms that Christ is effective in the members of the Church, the same he says afterwards: He sits at the right hand of the Father, giving gifts to men.

With this consolation, therefore, let us sustain ourselves, that the Son of God is truly present with us, helps and defends us, whether we have external protections, or are oppressed by the cross. The Son of God has not therefore cast us off, who believe in him, even if we are in the midst of torments. This consolation and invocation of the Son of God, and the true exercises of faith are greatly obscured by political imaginations.

The Church, therefore, in this life is not similar to a kingdom of the world, and yet it is a visible assembly, because it has external signs, through which its members are recognized, wherever in the world they are, namely the Gospel, the administration of the Sacraments, the confession of the Gospel, many testimonies of the Holy Spirit in invocation and in afflictions. For since God wishes Himself and His Son to be made known to all men, and to be invoked among the human race, He wishes His Church to be seen and heard. Wherefore let us not think the Church to be a Platonic idea, which can nowhere be seen, but wherever there is a gathering, truly retaining the foundation, that is, the articles of faith, and not stubbornly defending idols, there is truly the inheritance of Christ, and some members are elected to eternal glory, even if they are unlike one another, some weaker than others.

However, how great an evil it is to transform the kingdom of Christ into a political one is signified by this very image, that Christ is brought forth in purple and crowned with thorns. Nor is there any doubt that this very sad appearance was shown for this very reason, because this error was going to spread widely in the Church. The Roman Pontiff in many ways casts purple upon Christ, and crowns Him with thorns, as when he affirms that the empires of the world must be sought from the Roman see, as he wrote on the crown of Emperor Rudolph: The Rock gave to Peter, Peter the diadem to Rudolph. There are also thorns, the canons concerning the primacy and many ceremonies, which he feigns to be worship, and indeed necessary for eternal salvation. Thus also the Anabaptists sin, who bring forth laws about the Platonic sharing of goods, and about a new form of magistrates and judgments. And here and there other unlearned men often stir up tumults in cities about civil affairs, foreign to the evangelical ministry; among these, let those who are curable look upon Christ clothed in purple and crowned with thorns, and let them cease to stir up tumults about affairs foreign to the evangelical ministry, lest they themselves also fix thorns into the head of Christ, and affect Him with contumely, just as the soldiers mocking say: Hail, King of the Jews. These things, although they have been said briefly in this place concerning the distinction between the kingdom of Christ and the political, yet they must often be repeated, because the world sins in many ways in the confusion of this distinction.

Concerning the fifth.

Why the Jews say: It is not lawful for us to put any man to death, mention is not made in vain of the Jewish servitude in this place. For these words signify what kind of government this people had at that time. The Romans had granted the Jews autonomy in worship and inferior jurisdiction, but had taken away from them superior jurisdiction, that is, the trials of capital cases, as those who are moderately learned know, that in government these parts are often possessed by different people. But these things are recited for this reason, that we may learn that this history corresponds to the time of the Messiah predicted in the Prophets, who predict that Christ will come with the kingdom of Judah ceasing a little before the second dissipation of the Jewish nation, as is clearly said in Daniel. Here indeed let it also be considered how God preserves His Church in the midst of servitude, that we may learn that the Church does not remain perpetually on account of human protections. It was a testimony of the wrath of God that He had subjected the people to the Romans, whose empires were sufficiently harsh and bloody; many heirs of eternal life were cruelly put to death, and discipline was dissipated by the petulance of the soldiers. Meanwhile, however, so that doctrine and worship could remain, God willed that autonomy be granted to the Jews in inferior jurisdiction, just as now under the Turks there are Churches in many places.

Therefore, let us learn from this example that Churches are not preserved by human counsels or strengths, and when we are oppressed by servitude, let us know that it is to be tolerated as a punishment, yet not that the Church is therefore cast off by God, or is without a guardian. At that time, and before, the Parthian, Roman, and Herodian armies were wandering in Judea, and it is a wonder that in such great robberies, virgins and matrons truly worshipping God were nevertheless defended and preserved, such as Elizabeth, Anna, Mary, and countless others. Therefore, just as the pious were preserved then, and the ministry was defended, so let us know that God will preserve the Churches now also, even if they have been oppressed by servitude. And indeed the example of the Jewish nation signifies that even now in the last times there will be a harsh and sad servitude, which let us pray that God may mitigate.

Latin:

Haec cum dixisset Iesus, egressus est.

Quoties de passione filii Dei dicitur: utile est rudiores commonefieri de hac triplici meditatione passionis. Prima est paedagogica, recitare, audire, cogitare mediocri attentione historiam, et quodam studio discendi, et excitandae poenitentiae in nobis, et fidei. Haec meditatio non est aspernanda, si sit sine superstitione, imo necesse est historiam disci, ac subinde repeti, et historiae cogitatio initium est ardentium motuum spiritualium, qui Deo placent. Et sicut Ecclesia saepe proponit historiam, ita singuli homines assuefaciendi sunt, ut saepe eam legant et audiant, et omnes partes historiae diligenter distribuant, et considerent, ut fiat familiarissime nota. Nam hac ipsa cogitatione accenduntur motus spirituales in corde, iuxta illud: Fides ex auditu est, auditus per verbum Dei, nec sit frigida, nec inerudita lectio, sed cogitentur causae divini consilii, quatenus in verbo Dei patefactae sunt, ipsa historiae series, effectus, applicatio, et tota Ecclesiae gubernatio inde usque a principio.

Sunt enim causae passionis Christi, obiectum quod movit voluntatem filii Dei, peccatum et tristissima damnatio generis humani, quod noluit prorsus perire filius Dei.

Impulsiva causa, Patris amor, et Filii intercessio deprecantis pro nobis, de hac causa inquit filius: Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut filium suum unigenitum dederit pro mundo. Finalis causa, ut magnae parti generis hu- mani iusticia et gloria aeterna redderetur, et Deus haberet aeternam Ecclesiam, a qua agnosceretur et celebraretur, ut Psalm. 22. dicitur: Apud te laus mea, in Ecclesia magna confitebor tibi, vota mea reddam in conspectu timentium Deum.

Causa efficiens propter bonum finem, volun- tas filii Dei et persona eius, volens hanc obedien- tiam, propter arcanum consilium aeterni patris, cuius ira non poterat alia hostia placari. Hac voluntate Christus ipse est sacerdos, sese offerens aeterno patri pro nobis.

Materia vero passionis, in qua, id est, sub- iectum, est ipse filius Dei, et distribuantur prae- cipuae partes, quae dolorem senserunt, nervi corporis senserunt cruciatus, quos afferebat lace- ratio, cor fugiebat mortem, et pars cruciatuum corporis penetrabat ad cor, sed maiores cruciatus erant animae, qui etiam cor et totum corpus lan- guefaciebant. Nam anima naturali inclinatione abhorrebat a morte, et ut in aliis fortibus viris, semper magis causa aerumnarum excruciantur animi, quam ipsis aerumnis, sicut Davidem multo magis cogitatio culpae exercebat, quam ipsius exilii miseria. Ita in Christi anima causa passio- nis ingentes dolores ciebat, scilicet, quod sciebat Christus Deum irasci peccatis generis humani, et in se derivatam esse iram, ac si ipse se tantis sce- leribus polluisset. Hunc arcanum et inenarrabi- lem dolorem ex causa passionis ortum, non in- telligunt homines. Hic anima Christi luctata est, non solum cum cruciatibus corporis et cum morte, sed multo magis cum ira Dei, doluit filius Dei horribiliter offensum esse Deum et contumelia affectum, et agnovit in se derivatam iram esse, doluit et magnam partem generis humani non in- tellecto aut spreto hoc beneficio Dei, scilicet morte filii Dei, ruere in aeternum exitium. Sed hos dolores vicit haec consolatio, quod volens obediit patri, et expectavit auxilium Dei et liberationem, ut suo loco in historia dicetur, et supra diximus quaedam de Christi doloribus et lucta.

Causa instrumentalis et externa, non con- gruens cum fine, quem Deus constituerat, sunt diaboli et Iudaei, ac eorum satellites, qui arden- tes furore et odio Dei, et omnium Prophetarum, etiam Christum delere conati sunt.

Effectus, placatio irae Dei, ut iusticiae Dei satisfieret. Non enim temere abiecta est ira, sed voluit Deus reddi λύτρον, quia omnis lex obligat aut ad obedientiam, aut ad poenam. Deinde se- quuntur alii multi effectus, reconciliatio Dei et hominum, donatio iusticiae, Spiritus sancti et vitae aeternae, destructio operum diaboli, pec- cati et mortis.

Applicatio continet doctrinam poenitentiae et fidei. Primum vera et horribilis ira Dei ad- versus peccata nostra cogitetur. Cum enim vo- luerit filium fieri victimam pro genere humano, constat ingentem et non simulatam iram esse. Multa sunt tristissima testimonia irae Dei adver- sus peccata, ut mors et infinitae aliae calamitates hominum. Sed hoc testimonium longe superat omnia, quod in illo arcano consilio divino de- cretum est, ut filius Dei fieret victima.

Applicatio est igitur passionis, primum vere expavescere agnitione irae Dei adversus nostra peccata, sicut ipse dicit, Luc. 23.: Ne ploretis super me, sed plorate super vos et filios vestros. Deinde accedat et altera applicatio fidei, quae sta- tuat mandatum aeternum Dei et immutabile esse, ut credamus propter nos filium Dei factum esse victimam, et nos recipi a Deo, cum credimus no- bis remitti peccata propter ipsum. Hac fide in- coatur vita aeterna in cordibus, quia haec con- solatio liberat ea a pavoribus, et novam lucem ac vitam incoat.

Ad paedagogicam meditationem deinde et haec doctrina pertinet, quod videlicet applicatio- nem nostram sequi debeant gratiarum actio, prae- dicatio, confessio, imitatio in cruce. Huc ad- iungatur et doctrina de sacerdotio Christi, de quo scriptum est: Tu es sacerdos in aeternum secun- dum ordinem Melchisedech. Christus enim vere est summus sacerdos, cui haec definitio convenit. Sacerdos est persona, quae promissionem divi- nam habet, ut certo statuere possit se exaudiri, vocata mandato divino, ut doceat Evangelium, et oret, ac sacrificet pro aliis. Haec propriissime et primum competunt filio Dei, qui promissionem habet, qua certo scit se exaudiri, iuxta illud: Hic est filius meus dilectus, quo delector, et 1. Ti- moth. 2.: Unus mediator Dei, et hominum homo Christus Iesus. Et hic filius protulit arcanum decretum de reconciliatione ex sinu aeterni patris, ut Ioan, 1. dicitur: Unigenitus filius, qui est in sinu patris, ipse enarravit, et Ioan. 17.: Ego tradidi eis sermonem tuum. Quod autem oret pro nobis, verba aperte testantur, Ioan. 17.: Non pro eis tantum oro, sed pro omnibus, qui credent per verbum eorum in me, et Esa. cap. 53. scriptum est: Ipse peccata multorum tulit, et pro trans- gressoribus rogavit. Postremo et sacrificium pro nobis obtulit, suam mortem, et quidem id sacri- ficium pro nobis applicavit, sicut expresse inquit, Ioan. 17.: Pro eis ego sanctifico me, ut et ipsi sint sanctificati in veritate, et Matth. 20.: Filius hominis venit dare animam suam λύτρον pro omnibus. Haec autem applicatio fide apprehen- denda est, ut supra dixi, et Act. 10. scribitur: Huic omnes Prophetae testimonium perhibent, remissionem peccatorum accipere per nomen eius, omnes qui credunt in eum. Hoc dictum postu- lat, ut fide accipiamus beneficium Christi, id est, statuamus vere nobis donari remissionem, pro- pter huius mediatoris sacrificium et intercessio- nem. Huius totius doctrinae cogitatio est pae- dagogia quaedam, sed tamen non aspernanda, si fit sine superstitione. Nam per has cogitatio- nes accenduntur motus spirituales.

Est igitur secunda meditatio, quae proprie vocatur spiritualis, et est salutaris, vere expa- vescere corda cognitione irae Dei adversus nostra peccata, et hanc iram cernere in filium Dei effu- sam, sicut Paulus inquit ad Rom. 8., oportere nos fieri similes imaginis filii Dei. Et ad Rom. 6.: Insiti sumus similitudini mortis eius. Item: Ve- tus noster homo simul crucifixus est, ut aboleatur corpus peccati. Nec tamen maneant tantum pa- vores, sed accedere consolationem et vivificatio- nem oportet. Ergo in hac spirituali meditatione etiam nova lux et gaudium sentiatur, cum fides statuit iram Dei placatam esse per filium, et pro- pter filium nobis remitti peccata, et nobis reddi iusticiam et vitam, sicut scriptum est ad Rom. 6.: Sic oportet nos inseri similitudini resurrectionis Christi. Corinth. 2.: Per quem et simul resusci- tati estis per fidem, efficaciae Dei. Et ad Phi- lip. 3.: Ut inveniar in eo, non habens meam iu- sticiam, quae est ex lege, sed eam quae est per fidem Christi, quae est iusticia ex Deo per fidem, ut agnoscam eum, et potentiam resurrectionis eius, et societatem passionum eius.

Haec secunda meditatio diligenter discer- nenda est a tertia, quae est exemplaris, secunda apprehendit Christum propiciatorem et salvato- rem, et pretium et causam nostrae reconciliatio- nis, iusticiae et vitae aeternae, sed tertia, quae est exemplaris, intuetur Christum ut doctorem, cuius exemplis nos consolemur, et quem imitari studeamus, ut Davidis exempla nobis proponi- mus. Videmus Christum, Abel, Davidem, et alias sanctos, horribiles aerumnas sustinuisse. Sciamus ergo voluntatem Dei esse, ut Ecclesia sit subiecta cruci, nec nos abiectos esse, etiamsi dura patimur, imitemur et invocationem, quam illi in cruce exercuerunt, tolerantiam, spem, et alias virtutes. Haec exemplaris meditatio pia est, si non desit secunda. Neque enim recte agnoscit Christum, qui eum tantum putat doctorem fuisse, ut Mosen, aut tantum exempla ab eo petenda esse, ut a Davide, aut similibus.

Sed recte instituti in Evangelio, et intelli- gentes secundam meditationem, inde dulcissimam consolationem, et utiles admonitiones sumere pos- sunt. Nam in hac ipsa historia passionis Christi imagines proponuntur pene omnium, quae acci- dunt Ecclesiae. Personae sunt hic, sancti, firmi et infirmi, hostium multa genera, hypocritae, tyranni, sacerdotes, principes, vulgus, pericula varia, manifesta violentia, insidiae occultae, pro- ditio, amicorum fugae, σαρκασμοὶ in calamitate. Econtra vero pugnae, consolationes et liberationes mirandae sanctorum, et tristissimae poenae im- piorum, ut Iudae. Denique haec historia quasi prophetia est, significans Ecclesiae omnium tem- porum similes calamitates, consolationes, et libe- rationes. Horum exemplorum consideratio pios erudire, et confirmare et consolari potest.

Historia.

Distribuam autem historiam in aliquot actus, et ut lectio sit magis perspicua, initio tempora annotabo. Certum est Christum crucifixum esse, 8. Calend. April. hoc est, die 25. Martii, ut nunc est usitata mensium ratio, anno Tyberii 18. fue- ratque iam Christus ingressus annum 34. Et quanquam dierum praecedentium ratio non certo constitui potest, tamen haec mediocris distributio aliquid lucis affert historiae.

Die 14. Martii videtur ingressus iter ex de- serto, ubi Iohannes baptizaverat, unde a Iordane ad Iericho spatium est duorum miliarium germa- nicorum, in quo itinere caecum sanavit. Die 15. mansit apud Zachaeum. Die 16. iter fecit a Ieri- cho ac Bethaniam. Nam Iericho distat a Ierusa- lem paulo plus quatuor nostris miliaribus.

Die 17. Martii Lazarus excitatur ante diem Palmarum. Die 18. fortassis mansit in Bethania.

Die 19. coena cum Lazaro in Bethania in sab- bato. Die 20. dies Palmarum. Die 21. ma- ledixit ficui, et in templo acerrimas conciones ha- buit, quae in Matthaeo extant. Die 22. coena in Bethania in domo Simonis leprosi. Die 23. pactio Iudae. Die 24. dies azymorum, esus agni, et institutio coenae Dominicae. Fuitque verus paschatis Mosaici dies a vespere eius diei, ad postridianum iuxta rationem Mosaicam. Quare Christus et legitimo die comedit agnum, et vero paschatis die crucifixus est. Die 25. crucifixio. Die 26. fuit in sepulcro. Die 27. resurrectio.

Ex hac tabella animadverti potest, quo die Christus agnum comederit, et deinde agonem ad montem Oliveti incoaverit, mons olivarum vici- nus erat Ierosolymae in ea parte, qua urbs spe- ctabat orientem, ac saepe celebratur, ut 2. Reg. 15. in fuga Davidis. Et quanquam de nomine Cedron disputant, tamen consentaneum est ean- dem appellationem esse, quae est in eadem histo- ria Davidis. Exit igitur Christus eadem via, qua David olim oppressus ingenti dolore et luctu fu- gerat, exutus iam non solum regno, sed illa ex- cellenti virtutis gloria, quam habuerat: sed multo tristius est iter Christi, qui ad longe difficilius certamen egreditur.

Sit igitur primus actus, lucta, et res gestae in horto, quae narrantur ab aliis Evangelistis co- piosius. Matthaeus orditur eam narrationem a pavoribus: Coepit Iesus dolere, et vehementer angi animo, et Christus inquit: Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem, inter hos dolores preca- tur, et tanta est lucta, ut cruentus sudor erum- pat, mittitur et angelus ad eum confirmandum. Haec cum legunt homines profani, mirantur, cur tanta moestitia in viro forti extiterit, cum Socra- tes, imo interdum etiam puellae, ut Herculis filia apud Euripidem, dicantur maiori animi tranquil- litate mortem adiisse et sustinuisse, sed Eccle- sia cogitet causas, et discrimen mortis Christi, et aliorum hominum. Commune est hoc omnibus hominibus, cum mens praevidet mortem, ut ani- ma et cor expavescant cruciatus et mortem. Quia natura universaliter fugit destructionem sui, ac servari et incolumis manere cupit. Sic et Socra- tes et Cicero vere dolent, quanquam aliqua mo- deratione regunt gestus externos, tamen inclusus est in anima et in corde dolor, qui nullius ora- tione satis describi potest. Et in hac naturae de- pravatione non solum naturalis quaedam est in Cicerone fuga mortis, sed etiam accedunt vitiosi affectus, succenset Deo, miratur, cur haec prae- stans natura tantis malis onerata sit, aegre amit- tit vitae voluptates. Ita in aliis alii accedunt in- ordinati motus. At in Christo, etsi est natura- lis fuga mortis et dolor, tamen haec non sunt in- ordinata. Postea vero sunt dolores horrendi, quorum magnitudinem nec homines, nec angeli ulli possunt eloqui. Scit Christus Deum vere et horribiliter irasci peccatis, et hanc iram in se de- rivatam esse. Iacet igitur prostratus coram Deo, dolens se reum esse, ac si contaminasset sese horribili turpitudine, qua turpissimi cultores idolorum, homicidae, polluti libidinibus toto orbe terrarum se contaminarunt. Pro his pecca- tis nostris deprecator est, et luctatur cum ira Dei, ut semper partem irae deprecator in sese derivat, qui videtur malos sublevare, et minus irasci tur- pitudini, quam deberet, sicut Ioab vituperatur patrocinans Absoloni, sed hic dolor et lucta filii Dei, longe superat omnes omnium angelorum et hominum cogitationes.

Accesserunt et aliae causae tristissimi luctus, quod videlicet vidit suam gentem interituram esse, item quod vidit maximam partem generis humani ingratam fore pro hoc beneficio, tantae multitu- dinis aeternum interitum etiam vidit, et ingenti moesticia deploravit. Haec consideremus, cum hoc dictum legimus. Coepit dolere et angi animo, et singuli nostra peccata sciamus in Christum translata esse et auxisse eius dolores.

Supra autem respondimus ad obiectiones, quae breviter hic repetenda sunt. Prima est, in multis aliis viris et puellis non fuit tantus dolor in aditu mortis, quantus in Christo. Cur igitur ipse, cum habeat summam virtutum perfectio- nem, adeo expavescit? Respondeo: Nulla crea- tura potest sustinere magnitudinem irae Dei, tu- lit igitur filius Dei poenam, ne caeteri ferrent, ideo in Laurentio et aliis maior alacritas cernitur, quia causae praecipuae doloris in eis non sunt ta- les, ut in Christo. Beati quorum tecta sunt pec- cata, inquit Psalmus. Est igitur alacrior Lau- rentius, quia cum ira Dei derivata sit in Chri- stum, Laurentio parcitur, ne eam cernat. Chri- stus luctatus est et fuit λύτρον, ut nobis parcatur, quare Psalmus dicit: Si iniquitates observaveris Domine, Domine quis sustinebit.

Secunda obiectio: Non obtemperare omni- bus viribus Deo, est peccatum, in Christo est ali- qua fuga mortis: Quomodo igitur dicitur obe- dientia integra in eo fuisse sine peccato. Respon- deo breviter: Etsi haec lucta describi verbis non potest, tamen hoc retinendum est, quod dicitur ad Heb. 4., Christum tentatum esse secundum omnia, secundum similitudinem, sine peccato. Ac primum laceratio corporis ac nervorum late- raliter affert dolorem sine peccato. Est et in corde et voluntate naturalis moestitia fugiens mortem, quae in Christo sine vitio fuit, quia omnis natura onerata supra vires gemit, et expa- vescit magnitudinem oneris. Doluit Cicero, sed inordinate, dubitans an sit providentia, aut si esse providentiam cogitabat, irascens Deo, quod causa iustior vinceretur. Talis confusio dubita- tionum et blasphemiarum non fuit in Christo. Praeterea etiamsi alius in Christo maior dolor est, ut dixi, sensus irae Dei, tamen hic est sine in- dignatione et blasphemia adversus Deum, subiicit se Christus voluntati patris vera reverentia, sicut ad Heb. dicitur: Propter reverentiam exauditus est, id est, propter obedientiam non simulatam, sed a vera reverentia ortam, qua se filius aeterno patri volens ingenti amore generis humani subie- cit. Huius tanti amoris cogitatio utinam in nobis aliquantulum accenderetur. Assumsit genus hu- manum filius, et se vocat fratrem nostrum, et fraterno amore vere ardet. Nihil enim simula- tum aut ficticium est in Christo, et hoc tanto amore movetur, ut sese subiiciat horrendis poe- nis, et irae Dei pro nobis. Exuscitemus igitur nos huius amoris cogitatione, ut fiducia miseri- cordiae ipsius erga nos accendatur, et nos quo- que sensu aliquo gratitudinis moveamur, ut magis studeamus Deo obedire.

Tertia obiectio: Pugnantia non possunt in eodem esse. Cum autem Christus semper fuerit beatus, fuisse eum in excellenti laetitia sequitur. Quomodo igitur simul est tanta consternatio? Respondeo: Etsi alii discernunt partes seu poten- tias in Christo, et aliis tribuunt laetitiam, aliis dolorem, tamen simplicior responsio est, tem- pora discernere. Hoc fuit tempus, in quo beati- tudo seu gloria non fulsit in filio, ut alias. Nunc enim quiescente natura divina, et non exserente suam potentiam, iacet humiliatus, et ut tristissi- ma voce dicitur apud Esa: Percussus a Deo. His tribus argumentis consideratis, piae mentes de lucta Christi cogitantes, aliquo modo commone- fiunt, quae fuerint illius doloris causae. Et sin- guli in magnis doloribus propriis istam luctam intueantur. Quod cum faciemus, non solum ma- gis intelligi consternatio Christi poterit, sed etiam consolationem ab ipsius exemplo et victoria su- memus, tulit filius Dei tam horrendos cruciatus, feramus nos quoque. Sustinens autem pro nobis interpellavit, et nobis impetravit mitigationem et liberationem, sicut dicit: O mors, ero mors tua. Hac fide nos in nostris consternationibus eriga- mus, haec experientia illustrabit hanc doctrinam.

Iam ordine personas in primo actu conside- remus. Christus sentit cruciatus ingentes, cum his luctatur, et precationibus se sustentat, et consolationem experitur, nam et angelus ad eum confirmandum mittitur. In hac lucta vere fit vi- ctima, seu agnus Dei sustinens nostra peccata. Tunc enim ira Dei in eum effunditur, ac tale qui- dem caput est Ecclesiae. Quid interim Ecclesia ait? Apostoli nec magnitudinem dolorum Christi intelligunt, nec valde anguntur animis, imo etiam somno vincuntur. At Christus obiurgat eos, quod non sint magis vigilantes et intenti, ac praecipit, ut orent Deum, ne opprimantur tenta- tione. Haec particula universaliter pingit securi- tatem et negligentiam magnae partis in Ecclesia, nondum sentientis aerumnas, etiam cum alii con- flictantur ingentibus miseriis. Hic monet Chri- stus, ut sciamus commune periculum esse, et pe- tamus nos iuvari, regi, confirmari, ne aut secu- rae mentes ruant in Epicureum comtemtum, aut oppressae mole calamitatum evertantur despera- tione, ut Eli, Saul, alii innumerabiles. Semper tamen aliqui sunt in Ecclesia, qui vere agnoscunt voluntatem Dei de peccato et de mediatore Chri- sto, et intelligunt dolores Christi, et sentiunt aliquo modo similes dolores, et expectant libera- tionem, ut inde usque ab initio recitantur tristis- simi luctus Adae, Noae, Abrahae, Mosi, Davi- dis, etc. Ipso tempore passionis Maria intellexit cur pateretur filius, et socia fuit dolorum, et con- stanti fide expectavit liberationem.

Econtra personae inferentes bellum Christo, quae sunt principales causae certaminum, sunt diaboli, impii sacerdotes et eorum doctores, et ex ipso coetu Christi proditores: deinde politici magistratus, et maxima pars populi, et alii alias habent causas. Diaboli ardent simpliciter odio

Dei et Christi, et ut Deo aegre faciant, in omnia membra Ecclesiae atrocissime saeviunt: Impii sa- cerdotes et doctores adversantur Evangelio, quia taxat falsas opiniones et commenticios cultus. Oderunt autem plerique homines reprehensio- nem, vel naturali superbia, quia nos amamus et nobis placemus, vel metuentes potentiae et quae- stui. In proditoribus ut Doëg, Alcimo, Iuda concurrunt multae causae, odium diabolicum, cupiditas vindictae, spes potentiae et lucri. Po- litici magistratus metuunt mutationes regnorum, et qui ab impiis sacerdotibus magna commoda ha- bent, cum eis colludunt, multi etiam palam sunt Epicurei.

Tales etiam causae incendunt populum, Epicureus comtemtus Dei, superstitio, spes otii, lucri, benevolentiae potentum. Has et similes causas, quae irritant mentes adversus Christum, prodest considerare, ut adversus eas, animi im- becilles muniantur, et mali acrius refutari et ob- iurgari possint.

Adhuc narramus primi actus historiam in horto, ac diximus de lucta et precatione Christi, et de personis. Reliqua historia haec continet in eo loco. Apostolorum obiurgationem, de qua dictum est, et adhortationem ad precandum, quam diligenter nobis proponamus: Vigilate et orate, inquit, ne intretis in tentationem. Dolen- dum est sapientiam humanam plerunque in omni- bus hominibus imaginari, nostra diligentia posse vitari laqueos diaboli, et graves lapsus. At di- ctum Ieremiae nobis sit in conspectu: Scio Do- mine, quod non est hominis via eius. Nihil fa- cilius est homini, quam hallucinari, decipi, et errare. Ideo hoc dictum Christi saepe cogitemus, praecipit utrumque, vigilantiam et precationem, vult nos Christus esse intentos et circumspectos. Quia vero precari iubet, significat nostra circum- spectione non posse omnes lapsus caveri, sed opus esse divina gubernatione, et magnam conso- lationem nobis propositam esse sciamus, quoties praecipitur precatio. Sequitur enim precationem non esse inanem, ut omnes Epicurei cogitant, non enim frustra praecipitur. Hac consolatione confirmati, simus ardentiores in precando, et petamus regi a Deo mentes nostras, pericula, et exitus periculorum.

Deinde in eodem loco sequitur osculum pro- ditoris, quod significat simulatione amicitiae mul- tos insidiari doctoribus Evangelii, et praecipua pars huius actus est prehensio Christi, in qua ipsa consideretur potentia divina, ut agnoscamus Christum pati non coactum humana potentia, sed volentem, sicut in Esaia scriptum est: Oblatus est, quia voluit. Cadunt enim milites prostrati una voce Christi. Ad hunc actum pertinet et pugna Petri, in qua iterum consideretur error Apostolorum, qui adhuc somniabant imperium mundanum. Estque hic edita insignis vox, quae testatur Apo- stolos non gerere gladium, id est, ministerium Evangelii non esse potestatem gladii, ut vocant. Docet item ordinationem Dei esse, ut puniantur gladio omnes, qui sine legibus et contra vocatio- nem gladio utuntur. Cum enim dicitur: Omnis qui acceperit gladium, gladio peribit, intelligan- tur accipere gladium hi, qui potestatem gladii non datum a legibus aut magistratibus exercere conantur, ut faciunt omnes, qui iniusta homici- dia committunt, et omnes seditiosi. Est autem Christi dictum sumtum ex cap. 9. Genesis: Qui- cunque fuderit humanum sanguinem, per homi- nem fundetur et sanguis ipsius. Nec sine gravi causa haec lex repetita est in hoc ipso extremo agone Christi, fortassis ut mo- neatur tota posteritas, ne praetextu Evangelii ra- piat imperia, sicut Romani Pontifices fecerunt, et Anabaptistae, et saepe alii imperia quaesive- runt nulla legitima causa, sed tantum praetextu Evangelii. Simus igitur cauti, ne seditiosa con- silia adiuvemus. Significationes etiam sunt in ipso facto, Pe- trus dextram auriculam praecidit servo Pontificis. Ambitiosi doctores praecidunt auriculam, id est, offundunt dextrae auriculae falsas interpretatio- nes, quibus confirmant seditiosa consilia, ut cum Romani Pontifices moverunt bella contra Germa- nicos Imperatores Henricos, finxerunt se liberta- tem suffragationis in eligendis Episcopis defen- dere, species fuit honesta, sed tamen non fuit iusta bellorum inferendorum causa. Postrema pars actus huius in horto, est fuga omnium Apostolorum, quae est exemplum com- munis infirmitatis hominum. Hactenus de primo actu breviter dictum est: In quo valde multae partes sunt, quarum exhauriri doctrina non po- test, videlicet ipse pavor et dolor Christi, con- firmatio Christi, proditio Iudae, testimonium po- tentiae divinae in Christo, prosternante cohortem una voce, prohibitio pugnae, sanatio vulnerati, imbecillitas Apostolorum.

Secundus actus sit confessio Christi, primum in domo Hannae, deinde in domo Caiphae, et accusationes, contumeliae et condemnationes, et Petri negatio ac poenitentia. Praecipua est autem quaestio, et an sit Messias, et an sit filius Dei Christus, plane respondet, et utrumque asseve- rat: Sum Messias, et sum filius Dei. Existimo autem ipsis fuisse distinctas quaestiones: quia Pharisaei non sentiebant Messiam natura filium Dei esse, maximeque fremunt audita hac confes- sione, eamque vociferantur blasphemam esse, et audacter ferunt sententiam, reus est mortis, ac statim addunt multas contumelias.

Primum autem hic observentur responsiones Christi, cum de doctrina interrogat summus sa- cerdos, taxatur a Christo, et remittitur ad audi- tores: Cur, inquit, me interrogas? Interroga eos, qui me audierunt. Haec verba non sunt tergiver- santis aut defugientis confessionem, sed servat discrimen Christus inter manifestorum criminum condemnationem, et inquisitionem non manife- storum. De manifestis non interrogandum est. quid fateatur reus, aut non fateatur. Sed crimen diserte obiiciendum est, et vera testium autoritate confirmandum, praesertim de doctrina expresse ostendatur, quam sententiam impiam sparserit aliquis. Econtra vero in inquisitione arcanorum, primum praecedat fraterna admonitio, si suspicio praebuit occasionem. Deinde fiat inquisitio, si confirmantur suspiciones, nec dubium est hunc ipsum ordinem fori usitatum fuisse in synagoga, quia et Christus hanc formam sequitur, Matth. 18. Iuste igitur Christus reprehendit Pontificem, quod in causa manifesta non servet ordinem, aut si nondum manifesta est causa, non fuit iustum capere reum armata cohorte. Primum igitur lector hic consideret ordinem iudicii, et discernat causarum manifestarum condemnationem, ab in- quisitione arcanarum, in qua fraternam admoni- tionem praecedere necesse est.

Ac intellexit sacerdotis minister reprehendi interrogationem, ideo dat colaphos Christo, in- quiens: Sic respondes Pontifici? Hunc quoque refutat Christus, et hinc disputant rudes de tole- rantia, et allegant dictum Christi: Si quis per- cusserit te in dextram genam, obverte ei et alte- ram. Hoc inquiunt non observat Christus, quia non tacet, sed expostulat et litigat cum servo, hanc cavillationem propter rudiores diluam. Utrumque praeceptum est, causam veram, praesertim doctrinae, confessione perspicua defendere, et simul animo paratum esse ad violentiam perferendam. Ita hoc loco Christus affirmat, se recte respondisse, aut si non recte respondi, inquit: Ostende causam, tu vero iniustam in me saevitiam exerces, hoc igitur exemplum meminisse prodest. Non est tolerantia tacere, et adversarii falsam et iniustam causam silentio confirmare. Imo, praesertim doctrinae confessionem oportet perspicuam esse, ut scriptum est: Qui confessus fuerit me coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram patre coelesti. Deinde ubi de causa dixisti, quantum dici necesse est, mens sit parata ad tolerandas corporis lacerationes, quaecunque impendent, ut hic Christus sustinet varias contumelias et cruciatus. Nec dictum illud: Si quis percusserit te in dextram genam, intelligatur superstitiose de silentio, aut ipso gestu obvertendi alteram maxillam. Quia Petrus inquit: Patientes ubi opus est, id est, cum hostium furor in nos irruit, cor praestet tolerantiam, quae quid sit, alias saepe dicitur: Nos non iubemus hostes in nos saevire. Hanc regulam in multis vitae negotiis scire et sequi utile est. Si famam tuam laedit aliquis, non necesse est te tacere, sed modeste excuses te, et refutes adversarium, si ille non cedit refutatus, nec defendunt te iudices, ut debebant. Christus suo dicto et exemplo consolatur te, ut scias cur tolerantia praestanda sit, et quomodo placeat Deo.

Post Christi expostulationem cum ministro, describitur Petri lapsus. In hac historia multiplex doctrina continetur. Primum commonefactio proponitur de nostra infirmitate. Secundo exemplum poenitentiae traditur, et testimonium de recipiendis iis, qui lapsi sunt. Tertio discrimen hic considerandum est inter negationem Petri, et blasphemias.

Primo de infirmitate nostra.

Certum est Petrum sanctificatum Spiritu sancto, sicut Matth. 16. ad eum dicitur: Beatus es Simon Bar Iona, quia caro et sanguis non revelavit tibi, sed pater meus, qui in coelis est, et fuerat confirmata eius fides, spectata resuscitatione mortuorum, Lazari et aliorum, fecerat et ipse miracula. Ideo fuit in Petro bonum propo- situm, ut haec verba testantur, Lucae 22: Para- tus sum tecum in mortem ire. Videbatur ergo in Petro mediocre robur fidei esse, et tamen exiguis terriculamentis ancillae et servorum perturbatus, abiicit confessionem. Talis erat David donatus Spiritu sancto, et confirmatus multis suis et alie- nis miraculis. Imo spectator etiam fuerat tristis- simi exitus Saulis, quod exemplum proposuit Deus secuturis regibus, ut magis timerent Deum. Et tamen vincitur David flammis adulterii, et cu- mulat statim magna peccata. His exemplis infir- mitatis commonefacti, emendemus securitatem nostram, et deponamus fiduciam nostri, disca- mus timere Deum, et petere auxilium et guber- nationem divinam. Teneamus in promtu et dicta de hac doctri- na, Ioann. 15.: Sine me nihil potestis facere. Matth. 16.: Vigilate et orate, ne intretis in ten- tationem: Spiritus quidem promtus est, caro au- tem infirma. 1. Petr. ult.: Vigilate, quia adver- sarius vester diabolus, tanquam leo rugiens cir- cumit, quaerens quem devoret. 2. Cor. 10.: Qui videtur stare, videat ne cadat. Matth. 12.: Veniens invenit domum otiosam, et assumit se- cum alios septem spiritus deteriores, et fiunt no- vissima hominis illius deteriora prioribus. Ad Phil. 2.: Cum timore et tremore vestram salu- tem operamini. 2. Cor. 3.: Non sumus sufficien- tes ex nobis cogitare aliquid, tanquam ex nobis. His et similibus dictis excitemus nos ad agnitionem nostrae infirmitatis, ad timorem Dei, ad petitio- nem auxilii, sicut totus Psalm. 119. talis doctrina et precatio est: Fac cum servo tuo secundum mi- sericordiam tuam, et iustificationes tuas doce me. Item: Gressus meos dirige secundum eloquium tuum, et non dominetur mei omnis iniusticia. Secundo consideremus exemplum poeniten- tiae. Apud Lucam cap. 22. haec verba legun- tur: Et statim, loquente eo, gallus cantavit, et conversus Dominus intuitus est Petrum, et recor- datus est Petrus sermonis Domini, et egressus fo- ras, flevit amare. In his verbis describuntur con- tritio et causa contritionis. Amarae lacrymae significant dolorem in corde Petri agnoscentis tri- stem et magnum lapsum. Causa vero contritionis movens cor Petri fuit, quod Christum eum intui- tus, accendit agnitionem huius tanti lapsus et dolorem. Ita fit contritio movente corda Spiritu sancto per verbum Dei.

Etsi autem non scribitur, ubi fuerit hoc bi- duo Petrus, quid egerit, tamen consentaneum est, eum fuisse in magno luctu, sustentavit autem se hac voce: Rogavi pro te Petre, ne deficiat fides tua, haec scintilla fidei eum tantisper consolata est, donec postea resuscitatus Dominus magis confirmavit eum, inquiens: Petre diligis me? Pasce oves meas. Extat igitur testimonium, quod et labi possint renati, et lapsi rursus ad Deum converti, et quod vere recipiantur. Hoc testi- monium nobis semper in conspectu sit, non so- lum ad refutandos Novatianos, sed etiam ad nos ipsos confirmandos, ut statuamus vere nos recipi, etiamsi multis et magnis sceleribus polluti sumus, et admoneant nos tales historiae de promissioni- bus: Exuberat gratia supra delictum. Item: Vivo ego, dicit Dominus, nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur et vivat.

Tertio consideretur magnitudo lapsus: Pe- trus ter negat, et negationi sciens addit periurium, ut Marc. 14. expresse dicitur: Coepit execrari se et iurare. Hic quaeri solet quid intersit inter blasphemiam, et hunc lapsum, etsi alii a causis lapsus sumunt discrimen, quia metu supplicii su- peratus sit Petrus, et non odio Christi motus sit, ut Iudas, tamen nos iudicemus a posteriore. Cer- nitur Petri poenitentia, quae quidem mox secuta est lapsum. Non est autem blasphemia adversus Spiritum sanctum, quando sequitur vera poeni- tentia. Et ita nos universaliter iudicare debemus, etsi verum est alia peccata aliis atrociora esse, ta- men omnia magna sunt, et longe tristiora, quam ut a nobis comprehendi eorum magnitudo possit. Deinde etsi omnia sunt magna, tamen sciamus mandatum Dei immutabile esse, ut non despere- mus, sed redeamus ad Deum per poenitentiam, et fiduciam mediatoris Christi. Filius Dei longe potentior esse toto regno peccati credatur, qui hac fide redeunt ad Deum, hos statuamus non habere peccatum in Spiritum sanctum.

Non igitur fuit Petri lapsus blasphemia ad- versus Spiritum sanctum, sed Iudae, Caiphae, et similium furores, qui non redierunt ad Deum, fuerunt blasphemiae adversus Spiritum sanctum. Magis igitur in tali tentatione intuenda sunt man- data de poenitentia, et promissiones de fide, quam subtiliter quaerendae causae delicti. Lapsus in- gens est, et horribiliter offendit Deum, etiamsi ex metu crucis, non ex odio Christi ortus est. Etsi enim fatendum est esse gradus peccatorum, tamen non debent a nobis extenuari nostri lapsus. Quia omnes horribiliter offendunt Deum, et conscien- tia in vero agone, cum sentit iram Dei, longe ali- ter disputat de suis peccatis, quam otiosae men- tes. Quantum fuit Adae et Evae peccatum, quo intelligebant totum humanum genus incidisse in aeternam iram Dei, nec tum videbant illum exem- plum remissionis peccatorum, nec poterant aliud statuere, nisi se prorsus esse abiectos a Deo, sicut diabolos, donec rursus erecti sunt, data promis- sione remissionis propter filium Dei.

Retinenda est igitur sententia, quam dixi: Immutabile mandatum Dei esse, quantumvis ma- gna sunt peccata, ut agentes poenitentiam redea- mus ad Deum, fiducia reconciliationis propter Christum, nec propter magnitudinem nostri lap- sus desperemus, sed statuamus longe anteferen- dam esse potentiam filii Dei omnibus hominum peccatis. Nec ad reliquos lapsus addamus etiam blasphemiam, quae accusat Deum mendacii, et negat remitti peccata, sicut Saul et Iudas ideo damnantur, quia non credunt sibi propter filium Dei peccatum remitti. Et Cain accusatur huius blasphemiae, quod non redierit ad Deum, sed addiderit etiam blasphemam vocem: Maius est peccatum meum, quam ut veniam assequi possim.

Haec breviter satis sit dixisse de hoc loco, qui ex praecipuis unus est in historia passionis, et doctrinam inprimis utilem tradit, quae nos admo- net de nostra infirmitate, et consolationem neces- sariam proponit, quod Deus non velit desperare, quantumvis horribiliter lapsos, quia Petrum etiam cum periurio et execratione sui negantem, Chri- stus respiciens, revocat ad poenitentiam, et ad- monet eum dulcissimae vocis, quam dixerat: Ego rogavi pro te Petre, ne deficiat fides tua. Hanc vocem sibi proponant piae mentes, ac sciant filium Dei pro singulis precatum esse, qui agentes poe- nitentiam, fide confugiunt ad ipsum, sicut supra clare dixit: Non pro his tantum rogo, sed pro omnibus credituris, et quidem in ipso sermone ad Petrum mandat ei, ut conversus, confirmet fra- tres. Dixi de locis, qui in hoc secundo actu de- scripti sunt, in quo diligenter consideranda est confessio Christi, quae est testimonium de filio Dei, palam et diserte fatetur se esse et Messiam, et filium Dei, habentem divinam naturam, et qui- dem de resurrectione, et de divina potentia clare concionatur: Videbitis filium hominis sedentem ad dextram maiestatis, et hoc ipsum dici a Christo, quod sit vere et natura Deus, intelligant ipsi Pontifices, qui hanc vocem tanquam summam blasphemiam execrantur, ac ne quidem audiendum amplius iudicant, sed ut adversus manifeste blasphemum sine dubitatione pronunciant sententiam: Reus est mortis. Hic cogitetur quam horrendae tenebrae fuerint in illo coetu, qui vocatur populus Dei. Doctores et gubernatores praecipui tam sunt ignari promissionum et testimoniorum propheticorum de Christo, ut iudicent execrandam blasphemiam dici de Messia, quod sit filius Dei, sicut et alibi propter hanc ipsam vocem iudicant eum lapidandum esse. Minus mirandum est, sed aeque horrendum his postremis temporibus tantis tenebris oppressam fuisse Ecclesiam, tanquam praedictiones pictae sunt in hac ipsa historia, quae ostendit semper praecipue in Ecclesia esse hostes Christi Pontifices, qui pugnant de sua autoritate et potentia, oppressa luce verae doctrinae Evangelii de filio Dei.

Initium tertii actus ab ortu Solis sumamus. Nocte enim in aedibus Hannae et Caiphae, coram Pontificibus et Sacerdotibus confessio inter multas contumelias facta est. Nunc mane ducitur Christus ad magistratum politicum, ubi novum crimen ei obiicitur, plausibile apud ethnicum gubernatorem, videlicet hunc captivum fuisse autorem seditionum, et affectare regnum. Repetitur et alterum crimen, quod filium Dei se fecerit hic captivus. Duo igitur crimina omnium summa conferuntur in Christum, blasphemia et seditio, quorum alterum primam tabulam decalogi, alterum secundam evertit.

Recitemus autem breviter huius actus praecipuas partes: nam omnes enarrare nemo etiam in longissimo opere poterit. Primus locus est exemplum poenae, proditionis, cum Iudas horribiliter seipsum damnat, et sibi mortem consciscit, ut ingentes cruciatus abrumpat. Secundus, exemplum hypocrisis, quod Iudaei nolunt pollui ingressu in praetorium, interea vero polluunt se impio consilio interficiendi Messiae. Tertius, duplex accusatio, quod hic captivus sit blasphemus et seditiosus, sic inde usque ab initio certaminum Ecclesiae, cum imperiis et Pontificibus, Prophetae, Apostoli, et horum auditores, his duobus atrocissimis criminibus onerati sunt, quorum cogitatio homines moderatos multo durius excruciat, quam omnia crudelissima supplicia, quibus corpora lacerantur. Quartus, Confessio Christi de utroque articulo. Fatetur se filium Dei esse, et fatetur se Regem esse, et declarat regnum, inquiens: Re- gnum meum non est de hoc mundo, atque ita discrimen regni Messiae, quod est aeternum, et regni politici, quod cessaturum est, tradit. Quin- tus, Quare Iudaei dicant: Nobis non licet inter- ficere quenquam, ubi deploranda est horribilis mi- seria generis humani, quod non solum Iudaei, sed etiam Ethnici interficiunt Christum, ut significetur omnes homines reos esse mortis Christi, hoc est, propter omnium hominum peccata in toto genere humano Christum passum esse. Sextus, Herodes Christum contumeliis afficit ludens more Epicu- reorum, cum tamen dici vellet rex in populo Dei. Septimus, Confessio Pilati, quod hic captivus sit innocens, et rursus Pilati iniusticia hic describitur, qui ut aliquo modo dimittat Iudaeos placatos, in- nocentem Christum iubet flagellis caedi, et spinis coronari. Octavus, Vincitur Pilatus metu, cum minitantur Iudaei, se accusaturos ipsum apud Caesarem, quod hostem Caesaris dimittat. No- nus, Condemnatio Christi facta a Pilato, et dimis- sio Barrabae. Haec sunt praecipuae partes tertii actus, in quo consumuntur horae sex.

De primo.

Cum Iudas repraesentet omnium temporum haereticos, item desertores Evangelii, item con- siliarios potentum, qui artificiosa specie alienant animos principum ab Evangelio, aut alienatos confirmant, et in eis odia inflammant, in poena Iudae iram Dei omnes homines metuant, et vitent causas huius tam horrendae poenae. Periit Arius effusis intestinis, ut Iudas, periit Iuliani praefe- ctus, per os effuso stercore, et alii innumerabiles, nec desunt exempla nostrae aetati. Nam multi concionatores impii subito in ipsis concionibus extincti sunt. Timeamus ergo iudicium Dei, et in vera sententia Evangelii simus constantes, nec corrumpi nos sinamus pecunia, aut simulatione benevolentiae principum, aut spe bonorum, aut potentiae, ut adiuvemus furores eorum qui Evan- gelium oderunt.

De quarto articulo, videlicet de confessione Christi apud magistratum ethnicum, primum cri- men est, quod seditiose vocet se regem. Hic Christus expresse fatetur se esse regem, et tamen addit interpretationem: Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo. Hic discamus refutare imagina- tionem pontificiam, et multorum politicorum hominum, qui cogitant Ecclesiam esse politiam similem regno, in quo oporteat unum aliquod visibile caput esse, armatum potentia, et potestate condendi leges et interpretandi, laxandi et astringendi leges divinas et humanas. Et hoc caput volunt alligatum esse certo loco, et electioni certi collegii, ut in aliis regnis. Cum natura homines intelligant politica, libenter transformant Ecclesiam in talem humanam politiam. Sed haec imaginatio refutanda est propter multa incommoda quae sequuntur, quia tyrannica potestas hoc praetextu constituitur, qualis fuit pontificia, quae multos impios cultus et idola constituit: deinde doctrina de cruce et promissiones spirituales obscurantur. Nam oculi intenti in politica bona, his amissis putant Ecclesiam a Deo abiectam esse.

Ideo teneamus veram et eruditam definitionem regni filii Dei. Regnum Christi est gubernatio Christi colligentis sibi Ecclesiam per ministerium Evangelii, omnibus temporibus mundi, et liberantis eam a peccato et aeterna morte, et sanctificantis eam dato Spiritu sancto, ut sit aeterna ipsius haereditas, et mirabiliter defendentis et regentis eam in hac vita, ut vere invocet, et agnoscat exaudiri preces, ac celebret Deum, et resuscitantis eam ex morte ad vitam et gloriam aeternam.

In hac descriptione dicitur Christum non otiosum esse, ut fingitur in politica κακοζηλίᾳ, sed vere efficacem esse, et sic saepe definit hoc regnum Paulus, ut ad Ephes. 1.: Ipsum dedit caput super omnia Ecclesiae, quae est corpus eius ac plenitudo, id est, integrum corpus Christi, omnia in omnibus perficientis. Aperte affirmat Christum efficacem esse in membris Ecclesiae, idem postea dicit: Sedet ad dextram patris, dans dona hominibus.

Hac igitur nos consolatione sustentemus, quod vere filius Dei nobis adest, iuvat et propugnat nos, sive habeamus externa praesidia, sive simus oppressi cruce. Non propterea abiecit nos filius Dei, credentes in ipsum, etiamsi sumus in mediis suppliciis. Haec consolatio et invocatio filii Dei, et vera exercitia fidei valde obscurantur politicis imaginationibus.

Ecclesia igitur in hac vita non est similis regno mundi, et tamen est coetus visibilis, quia habet externa signa, per quae agnoscuntur membra, ubicunque terrarum sunt, videlicet Evan- gelium, Sacramentorum administrationem, con- fessionem Evangelii, multa testimonia Spiritus sancti in invocatione et in afflictionibus. Cum enim velit Deus se et filium suum innotescere omnibus hominibus, et invocari in genere huma- no, vult Ecclesiam suam conspici et exaudiri. Quare non putemus Ecclesiam esse ideam Plato- nicam, quae nusquam conspici possit, sed ubi- cunque est coetus, revera fundamentum retinens, id est, articulos fidei, et non defendens pertina- citer idola, ibi est vere haereditas Christi, et ali- qua membra electa sunt ad aeternam gloriam, etiamsi sunt dissimilia, alia imbecilliora aliis.

Quantum autem mali sit, transformare re- gnum Christi in politicum, hac ipsa imagine signi- ficatum est, quod Christus producitur in purpura et spinis coronatus. Nec dubium est hanc ipsam tristissimam speciem, ostensam esse hanc ipsam ob causam, quia hic error in Ecclesia late grassa- turus esset. Romanus Pontifex multipliciter in- jicit purpuram Christo, et coronat eum spinis, ut cum affirmat imperia mundi petenda esse a sede Romana, ut in corona Rodolphi Imp. scripsit: Petra dedit Petro, Petrus diadema Rodolpho. Sunt etiam spinae, canones de primatu et multis cere- moniis, quas fingit esse cultus, et quidem neces- sarios ad aeternam salutem. Sic peccant et Ana- baptistae, qui leges de Platonica communicatione rerum, et de nova forma magistratuum et judi- ciorum ferunt. Et passim alii indocti saepe tu- multuantur in civitatibus de negotiis civilibus, alienis a ministerio evangelico, inter hos qui sunt sanabiles, intueantur Christum amictum purpura et coronatum spinis, et desinant tumultuari de negotiis alienis ab evangelico ministerio ne capiti Christi infigant et ipsi spinas, et eum contumelia afficiant, sicut milites illudentes inquiunt: Ave rex Iudaeorum. Haec de regni Christi et politici discrimine, etsi breviter hoc loco dicta sunt, ta- men saepe sunt repetenda, quia mundus multipli- citer in confusione huius discriminis peccat.

De quinto.

Cur Iudaei dicant: Nobis non licet interficere quenquam, non frustra fit mentio servitutis Iu- daicae in hoc loco. Nam haec verba significant, qualis tunc gubernatio huius populi fuerit. Ro- mani concesserant Iudaeis αὐτονομίαν in cultu et iurisdictione inferiori, sed demerant eis iuris- dictionem superiorem, id est, iudicia rerum ca- pitalium, ut norunt mediocriter docti, saepe in gubernatione has partes a diversis possideri. Ideo autem haec recitantur, ut discamus convenire hanc historiam ad tempus Messiae praedictum in Pro- phetis, qui praedicunt Christum venturum ces- sante regno Iuda paulo ante dissipationem secun- dam gentis Iudaicae, ut in Daniele clare dicitur. Hic vero etiam consideretur, quomodo Deus ser- vet suam Ecclesiam in media servitute, ut disca- mus, non propter humana praesidia Ecclesiam manere perpetuo. Erat testimonium irae Dei, quod subiecerat populum Romanis, quorum im- peria satis dura et cruenta erant, multi haeredes vitae aeternae crudeliter interficiebantur, et mili- tum petulantia dissipabatur disciplina. Interim tamen, ut possent manere doctrina et cultus, Deus in inferiore iurisdictione voluit Iudaeis αὐτονο- μίαν concedi, sicut nunc sub Turcis sunt Eccle- siae in multis locis.

Hoc igitur exemplo discamus, non humanis consiliis aut viribus servari Ecclesias, et cum ser- vitute opprimimur, sciamus tanquam poenam to- lerandam esse, nec tamen propterea Ecclesiam a Deo abiectam esse, aut sine custode esse. Vaga- bantur et illo tempore, et antea in Iudaea exerci- tus Parthici, Romani, Herodiani, ac mirum est, in tantis latrociniis tamen defensas esse, et serva- tas virgines, et matronas Deum vere colentes, ut Elizabeth, Annam, Mariam, et alias innumera- biles. Ut igitur pii tunc servati sunt, et defensum est ministerium, Ita sciamus nunc quoque Deum Ecclesias servaturum esse, etiamsi fuerint oppres- sae servitute. Et quidem exemplum gentis Iudai- cae significat, etiam nunc postremis temporibus duram et tristem servitutem futuram esse, quam ut Deus mitiget, oremus.

## 19:1 Argument
Chapter XIX.

The fourth act, beginning almost from the start of the sixth hour, contains three hours, and somewhat more. For Christ died at the ninth hour, and since there were seasonal hours used at that time, let us know that the sixth is the meridian hour, then indeed the ninth, which for us is the third from midday. Contained, however, in this act are the condemnation made by Pilate, the punishment of Christ, His words on the cross, death, and burial. But it has often been said already, that the greatness of these things cannot be set forth by the speech of any person, or by any volumes, but the thought of this wondrous counsel of God, and of the sacrifice of Christ, and of the benefit for which the Son of God was made a victim, must be repeated assiduously throughout one's whole life; nevertheless, I shall briefly recite some parts.

The first passage is: Pilate, fearing that he might be accused before Caesar, condemns Christ against his conscience, although he indeed shows beforehand by many signs that he disapproves of this very condemnation, and says that he will release this Jesus, as they were accustomed to release some prisoner at the feast. But the Jews prefer a robber and author of sedition; he washes his hands and says that he is innocent, which was a sign of a wounded conscience, for in truth he knew that he was not innocent: for he who commits a crime and he who consents to it deserve the same punishment. I will not say more about this passage, but let us here deplore that the blindness of Kings, Princes, and all powerful men is a madness, who in a similar way rage against the Church, incited by impious priests. And although they wish to shift the blame onto the priests, saying that they ought to follow the authority of the Church, yet in truth they are and will be guilty before God, because it was not commanded to the priests alone that they should know the Gospel, but it was said to all men concerning Christ: Hear him, and it was said specifically to kings: And now, O kings, understand; be instructed, you who judge the earth.

The name Gabbatha signifies an elevated place, from the word Gaba, which is height, and the allegory warns that eminences and supreme powers war against God, and rage against Christ and the Church, just as the whole history of the world shows has most horribly happened for the most part. Here also, with a most sad voice, the Jews condemn themselves, saying: That they have no king but Caesar; they openly deny the Messiah, and they prophesy that they will have Caesar—that is, not the Messiah the Savior, but Caesar Titus, who a little later is going to destroy the entire Jewish polity with great cruelty. Moreover, Caesar signifies the same as cruel; they even openly cry out: Let his blood be upon us and our children. It is necessary for all the pious to shudder, hearing or thinking of this voice; but when we consider this great madness of this people, let us be stirred up to ask with true and ardent prayers that we may be governed by God, lest we fall into similar insanity and madness.

The second passage is: The soldiers lead Christ out, and lay the cross upon him.
