And the opinion of these, whether many or few, is a confession. And these can be helped by the confession of the saints who were before, just as we regarding the three persons are helped by Gregory Thaumaturgus, by Irenaeus, by the confession of the Nicene Synod; likewise regarding the baptism of infants we are helped by the sincere testimonies of the ancient Church, as it is written in Luke 22: And you, when you have turned, strengthen your brothers.

Now he who acknowledges that he is convinced by the word of God obeys the judgment because of the word of God, not because of the rank of the judges: and although the hearer is reminded by the voice of the judges, nevertheless faith rests on the divine testimony, as in this saying: In the beginning was the Word. But many, because they do not wish to be convinced by the word of God, afterwards also contradict, just as

the Arians afterwards also contradicted the Nicene Synod: nor does a declaration have validity because of the rank or number of the judges, as in a political judgment.

But let someone say here: Will there therefore never be an end to dissensions in the Church? I answer: There is no end as in empires, but eventually God removes the blasphemers, just as He destroyed the Jewish Synagogue, the Manichaeans, the Arians, and others. Even after the Apostles' decree concerning the law, nevertheless many remained who retained circumcision and other Mosaic ceremonies.

Another dissimilarity.

In political judgments, both parties can be obligated before the sentence to promise that they will obey the judgment. But in judgments of doctrine in the Church, pious men should by no means obligate themselves before the sentence, because men can err, and often the greater part in Synods is fascinated by evil opinions, as in the Synod of Sirmium; although it was specious, and great men from the Greek and Latin Church had gathered, nevertheless a notable error occurred: they removed the word ὁμοούσιος from the Symbol, and in its place they wanted to insert ὅμοιος, that is, similar, so that this equivocation might remove the dissension, but because the ambiguity obscured the truth and confirmed the Arians, those who judged rightly after the Synod of the Church did not want to admit this corruption.

For the truth is not bound to the greater number, nor to the Roman Bishop, or to the title of Bishops, because it is written in Romans 2: God does not accept the person of man. And in John 1 it is written that the true Church is not a gathering sprung from natural propagation, or collected by human colleges and ordinations, as are the colleges of Bishops: but born of God, according to these words: Who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

And there were many impious Synods, in which, however, great men participated, such as that of Sirmium and Seleucia under Constantius, who, when he had called the Bishops to Nicaea to make a decree contrary to the previous Nicene Synod, were dispersed by an earthquake. Afterwards, however, they gathered in Seleucia, where with the greatest contentions impious decrees were made against the ὁμοούσιον.

There are many such ancient examples. It is useful to consider the errors of recent Synods as well. In the Lateran Council, which is greatly celebrated as ecumenical, decrees were made concerning transubstantiation, and concerning enumeration in confession, and the recent Council of Trent made a decree that one must always doubt whether we are in grace. And it falsely twisted to this error the saying of Solomon in Eccles. 9: Man knows not whether he is worthy of love or hatred. Since, therefore, there is no doubt that in Synods the greater part can err, let no one bind himself before a judgment to obey the decision, but afterwards let him consider what has been pronounced, and follow the rule: If anyone teaches another Gospel, let him be anathema, Galat. 1.

Let the pious also consider what many of the ancients judged concerning most assemblies, such as that Epistle of Nazianzen to Procopius the prefect, which I have appended here for the sake of the younger ones.

Gregory to Procopius.

I am so disposed, if the truth must be written, that I would rather avoid all assemblies of Bishops, because I have seen no end of any Synod that was good, or that removed evils rather than increased them. For the desire for contention and for preeminence, and rivalry (lest you think me harsh for writing thus) overcome reason, and someone judging a new crime is more quickly accused himself than he corrects others. Therefore I restrain myself, and I love this quiet, in which invocation is not hindered. But now I also have an illness excusing me in this excuse, drawing breath as if it were my last, and weakened in my whole body. You will therefore forgive me, and persuade the pious emperor not to attribute it to sloth, but to grant pardon to my sickness, on account of which he knows he granted me the power, when I prayed to him, to hide myself in this retreat, when he offered other splendid offices, etc.

Here someone might say: What is the use of the judgments of the Church, if they do not end discords? I answer: True judgments in the true Church are of much use, because God wills that there always exist a true confession of some, according to that saying in Psalm 149: His praise is the Church of the saints, and He wills that by the voice and testimonies of these, the present and future generations be instructed, and many infirm ones be confirmed, but afterwards God in His own time will restrain the contradictors, as He restrained the Jewish Synagogue.

It must also be considered what kind of assemblies come together to judge, whether only an impious Synagogue comes together, as for the condemnation of Stephen.

If such is the assembly, it is manifest that one must contradict impious decrees.

Latin:

Ecclesia Dei viventis columna et sedes veritatis.

Hic inserit Ecclesiae descriptionem et magno animi motu in hac ipsa commemoratione accendi- tur, ac celebrat magnitudinem bonitatis Dei, qui mirando consilio misit filium, et colligit aeternam Ecclesiam voce Evangelii, et in genere humano inter diabolorum furores, inter regum et impio- rum tumultus inter impiorum ruinas semper Ec- clesiae reliquias servat. Haec perpetuitas Eccle- siae est illustre testimonium praesentiae Dei et ve- ritatis doctrinae.

Primum autem nota sit definitio Ecclesiae, quam recte constitutam tenere propter multas cau- sas necessarium est. Multi enim nominant Ec- clesiam simpliciter regnum pontificium, ut Cai- phas nominabat Ecclesiam agmen cum ipso con- iunctum, erroribus, sacrificiis, officiis et tradi- tionibus. Alii omnino removentes externam spe- ciem, loquuntur de Ecclesia invisibili tanquam de idea Platonica, quae nusquam cernitur aut exauditur. Et propterea vagantur, et nullius congregationis cives esse volunt: haec imaginatio etiam reprehendenda est. Etsi enim plerunque regna pontificia magna sunt, et obscurant veram Ecclesiam, et valde exiguus numerus est recte invocantium, ut tempore Zachariae magnum erat regnum Pharisaeorum et Saducaeorum: tamen semper aliquis visibilis coetus est alias maior, alias minor, qui est custos fundamenti, hic coetus quaerendus est, et ad hunc pii ubicunque sunt adiungere se debent sua confessione et simili in- vocatione. Sic igitur haec definitio.

Ecclesia in hac vita est coetus visibilis, am- plectentium Evangelium, et recte utentium sa- cramentis, in quo coetu Deus est efficax per mi- nisterium et multos ad vitam aeternam sanctificat, multi tamen in eodem coetu sunt, qui non sunt sancti, sed tamen de vera doctrina in externa professione cum sanctis consentiunt. Ut Mariae tempore erant Ecclesia visibilis, Zacharias, Si- meon, Ioseph, Maria, Elizabeth, Anna, et alii multi, horum doctrinam audientes et cum eis sentientes, et eadem invocatione Deum colentes, quorum alii plus, alii minus lucis habebant.

Talis coetus etsi non tenet regnum, sed pas- sim multi sparsi sunt, tamen conspicitur et audi- tur. Vult enim Deus in genere humano agnosci filium, sicut inquit ad omnes gentes, Psalmo 2.: Osculamini filium. Ideo vult Ecclesiam et conspici et exaudiri sonantem Evangelium de filio, sicut scriptum est Psalmo 18.: In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum.

visibilis, et praesidia necessaria ad defensionem regis, legum, iudiciorum et populi, et rex habet potestatem legis aliquas condendi, et ambiguas interpretandi. Et valet interpretatio propter regiam autoritatem.

Ut in regno Gallico sunt leges in aliquibus circumstantiis dissimiles ab aliarum politiarum legibus, et iudicia constituta sunt certis personis et locis: nec licet Gallicas controversias referre ad iudicia aliorum regnorum. Est et rex visibilis, et hic munitus est necessariis praesidiis, et habet potestatem interpretandi leges, et condendi aliquas novas. Tale est regnum pontificis Romani. Tale fuit et regnum impiorum pontificum in Israël. Talia regna in Ecclesia multi omnibus temporibus somniarunt.

Saepe autem horribiliter oppressa et obscurata est regnis idolatricis, ut Esaiae 1. dicitur: Nisi Dominus reliquisset nobis semen, sicut Sodoma facti essemus. Et Matth. 24.: Nisi abbreviati essent hi dies, omnis caro periisset. Et tamen reliquiae supersunt et subinde instauratur Ecclesia, ut Esaiae 46. dicitur: Etiam in senecta gestabo te etc. Et Esaiae 59.: Hoc est foedus meum cum eis, dicit Dominus, spiritus meus, qui est in te, et verba mea quae posui in ore tuo, non recedent ab ore tuo, et ab ore seminis tui in sempiternum. Item, Matth. 28.: Ego vobiscum sum usque ad consummationem seculi. Et in symbolo quotidie hoc profitemur: Credo esse Ecclesiam sanctam catholicam, Credo igitur promissiones Ecclesiae traditas firmas esse, Credo me exaudiri et recipi iuxta illas promissiones.

Sed discamus fugiendas esse has imaginationes, et Ecclesiam etsi visibilis est, tamen dissimilem esse imperiis politicis. Et regna illa pontificia significata sunt, quando filius Dei indutus est purpura, et laceratus corona spinea, sic contumelia afficiunt filium Dei pontifices, et scriptores, qui Ecclesiam in tale regnum transformant, ubi sine mandato Dei et leges et cultus instituuntur, de privatis Missis, de coelibatu, et aliis superstitionibus: et expresse damnantur alii homines, qui hos ritus non servant, et praeficitur Romanus Episcopus tanquam rex armatus potestate condendi novas leges, et novos cultus, et potestate interpretationis, et munitus suis et regum exercitibus.

Ac magna consolatio est, quod semper in tali coetu vocatorum sunt aliqui electi, quia cum semper sit aliquis numerus electorum, et non sit nisi inter vocatos, ut Paulus inquit Roman. 8.: Quos elegit hos et vocavit. Sciamus non alibi quaerendos esse electos extra coetum vocatorum, et libenter nos ad hunc coetum aggregemus: ideo dictum est, In hoc coetu Deum efficacem esse per ministerium, ibi enim convertuntur electi.

Sciamus igitur externam speciem Ecclesiae dissimilem esse imperiis politicis. Etsi aliquo modo similis est piae scholae, et tamen verum est, Monarchiam seu regnum in hoc visibili coetu esse invisibiliter, ita scilicet, quia filius Dei in hoc coetu verissime adest, et vere est rex et caput credentium, quos regit suo verbo et Spiritu sancto, et adiungit aeterno patri, sicut Ephes. 1. scriptum est: Omnia subiecit sub pedes eius, et ipsum dedit caput super omnia Ecclesiae, quae est corpus eius, congregatio integra perficientis omnia in omnibus. Sic dicit ipse Matth. 18.: Ego in medio eorum sum. Item, Iohan. 17.: Ego in eis. Psalm. 2.: Ego autem constituo regem meum super montem Zion.

Sed in hac vita manet haec dissimilitudo, quod mixti sunt electis in externa societate aliqui non electi et hypocritae, qui non sanctificantur, ut Matth. 13. de bonis et malis piscibus dicitur. Removenda sunt igitur Anabaptistarum somnia, qui Ecclesiam constituere volebant, in qua tantum sancti essent.

Et quia de visibili coetu loquimur, externa signa consideranda sunt, videlicet puritas doctrinae, et legitimus usus Sacramentorum. Interdum autem et externa miracula Deus addit.

Externa vero species ministrorum Evangelii et auditorum est aliquo modo similis Aristocratiae, sed alligata Evangelio, et sine potestate po- Etsi autem loquimur de visibili Ecclesia, tamen removenda est imaginatio et κακοζηλία, quae transformat Ecclesiam in regnum politicum seu mundanum, cuius propria haec sunt: Leges de forma gubernationis in moribus, iudiciis, et certis ritibus, ordine personarum, locorum, Rex litica et sine praesidiis corporalibus, ut Oseae 1.: Non in arcu et gladio, sed in Domino Deo suo salvabo eos, etc. Item in Zacharia capite 4.: Non in exercitu, non in robore, sed in spiritu meo etc. Nec imaginandum est, inclusam esse Eccle- siam in unius regni politiam, sicut scriptum est Matthaei 24.: Ecce hic est, ecce illic est. Sed membra verae Ecclesiae in diversa loca sparsa sunt, et alicubi Deus praebet hospitia publicae congregationi et verae doctrinae studiis, alias ma- gis alias minus commoda.

Valde autem offendit oculos sapientum haec deformis species, quae videtur esse ἀναρχία et dissipatio, nec videtur divinitus consociari et cu- stodiri, quod tam varie laceratum est, sine visi- bili capite, sine certa sede, sine ordine. Cum igitur sapientes ab hac specie abhorreant, con- currunt ad defensionem ordinariae potestatis, ut nominant. Et magna certamina ex hac iudicii dissimilitudine oriuntur.

Haec de specie externa Ecclesiae considerare necesse est, ne deformitate dissipationis deterrea- mur a veritate, sed regulam teneamus: Si quis aliud Evangelium docet, anathema sit. Post- quam diximus, quae et ubi sit vera Ecclesia, et qualis sit eius species, sequuntur iam hae quae- stiones.

Prima: An in ea sit veritas semper sine er- roribus. Secunda: Qualis sit potestas ministrorum. Tertia: Quae sit autoritas in iudicando, et in interpretatione.

De prima Quaestione.

An semper sit in Ecclesia veritas sine erro- ribus.

Respondeo: Hae propositiones, Ecclesia er- rat, item Ecclesia est columna et sedes veritatis, sunt synecdochae, et alia de aliis congregationi- bus intelligitur, et loquuntur de diversis generi- bus errorum.

Saepe est magna multitudo, quae titulum habet Ecclesiae, quae tamen non est vera Eccle- sia, sed coetus hostilis bellum gerens cum electis. Sicut erant Pontifices, Pharisaei, Sadducaei, tempore Zachariae. Hi nec fundamentum retine- bant, quod ita nominat Paulus 1. Corinth. 3.: Fundamentum aliud poni non potest, praeter id, quod positum est, quod est Iesus Christus. Defendebant enim Pharisaei et Sadducaei multos errores contra articulos fidei. Talis multitudo etiamsi titulum sibi arrogat, et dominatur in Ecclesia, tamen nequaquam est vera Ecclesia seu pars verae Ecclesiae. Ideo scriptum est Iohan. 8.: Vos ex patre diabolo estis, Et talem fuisse multitudinem in Israël manifestum est, fore etiam talem post Apostolos praedictum est, et res ostendit, Matth. 24.: Multi Pseudoprophetae surgent et seducent multos. Et 1. Timoth. 4.: Spiritus certo dicit postremis temporibus multos a fide discessuros esse, et credituros spiritibus impostoribus. Et horrenda est descriptio Antichristi 2. Thessal. 2.: Dominantis in templo Dei, horribili furore stabilientis idola et mendacia, quae pugnant cum articulis fidei. Haec tristissima descriptio loquitur de late dominantibus, et de magna multitudine, et de horrendis idolis et mendaciis. Hinc satis perspicuum est, multos, qui titulum habent Ecclesiae, errare: ac necesse est haec testimonia meminisse, ut opponantur allegantibus nomen Ecclesiae de impia congregatione. Sed de altera parte quae est vera Ecclesia dicamus. Etsi in hac quoque multi sunt infirmi, et alias plus, alias minus est caliginis, tamen in hac retinetur fundamentum, alioqui prorsus nulla esset Ecclesia. Semper autem aliquos esse electos ostendit Dominus, cum inquit Matthaei 24.: Breviabuntur hi dies propter electos. Item, semper verus est articulus fidei: Credo esse sanctam Ecclesiam catholicam. Item: Ego vobiscum sum usque ad consummationem seculi. Item, Esaiae 59.: Hoc est foedus meum cum eis, dicit Dominus, spiritus meus qui est in te, et verba mea, quae posui in ore tuo, non recedent ab ore tuo et ab ore seminis tui, deinceps et in sempiternum. Matth. 24.: In adventu filii hominis duo erunt in agro, unus assumetur, alter relinquetur. Etsi autem et haec vera Ecclesia edit confessionem, exauditur et conspicitur, tamen eam illa dominatrix Synagoga longe superat multitudine et splendore, ut tempore passionis Christi magna erat paucitas. Et Esaias inquit cap. 1.: Nisi Dominus reliquisset nobis semen. Et hic consideretur immensa bonitas Dei: sicut enim in Paradiso diabolus totum genus humanum perdere conatus est, ita perpetuo grassatur et perdit plurimos. Sed tamen reprimit eum filius Dei, ne universum genus humanum pereat, eripit et servat multos, et subinde instaurat Ecclesiam, ideo de hoc parvo coetu invocantium dicitur Danielis 11.: Et docti in populo docebunt multos, et ruent in gladio et flamma. Manent autem in hac vita, et in hac vera Ecclesia multae infirmitates, et quidem seniores magis agnoscunt et deplorant suam caliginem, et alienam, et suas sordes. Ideo inquit Paulus 1. Corinth. 3.: Alii super fundamentum extruunt aurum, alii argentum, alii stipulas. Extruunt aurum et argentum, cum refutant haereses et il- lustrant articulos fidei, Stipulas nominat contagia opinionum, in quibus aliquid erroris est, ut de Ceremoniis, ut multum stipularum Augustinus et alii sancti super fundamentum extruxerunt. Cum igitur Paulus inquit, Ecclesiam esse columnam et sedem veritatis, sciamus eum loqui de vera Ecclesia retinente fundamentum, et non propugnante pertinaciter idola et mendacia pu- gnantia cum articulis fidei: quia Deus semper in aliqua parte generis humani vult agnosci, etiamsi est exigua. Huc pertinet et dictum ad Ephes. 5. Ut sistat sibi Ecclesiam non habentem maculam, et ut sit sancta et inculpata, scilicet in vera do- ctrina, et vera fide Deum invocans, et iusta pro- pter filium Dei, imputatione et incoatione.

De secunda Quaestione.

De potestate ministrorum.

Expressum mandatum est Marci ultimo: Praedicate Evangelium omni creaturae. Et 2. Corinth. 3.: Sumus ministri novi testamenti, non literae, sed spiritus. Et Iohan. ultimo: Sicut misit me pater, sic ego mitto vos. Hoc mandatum complectitur ea, quae ad substantiam ministerii evangelici pertinent, videlicet praedi- cationem Evangelii, administrationem Sacramen- torum, excommunicationem contumacium, Ab- solutionem agentium poenitentiam, iudicia de vocatis ad ministerium evangelicum. Recte etiam addi possunt iudicia de doctrina, quia haec pars necessaria est in praedicatione Evan- gelii. Nequaquam vero ulla creatura potestatem habet nova dogmata condendi de essentia aut vo- luntate Dei, aut novos cultus instituendi, Sed filius qui in sinu patris est, enarravit nobis. De hoc dictum est Matth. 17.: Hunc audite. Item ipse inquit Iohan. 17.: Pater sanctifica eos in ve- ritate, Sermo tuus est veritas. Item Matth. 15.: Frustra colunt me mandatis hominum. Ideo falsa et impia est imaginatio Episcoporum, et similium qui tribuunt Episcopis aut aliis potestatem consti- tuendi novos cultus.

Est autem debita obedientia in illis, quae proprie ad miniserium pertinent, sancita in hoc dicto, Lucae 10.: Qui vos audit, me audit, Qui vos spernit, me spernit. In his dictis deducit nos Dominus ad ipsam Evangelii vocem, se vult au- diri in praedicatione ministrorum, nec constituit haec sententia regnum aliquod extra ministerium, sicut Episcopi postulant obedientiam traditioni- bus praestari, quae sunt extra vocem Evangelii. Praeterea nec habent ministri Evangelii potesta- tem gladio aut vi corporali coërcendi. De qua re alias saepe dicitur.

De tertia Quaestione.

Manifestum est oriri controversias etiam in vera Ecclesia, ut Actorum 15. apparet, ideo de iudiciis quaeritur: Qui sint iudices, et quae sit norma iuxta quam iudicari oportet, Et quae sit autoritas iudicum, et quomodo necesse sit obtem- perare iudicato.

Hic primum considerentur iudicia politica, ibi iudex est ipse rex aut praetor cum maiore parte consilii. Norma est in quolibet regno pro- priae leges, quibus obtemperare et iudicem, et litigantes necesse est. Autoritas iudicum talis est, ut cum in lege est ambiguitas, possint addere certam declarationem, et haec additio postea ha- bet vim legis propter gradum magistratus, et de- betur ei obedientia, etiamsi alicui litiganti secus videtur.

Ita dicitur iudicatum valere autoritate regia vel praetoria, quia Deus armavit magistratum po- liticum hac potestate, et negotia sunt subiecta rationi. Potest sapiens magistratus probabilem rationem videre, cur ita pronunciandum sit. Debetur autem ei obedientia propter gradum, ut sit pax et finis litium, et cum non obediunt con- demnati, iustum est eos cogere. Talem esse ordinem et autoritatem iudiciorum politicorum sciamus.

Postea consideretur, quatenus congruat haec imago ad iudicia Ecclesiae, quae aliquo modo dis- similia sunt iudiciis politicis.

Primum recte hoc dici potest, Ministros Evangelii debere praeesse iudiciis, et habere mandatum convocandi Ecclesiam ad cognitionem, ut in Actis cap. 15. Apostoli praesunt cognitioni, et adhibent alios ex coetu seniorum. Norma vero est verbum Dei, et symbola, quae certe sunt breves articuli, sumti tantum ex verbo Dei, iuxta hanc normam nunc quidem post Apostolos iudicare necesse est, iuxta hoc dictum, Gal. 1. cap.: Si quis aliud Evangelium docet, anathema sit.

Sed quid si sit ambiguitas? Hic primum respondeo: Non est ambiguitas in fundamento, id est, in partibus doctrinae necessariis, in libris propheticis, apostolicis et symbolis, dextre consideratis sententiis sine sophistica, et collato integro doctrinae corpore, Ut, etiamsi Samosatenus contendit esse ambiguitatem in dicto: In principio erat Verbum, tamen circumstantia textus eum convincit, quae oste... Verbum ibi intelligi oportere personam, quia textus inquit: Omnia per ipsum facta sunt. Item: Et Verbum caro factum est. Item Ioh. 8.: Antequam Abraham natus est, ego sum. Et: Abraham vidit diem meum.

Praeterea etiamsi quis sophistice contendit esse ambiguitatem, ut Anabaptistae de infantum Baptismo vociferantur, tamen cum semper sit vera Ecclesia, semper in aliquibus seu multis seu paucis manet vera lux. Hi in iudicando pronunciant, ostendunt suam confessionem, Narrant quid intelligant, et sunt certi ex ipso sermone prophetico et apostolico, et testimoniis Spiritus sancti in ipsis, iuxta illud Ephes. 1.: Obsignati estis Spiritu sancto.

Et sententia horum seu multorum seu paucorum confessio est, Ac possunt hi adiuvari confessione sanctorum, qui antea fuerunt, sicut nos de tribus personis adiuvamur a Gregorio Neocaesariensi, ab Irenaeo, a confessione Nicenae Synodi, item de baptismo infantum adiuvamur sinceris testimoniis antiquae Ecclesiae, sicut scriptum est Lucae 22.: Et tu conversus confirma fratres tuos.

Iam qui agnoscit se convinci verbo Dei, obtemperat iudicato propter verbum Dei, non propter gradum iudicum: et quanquam commonefit auditor iudicum voce, tamen fides nititur testimonio divino, ut in hoc dicto: In principio erat Verbum. Multi autem quia non volunt convinci verbo Dei, postea quoque contradicunt, sicut

Ariani postea quoque Nicenae Synodo contradice- bant: nec valet declaratio propter iudicum gra- dum aut numerum, sicut in iudicio politico.

Sed dicat hic aliquis: Nunquam igitur finis erit dissensionum in Ecclesia? Respondeo: Non est finis ut in imperiis, sed tandem Deus tollit blasphemos, sicut delevit Synagogam Iudaicam, Manichaeos, Arianos et alios. Etiam post Apo- stolorum decretum de lege, tamen manserunt multi, qui circumcisionem et alias ceremonias Mosaicas retinuerunt.

Alia dissimilitudo.

In iudiciis politicis utraque pars obligari po- test ante sententiam, ut promittat se obtempera- turam esse iudicato. Sed in iudiciis doctrinae in Ecclesia homines pii nequaquam se obligent ante sententiam, quia homines errare possunt, et saepe maior pars in Synodis est fascinata malis opinio- nibus, ut in Synodo Syrmiensi, quanquam spe- ciosa erat, et magni viri ex Graeca et Latina Eccle- sia convenerant, tamen insigne erratum accidit, sustulerunt ex Symbolo vocabulum ὁμοούσιος, et pro eo inseri voluerunt ὅμοιος, id est, similis, ut hic cothurnus tolleret dissensionem, sed quia ambiguitas obscurabat veritatem et confirmabat Arianos, post Synodum Ecclesiae recte sentientes hanc corruptelam admittere noluerunt.

Non est enim alligata veritas ad maiorem numerum, nec ad Romanum Episcopum, aut ad titulum Episcoporum, quia scriptum est Roma 2.: Deus personam hominis non accipit. Et Iohan. 1. scriptum est, veram Ecclesiam non esse coetum propagatione naturali ortum, aut humanis colle- giis et ordinationibus collectum, ut sunt Episco- porum collegia: sed ex Deo natum, iuxta haec verba: Qui non ex sanguinibus, neque ex volun- tate carnis, neque ex voluntate viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt.

Et multae fuerunt Synodi impiae, quibus tamen viri magni interfuerunt, ut illa Syrmiensis et Seleuciensis sub Constantio, qui cum vocasset Episcopos Niceam, facturos contrarium decretum priori Synodo Nicenae, terraemotu dissipati sunt. Postea vero convenerunt in Seleucia, ubi maxi- mis contentionibus impia decreta facta sunt con- tra ὁμοούσιον.

Talia exempla vetera multa sunt. Utile est et recentium Synodorum errata considerare. In Concilio Lateranensi, quod valde celebratur tan- quam οἰκουμενικὸν, decreta facta sunt de trans- substantiatione, et de enumeratione in confes- sione, et recens Tridentina Synodus decretum fe- cit, semper dubitandum esse, an simus in gratia. Et falso detorsit ad hunc errorem dictum Salo- monis Eccles. 9.: Nescit homo an amore vel odio dignus sit. Cum igitur non dubium sit, in Sy- nodis maiorem partem errare posse, nemo se obliget ante sententiam ad obtemperandum iudi- cato, sed postea consideret, quid sit pronuncia- tum, et regulam sequatur: Si quis aliud Evange- lium docet, anathema sit, Galat. 1.

Considerent etiam pii, quid multi veterum de plerisque congressibus iudicarint, Qualis est illa Nazianzeni Epistola ad Procopium praefectum, quam propter iuniores huc adscripsi.

Gregorius Procopio.

Sic affectus sum, si verum scribendum est, ut malim omnes Episcoporum conventus vitare, quia nullius Synodi finem vidi bonum, aut qui magis tolleret mala quam augeret. Nam cupi- ditas contentionis ac principatus, et aemulatio, (ne tamen me durum esse censeas sic scriben- tem) vincunt rationem, et citius aliquis iudicans de novo crimine ipse accusetur, quam alios cor- rigat. Propterea me reprimo, et hanc quietem amo, in qua non impeditur invocatio. Nunc vero et morbum habeo excusantem me in hac ex- cusatione, subinde tanquam extremum halitum ducens, et languefactus toto corpore. Ignosces igitur mihi, et persuadebis pio imperatori, ne tribuat ignaviae, sed veniam det aegritudini, propter quam scit se mihi precanti tribuisse pote- statem, ut me in hunc secessum abderem, cum alia splendida officia offerret etc.

Hic dicat aliquis: Quid prosunt iudicia Ec- clesiae, si non finiunt discordias? Respondeo: Vera iudicia in vera Ecclesia multum prosunt, quia vult Deus semper extare aliquorum veram confessionem, iuxta illud dictum Psalmo 149.: Laus eius Ecclesia sanctorum, Et vult horum voce et testimoniis erudiri praesentes et posteros, et multos infirmos confirmari, postea vero Deus suo tempore compescet contradicentes, ut compescuit Synagogam Iudaicam.

Considerandum est etiam, quales coetus ad iudicandum conveniant, an tantum Synagoga im- pia conveniant, ut ad Stephani condemnationem.

Si talis coetus est, manifestum est oportere de- cretis impiis contradici.

## 3:16
And manifestly great is the Sacrament etc.

In the Greek codices it is read thus: God was manifested in the flesh. Since, however, Paul had said before that truth is in the Church, he adds what this truth is, namely that God was manifested in the flesh, and justified by the spirit, as if he were saying: In other congregations there is not the truth of God, nor is the true God acknowledged there, nor is He worshipped there with true invocation, but only in this congregation, which is named the Church of the sons of God, is there true knowledge of God, and invocation of the true God, where God is acknowledged, who revealed Himself in the flesh, just as the Son Himself says in John 14: He who sees me, sees also the Father. Likewise: No one comes to the Father except through the Son.

Now here the whole doctrine must be embraced, which the Son delivered to the Church, according to that John 1: The Son who is in the bosom of the Father, He has declared Him to us. Let us know, therefore, that God is to be acknowledged and invoked just as He revealed Himself through this very Son, whom He sent with ineffable wisdom and goodness, so that by assuming human nature He might become a victim for us, and be a propitiator, redeemer, and high priest, and restorer of justice and eternal life.

Thus the true God is acknowledged and invoked, when we acknowledge this Son with true faith, and invoke the true God, who revealed Himself by sending, crucifying, and raising this Son, as we have often said elsewhere, that in invocation one must think about whom we are addressing, and one must discern the true God from all fictitious deities.

I invoke You, almighty and true God, eternal and only Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who revealed Yourself with immense goodness, and said concerning the Son, Hear Him, Creator of heaven and earth, of angels and men, and preserver, together with Your Son our Lord Jesus Christ, and Your Holy Spirit, wise, good, truthful, just, judge, chaste, merciful, most free, guardian of Your Church, whom our fathers invoked, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, David, the Baptist, Paul, have mercy on me, and remit my sins, and justify me through and on account of Jesus Christ Your only-begotten Son our Lord, crucified for us and raised, Your λόγον καὶ εἰκόνα, whom You willed to be a victim for us, both mediator and intercessor, by a wonderful and ineffable counsel and immense goodness, sanctify my heart and soul with your Holy Spirit, rule and teach me, preserve the Church etc.

In such a form of invocation there is a reminder concerning the invocation of the true God, and concerning the separating of the invocation of the Church from that of the heathen.

Latin:

Et manifeste magnum est Sacramentum etc.

In Graecis codicibus sic legitur: Deus mani- festatum est in carne. Cum autem antea Paulus dixisset, in Ecclesia veritatem esse, addit, quae sit haec veritas, scilicet quod Deus manifestatus sit in carne, et iustificatus per spiritum, quasi dicat: In aliis congregationibus non est veritas Dei, nec ibi verus Deus agnoscitur, nec vera in- vocatione ibi colitur, sed tantum in hac congre- gatione, quae nominatur Ecclesia filii Dei, de Deo vera noticia, et veri Dei invocatio est, ubi agnoscitur Deus, qui se in carne patefecit, sicut ipse filius dicit Iohan. 14.: Qui videt me, videt et patrem. Item: Nemo venit ad patrem nisi per filium.

Iam hic tota doctrina complectenda est, quam filius tradidit Ecclesiae, iuxta illud Ioh. 1.: Filius qui est in sinu patris, ipse enarravit nobis. Sciamus igitur sic agnoscendum et invocandum esse Deum, sicut se patefecit per hunc ipsum filium, quem inenarrabili sapientia et bonitate misit, ut assumta humana natura fieret victima pro nobis, et esset propiciator, redemtor, et summus sacerdos, ac restitutor iusticiae et vitae aeternae.

Ita verus Deus agnoscitur et invocatur, cum hunc filium vera fide agnoscimus, et verum Deum, qui se hoc filio misso, crucifixo, et resuscitato patefecit, invocamus, sicut alias saepe diximus, in invocatione cogitandum esse, quid alloquamur, et discernendum esse verum Deum ab omnibus com- mentitiis numinibus.

Invoco te omnipotens et vere Deus, aeterne et unice pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui te patefecisti immensa bonitate, et dixisti de filio, Hunc audite, conditor coeli et terrae, angelorum et hominum, et conservator, una cum filio tuo Domino nostro Iesu Christo, et Spiritu sancto tuo, sapiens, bone, verax, iuste, iudex, caste, misericors, liberrime, custos Ecclesiae tuae, quem invocaverunt patres nostri, Abraham, Isaac, Iacob, Moyses, David, Baptista, Paulus, miserere mei, et remitte mihi peccata mea, et iustifica me per et propter Iesum Christum filium tuum unigenitum Dominum nostrum, crucifixum pro nobis et resuscitatum, λόγον καὶ εἰκόνα tuum, quem voluisti pro nobis esse victimam, καὶ μεσίτην καὶ ἱκέτην, mirabili et inenarrabili consilio et immensa bonitate, sanctifica cor et animam meam Spiritu sancto tuo, rege et doce me, serva Ecclesiam etc.

In tali forma invocationis commonefactio est de veri Dei invocatione, de segreganda invoca- tione Ecclesiae ab ethnica.

## 3:16
Justified by the spirit.

That is, Christ was declared by the giving of the Holy Spirit, and by miracles performed through the Holy Spirit, and he was declared in such a way that it is certain that he is truthful and righteous and that the Gospel is not a fable. For the Holy Spirit gave testimony publicly through miracles, as the Lord says in John 16: The Spirit will glorify me. And privately he confirms the hearts of believers, when he raises them up in the midst of death, and delivers us from sin, and from the sorrows of hell by true consolation, which is felt in the hearts, and is the beginning of eternal life, as it is said in Romans 8: You have received the spirit, by which we cry Abba Father, the Spirit himself bears witness to our spirit that we are children of God.

Let the younger students diligently observe the phrase in the word 'was justified,' and consider how it is used in every place.

Seen by angels.

I think that a secret and great matter is signified when he says that Christ was seen by good and evil angels. The good angels see the causes of all the works of God, and why he willed that the human race be redeemed in this way, and what the union of the divine and human nature is like, and they serve this Lord, as Gabriel is the messenger to Mary in Luke 1. An angel comes to the Lord in his agony to strengthen him in Luke 22. They serve him also in the defense of the Church in Psalm 34 and Hebrews 1. In all these things they rejoice in the wisdom and goodness of God, and they celebrate God with thanks in huge and ineffable joy, and they rejoice to be partners in the ministry for the salvation of men, because they want God to be honored by many, and they truly love us, and they grieve that many men perish.

Concerning this wisdom and joy of the angels, Peter says in 1 Peter 1: Which things the angels looking into rejoice. On the contrary, there were, are, and will be great struggles with evil spirits, Matthew 4: The tempter approached him. And John 14: The Prince of the world comes, and has nothing in me.

These also are illustrious testimonies of the presence and goodness of God, and at the same time huge miracles, that the nations were called to the fellowship of the Gospel, that many were truly converted, and showed their confession amidst such great persecutions.

But the most illustrious testimony is the resurrection of Christ, and his ascension into heaven, seen by the eyes of a great multitude.

Concerning these manifestations of God and testimonies he says that the truth is in the Church, so that we may most firmly conclude that only in this assembly, in which the foundation is retained, that is, the articles of faith uncorrupted, is there the true knowledge and invocation of God, as it is often said elsewhere: He who does not believe in the Son, the wrath of God remains upon him, John 3.

Latin:

Iustificatus per spiritum.

Id est, Christus declaratus dato Spiritu sancto, et factis miraculis per Spiritum sanctum, ac ita declaratus est, ut constet veracem et iustum esse et Evangelium non esse fabulosum. Nam Spiritus sanctus et publice testimonium dedit per miracula, sicut inquit Dominus Iohan. 16.: Spi- ritus me glorificabit. Et privatim confirmat corda credentium, cum erigit ea in media morte, et liberat nos a peccato, et ex doloribus inferorum vera consolatione, quae sentitur in cordibus, et initium est vitae aeternae, ut Roman. 8. dicitur: Accepistis spiritum, quo clamamus Abba pater, ipse spiritus testimonium praebet spiritui nostro, quod simus filii Dei.

Diligenter autem observent iuniores phrasin in verbo Iustificatus est, et considerent, quo- modo quolibet loco usurpetur.

Conspectus Angelis.

Existimo rem arcanam et magnam significari, cum ait, conspectum esse Christum ab angelis bonis et malis. Vident boni angeli causas om- nium operum Dei, et quare sic redimi voluerit genus humanum, et qualis sit copulatio divinae et humanae naturae, et serviunt huic Domino, ut Gabriel est nuncius ad Mariam Lucae 1. Ve- nit angelus ad Dominum in agone ad eum con- firmandum Lucae 22. Serviunt ei et in defen- sione Ecclesiae Psalmo 34., Ebrae. 1. In his rebus omnibus laetantur sapientia et bonitate Dei, et Deum grati celebrant ingenti et inenarrabili lae- titia, et gaudent esse socii ministerii pro salute hominum, quia volunt Deum honore a plurimis affici, et nos vere diligunt, et dolent multos ho- mines perire.

De hac angelorum sapientia et laetitia dicit Petrus 1. Petri 1.: Quae angeli intuentes lae- tantur. Contra vero cum malis spiritibus magna certamina fuerunt, sunt et erunt, Matthaei 4.: Accessit ad eum tentator. Et Iohannis 14.: Ve- nit Princeps mundi, et non habet in me quid- quam.

Sunt et haec illustria testimonia praesentiae et bonitatis Dei, et simul ingentia miracula, quod gentes ad societatem Evangelii vocatae sunt, quod multi vere conversi sunt, et confessionem inter tantas persecutiones ostenderunt.

Maxime vero illustre testimonium est resur- rectio Christi, et ascensio in coelum conspecta magnae multitudinis oculis.

De his patefactionibus Dei et testimoniis in- quit, in Ecclesia veritatem esse, ut firmissime sta- tuamus tantum in hoc coetu, in quo retinetur fundamentum, id eat, articuli fidei incorrupti, veram agnitionem et invocationem Dei esse, sicut saepe alias dicitur: Qui non credit in filium, ma- net ira Dei super eum, Ioh. 3.

## 4:1 Argument
Chapter four.

In the first chapter he briefly embraces the sum of the doctrine, where he speaks of the distinction between the Law and the Gospel. Likewise when he says: Wage a good warfare, having faith and a good conscience. In the second chapter he speaks of the exercises of faith, of invocation, and of other good works. In the third chapter of the ministry and of the Church.

Now in the fourth chapter he adds most grave admonitions, that the Church may take heed, and not be deceived by false dogmas: for just as a physician points out what is healthy, and commands to avoid things harmful to health, so in teaching it is necessary that both be done. True doctrine must be proposed, and it must be shown which false opinions are to be avoided and exploded.

Three things, however, should be considered here especially. First, he says by name that the Devil is the author of impious opinions and vicious traditions, just as it is said of Judas in Luke 22: Satan entered into his heart. Therefore, when we read or hear the frenzies of Marcion, the Manichaeans, and the like, and the Anabaptists, which seem not to fall to men, let us be terrified and know that such men are dwellings of devils, and are not ruled by the powers of nature, but are impelled by devils. Let prayer therefore be more ardent, as the Lord says in Luke 22: Pray, that you may not enter into temptation. And the Prophet says in Psalm 118: Deal with thy servant according to thy mercy, and teach me thy justifications. Secondly, Paul affirms that many will certainly spread and defend evil doctrines in the Church; therefore, let us not flatter ourselves with a sense of security because of the title, so as to think that no errors cling to this multitude which is called the Church.

Thirdly, he says expressly, and sets forth certain examples of traditions in particular, so that it may be recognized which Bishops and Doctors are to be avoided, and which are the impious traditions. Wherever, therefore, these marks are found, it is certain that the defenders of such errors are not members of the true Church, but organs of the devil.

This admonition greatly confirms pious and modest men against the terrible clamors of adversaries, who oppose us with the name of the Church as if it were a Gorgon to be venerated, and shout that the principal part of the Church is the Bishops and the Mass-priests. Against these, in turn, these sayings must be constantly opposed, in which the divine voice affirms that devils are the authors of such traditions, and specifically of the prohibition of marriage and the distinction of foods.

Latin:

Caput quartum.

In primo capite breviter summam doctrinae complectitur, ubi de discrimine Legis et Evan- gelii dicit. Item cum ait: Milita bonam mili- tiam, habens fidem et bonam conscientiam. In secundo capite dicit de exercitiis fidei, de invoca- tione et de aliis bonis operibus. In tertio capite de ministerio et de Ecclesia.

Nunc in quarto capite addit admonitiones gravissimas, ut caveat Ecclesia, nec decipiatur falsis dogmatibus: ut enim medicus monstrat sa- lubria, et iubet vitare res nocituras valetudini, ita in docendo fieri utrunque necesse est. Propo- nenda est vera doctrina, et ostendendum, quae falsae opiniones vitandae et explodendae sint.

Tria autem praecipue hic considerentur. Primum nominatim inquit, Diabolum autorem esse impiarum opinionum, et vitiosarum tradi- tionum, sicut de Iuda dicitur Lucae 22.: Satanas intravit in cor eius. Ideo cum legimus vel audi- mus furores Marcionis, Manichaeorum et simi- lium, et Anabaptisticos, qui videntur non cadere in homines, expavescamus et sciamus tales ho- mines habitacula esse diabolorum, et regi non naturae viribus, sed impelli a diabolis. Sit igi- tur precatio ardentior, sicut Dominus inquit Lucae 22.: Orate, ne intretis in tentationem. Et Propheta inquit Psalm 118.: Fac cum servo tuo secundum misericordiam tuam, et iustificatio- nes tuas doce me. Secundo affirmat Paulus, certo multos in Ecclesia sparsuros et defensuros esse mala dog- mata, non igitur securi nobis blandiamur propter titulum, ut cogitemus nullos errores in hac mul- titudine haerere, quae nominatur Ecclesia.

Tertio diserte inquit, et in specie ponit quaedam exempla traditionum, ut agnosci possit, qui Episcopi et Doctores vitandi sint, et quae sint impiae traditiones. Ubicunque igitur hae notae inveniuntur, certum est defensores talium errorum non esse membra verae Ecclesiae, sed organa diaboli.

Haec admonitio valde confirmat pios et mo- destos homines contra terribiles clamores adver- sariorum, qui opponunt nobis tanquam Gorgo- nem venerandum nomen Ecclesiae, et vociferan- tur Ecclesiae praecipuam partem esse Episcopos et Sacrificulos. His rursus constanter opponenda sunt haec dicta, in quibus vox divina affirmat diabolos autores esse talium traditionum, ac no- minatim prohibitionis coniugii, et discriminis ciborum.

## 4:1
Concerning the last times.

Although all ages from the beginning of the human race have had many great confusions of religions, wars, and devastations, yet the divine voice often testifies that in the final old age of the world there will be greater confusions than there were before. And evils grow for three reasons: First, because with accumulated sins, greater punishments follow. Second, in these very sins and punishments, nature becomes more languid and discipline more dissolute. Third, because the rage of the devils grows, who, now knowing that the day of judgment is at hand, in which their malice will be openly shown to all angels and men, rage more fiercely against the Church out of hatred for the Son of God.

Let us consider these great dangers of our age in some way, and, becoming terrified, let us be more vigilant in learning, more modest in all business, and more ardent in seeking help. Let us also look at the promises specifically made to the last age, as in Isaiah 46: Even in old age and gray hairs I will carry you. And Psalm 71: Do not cast me off in the time of old age, when my strength fails. Likewise: Even in old age do not forsake me. By these thoughts let us rouse ourselves to vigilance and to prayer.

This admonition is also useful for this purpose, that we may not, disturbed by scandals, think that there is no Church of God, but that we may know that among these very confusions there is nevertheless some true Church, and that we may learn where it is to be sought, and join ourselves to it, and in it invoke the true God in the true knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ with firm faith and hope, and determine that the promises are valid for us, and always console ourselves with this article: I believe in the holy catholic Church. Likewise, Matt. 28: I am with you even to the end of the age. Likewise, 1 Cor. 11: Do this until he comes.

Many will fall away from the faith.

It is a necessary diligence to consider the differences of professions in the human race. Heathens, Jews, and Mahometans openly profess that they are enemies of Christ and the Gospel, and they openly reject the symbols. These can easily be recognized. But let our hearts first be fortified against them, just as antiquity collected many refutations against the Heathens, which it is useful to consider.

The first and most illustrious confirmation of the Church is the miracles inimitable by creatures, which testify that this doctrine was delivered by God, such as the resurrection of the dead, the repression of the course of the sun, childbirth in an exhausted age, and the leading out from Egypt. God wants us to look at these testimonies, because they were made and written for this reason, that they might be testimonies, and also that we might recognize that this is truly God who revealed himself by these testimonies, and distinguish him from all fictitious deities, just as in the first commandment he alleges the revelation: I am the Lord your God, who led you out of Egypt.

Although such things do not happen daily, yet those deeds were known to many, and are recounted by those worthy of belief. Furthermore, the Church is never without miracles, even if they do not strike the eyes in the same way: and the preservation and restoration of the Church and the evangelical ministry, which so many kings and evil doctors have tried to destroy with immense rage, is a perpetual miracle. Other sects, even if they have lasted for some time, yet once oppressed, are not restored.

The second confirmation is the antiquity of our doctrine. For since it is consistent that God revealed himself to the human race, and no doctrine concerning revelation exists that is older, indeed, it cannot even be known whence, by whom, or at what time the heathen religions were delivered: it must be confessed that this most ancient doctrine is to be embraced above others. And it is useful to compare histories, and to observe the signs of antiquity.

The third confirmation is firm, the prophecies concerning kingdoms, which, since the event has shown them to be true, it is manifest that both the human race is ruled by God, and this doctrine is from God.

Fourth, the comparison of doctrines. The heathens only teach the law, and indeed they corrupt it, because they invent many monstrous and abominable things about idols, and permit foul lusts. Afterwards, nothing certain is said by the heathens concerning the remission of sins, or concerning the causes of calamities in the human race. It is manifest, therefore, that their doctrine is insufficient, and does not show liberation from evils. It is useful to think upon this comparison, because it shows the kinds of doctrines, the distinction between the law and the Gospel.

Fifth, the Holy Spirit, vivifying hearts in true consolation, shows the truth and efficacy of the Gospel, just as the Lord says in John 16: When the Spirit of truth comes, he will lead us into all truth. And Rom. 8: The Holy Spirit gives testimony to our spirit, that we are the children of God. Thus Adam had external and internal testimonies: outwardly he heard the divine voice, inwardly he felt himself being liberated from death and being vivified.

These causes concerning the distinction between the heathens and the Church are to be considered often and attentively.

It is easier to refute the Jews who fight against the Church, who profess that they agree with the Prophets: for from these they can be convinced that the doctrine of the Apostles agrees with the prophetic. However, the Jews dissent from us concerning the Messiah, whom they deny to be the coeternal Son of God, they deny the Passion, they deny that he gives righteousness and eternal life, they contend that he will have a political kingdom, etc. These principal errors can be clearly refuted from the testimonies of the Prophets.

The Mahometans differ little from the impious Jews, nor yet do they receive the Prophets, but they can be refuted by the circumstance of time. For since the Church existed at the beginning, but the dogma of Mahomet was born recently after the Apostles, about the six-hundredth year, and fights against the Prophets and Apostles: it is impossible for the Mahometans to be the Church of God. Moreover, the doctrine of Mahomet contains nothing except a particle of the law concerning works, then it adds blasphemies against the Son of God, and against the Holy Spirit, and certain superstitious rites and foolish satisfactions for offenses; thus the Mahometans reject the whole Gospel, and corrupt the law.

I have spoken about the heathens, Jews, and Mahometans, where it must be considered for each one from where refutations are to be taken. Now I will speak about those whom Paul calls those falling away from the faith. There are two kinds of these. Others openly deny some article of the creed, as the Manichaeans posited two coeternal principles, Good and Evil. Arius denied that the Son of God is ὁμοούσιον to the eternal Father, Macedonius contended that the Holy Spirit is only a created motion in angels and in the hearts of men. Some have denied that the bodies of men will rise again. Such people, openly deleting some article of the creed, can easily be recognized, and are to be refuted from prophetic and apostolic testimonies, since they still wish to appear to agree with the Prophets and Apostles.

Others do not so openly delete the articles of faith, but secretly corrupt them with interpretations which dissent from the articles of the creed themselves, as the Pope and the monks retain the words of the creed, and yet add to certain articles false interpretations fighting against the Gospel, as specifically in these two articles, I believe in the remission of sins. Likewise: I believe in the holy catholic Church. For they corrupt the article, I believe in the remission of sins, because they add the interpretation, I believe that remission is given to others, not to me. Likewise: I do not believe in remission, but I doubt. I do not believe it is given freely on account of the Son of God, but is given on account of sufficient merits, on account of sufficient contrition and other works. Likewise, on account of satisfactions. These additions fight against the Gospel, which explains the whole article, I believe in the remission of sins.

The corruptions of the other article concerning the Church are also pernicious, because they invent that the Church is a political kingdom, in which it is necessary for Bishops to rule, and to establish dogmas and cults, and that the observation of these decrees is righteousness before God. This hypothesis having been posited, the Bishops proceed further, they constitute idols, and they pass laws accommodated to their own power and their own wealth, such as the law concerning marriage. Afterwards, they force men by bodily violence to obey, just as Nebuchadnezzar forced his nations to worship the statue.

Thus the corruptions of both articles lead minds away from the recognition of the mediator, and extinguish the light of the Gospel concerning the remission of sins, concerning faith, concerning interior worship, concerning true invocation, and they draw men away to idols. It is manifest, therefore, that those who embrace such corruptions fall away from the faith. These things become clear when the examples of all times are considered.

I deny the minor premise, because to bear children is a work which God both established and helps. But the fall of Eve is the proper work of a woman; it was of this fall that Christ was speaking.

I have recited these examples so that the younger generation may consider the games of sophistry and diabolical deceits, and may fortify themselves with true doctrine: for when the sources are correctly known, refutation is easy.

Whenever there has been a departure from the Word of God at the beginnings of errors, which at first seemed small, foul idols have gradually been added: just as in Israel impiety proceeded to human sacrifices and to obscene idols, in the Papacy the manifest idols are the invocations of the dead, the rushing to statues, the carrying about of the bread, and many profanations in the Lord's Supper. And there is manifest filthiness in the law of celibacy.

But as for what Paul said, that creatures are good things, understand it insofar as they are from God, and as their use has been ordained: but abuse is a vice in the will of those who abuse them. Therefore, Paul soon adds a sentence full of erudition, 'It is sanctified by the word and prayer,' that is, the use of marriage, food, government, and dominion becomes holy, granted by God, and pleasing to God through the word and prayer, that is, when the user follows the Word of God, which governs the use, and has knowledge of the Gospel, and knows that these external things are not eternal righteousness, but that God is gathering to Himself an eternal Church in this mortal life, and wills for the time being that life be sustained by food, and that propagation ordained by the Word of God remain, and that common society be preserved. Although these things are not eternal righteousness, nevertheless the goodness and wisdom of God shine in them, and God wills that we exercise and show obedience in their use.

Paul warns the Church about these frenzies, and expressly sets forth two signs: the prohibition of marriage and the distinctions of foods. Let us know, therefore, that the defenders of such errors are not the Church of God. And let us confirm ourselves by this testimony of Paul, so that we may know that those errors are rightly censured, and that the Church of God is the assembly which embraces the uncorrupted voice of the Gospel and disapproves of those errors. Furthermore, the doctrine concerning traditions and marriage has been delivered in its entirety elsewhere.

Latin:

De novissimis temporibus.

Etsi omnia secula inde usque ab initio gene- ris humani multas magnas confusiones religio- num, bella et vastationes habuerunt: tamen vox divina saepe testatur, in ultima senecta mundi maiores futuras esse confusiones, quam fuerunt antea. Et crescunt mala propter tres causas: Prima, Quia cumulatis peccatis sequuntur maio- res poenae. Secunda, In his ipsis peccatis et poenis natura fit languidior et disciplina dissolu- tior. Tertia, Quia rabies diabolorum crescit, qui iam scientes instare diem iudicii, in quo eorum malitia omnibus angelis et hominibus pa- lam ostendetur, odio filii Dei magis saeviunt in Ecclesiam.

Haec magna pericula nostrae aetatis aliquo modo consideremus, et expavescentes simus vigi- lantiores in discendo, et modestiores in omnibus negotiis, et ardentiores in petendo auxilio. In- tueamur etiam promissiones nominatim factas ul- timae aetati, ut Esaiae 46.: Etiam in senecta et canicie vos gestabo. Et Psalmo 71.: Non proii- cias me tempore senectae, cum deficiet virtus mea. Item: Etiam in senecta non relinquas me. His cogitationibus exuscitemus nos ad vigilantiam et ad precationem.

Prodest haec admonitio ad hoc quoque, ne scandalis turbati existimemus nullam esse Dei Ec- clesiae, sed sciamus inter has ipsas confusiones tamen aliquam esse veram Ecclesiam, et disca- mus ubi quaerenda sit, et nos ei adiungamus, et in ea verum Deum in vera agnitione Domini no- stri Iesu Christi firma fide et spe invocemus, et statuamus promissiones nobis ratas esse, et sem- per nos consolemur hoc articulo: Credo Ecclesiam sanctam catholicam. Item, Matth. 28.: Ego vobiscum sum usque ad consummationem seculi. Item, 1. Cor. 11.: Hoc facite donec veniat.

Multi deficient a fide.

Necessaria diligentia est considerare discri- mina professionum in genere humano. Ethnici, Iudaei, Mahometistae palam profitentur, se esse hostes Christi et Evangelii, et palam reiiciunt symbola. Hi facile agnosci possunt. Sint autem primum adversus hos munita pectora, sicut ad- versus Ethnicos vetustas collegit multas refutatio- nes, quas cogitare utile est.

Prima autem et maxime illustris confirmatio est Ecclesiae miracula inimitabilia creaturis, quae testantur hanc doctrinam a Deo traditam esse, ut resuscitatio mortuorum, repressio cursus solis, partus in effoeta aetate, eductio ex Aegypto. Haec testimonia vult nos Deus intueri, quia ideo facta et scripta sunt, ut sint testimonia, item ut agnoscamus hunc vere esse Deum, qui se his te- stimonitis patefecit, et discernamus eum ab om- nibus commentitiis numinibus, sicut in primo praecepto allegat patefactionem: Ego sum Domi- nus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de Aegypto.

Etsi autem non fiunt similia quotidie, tamen facta illa multis nota fuerunt, et a fide dignis re- citantur. Praeterea nunquam Ecclesia caret mira- culis, etiamsi non pariter incurrunt in oculos: et perpetuum miraculum est, conservatio et instau- ratio Ecclesiae et ministerii evangelici, quod toties delere conati sunt immani rabie plurimi reges et mali doctores. Caeterae sectae etiamsi aliquandiu duraverunt, tamen oppressae non in- staurantur.

Secunda confirmatio est, Antiquitas nostrae doctrinae. Cum enim consentaneum sit, Deum se patefecisse generi humano, et nulla extet doctrina de patefactione antiquior, imo ne quidem sciri possit unde, per quos, quo tempore, ethnicae religiones traditae sint: fatendum est hanc anti- quissimam prae caeteris amplectendam esse. Ac utile est conferre historias, et signa antiquitatis observare.

Tertia confirmatio firma est, Vaticinia de regnis, quae cum eventus ostenderit vera esse, manifestum est utrunque, et a Deo regi genus humanum, et hanc doctrinam a Deo esse.

Quarta, Collatio doctrinarum. Ethnici tantum docent legem, et quidem corrumpunt, quia multa portentosa et abominanda fingunt de idolis, et tetras libidines permittunt. Postea Ethnici de remissione peccatorum, de causis calamitatum in genere humano nihil certi dicitur. Manifestum est igitur, eorum doctrinam insufficientem esse, et non ostendere liberationem a malis. Hanc collationem cogitare utile est, quia ostendit genera doctrinarum, discrimen legis et Evangelii.

Quinta, Spiritus sanctus in vera consolatione vivificans corda, ostendit Evangelii veritatem et efficaciam, sicut Dominus inquit Iohan. 16.: Cum veniet spiritus veritatis, ducet nos in omnem veritatem. Et Rom. 8.: Spiritus sanctus dat testimonium spiritui nostro, quod simus filii Dei. `Ita Adam habuit testimonia externa et interiora: foris audiebat vocem divinam, intus sentiebat se ex morte liberari et vivificari.

Hae causae de discrimine Ethnicorum et Ecclesiae saepe et attente considerandae sunt.

Facilius est refutare Iudaeos pugnantes cum Ecclesia, qui profitentur se assentiri Prophetis: ex his enim convinci possunt, Apostolorum doctrinam cum prophetica congruere. Dissentiunt autem Iudaei a nobis de Messia, quem negant esse filium Dei coaeternum, negant Passionem, negant eum dare iusticiam et vitam aeternam, contendunt regnum politicum habiturum esse etc. Hi praecipui errores refutari ex Prophetarum testimoniis perspicue possunt.

Mahometistae parum differunt ab impiis Iudaeis, neque tamen recipiunt Prophetas, sed refutari possunt a circumstantia temporis. Cum enim Ecclesia fuerit initio, dogma autem Mahometi recens sit natum post Apostolos, circiter annum sexcentesimum, et pugnet cum Prophetis et Apostolis: impossibile est Mahometistas esse Ecclesiam Dei. Nihil autem continet doctrina Mahometi, nisi particulam legis de operibus, deinde addit blasphemias contra filium Dei, et contra Spiritum sanctum, et superstitiosos quosdam ritus et stultas satisfactiones pro delictis; ita totum Evangelium reiiciunt Mahometistae, et corrumpunt legem.

Dixi de Ethnicis, Iudaeis et Mahometistis, ubi de singulis considerandum est, unde suman- tur refutationes. Iam dicam de his, quos Paulus nominat deficientes a fide. Horum duo genera sunt. Alii aperte negant articulum aliquem sym- boli, ut Manichaei posuerunt duo principia coaeterna, Bonum et Malum. Arius negavit filium Dei esse ὁμοούσιον aeterno patri, Mace- donius contendit Spiritum sanctum tantum esse motum creatum in angelis et in hominum cordi- bus. Aliqui negaverunt corpora hominum resur- rectura esse. Tales palam delentes articulum aliquem symboli facile agnosci possunt, et re- futandi sunt ex testimoniis propheticis et aposto- licis, cum adhuc videri velint assentiri Prophetis et Apostolis.

Alii non ita palam delent articulos fidei, sed occulte eos corrumpunt interpretationibus, quae dissentiunt ab ipsis articulis symboli, ut Papa et monachi retinent verba symboli, et tamen quibusdam articulis addunt falsas interpretatio- nes cum Evangelio pugnantes, ut nominatim his duobis articulis, Credo remissionem peccatorum. Item: Credo esse Ecclesiam sanctam catholicam. Corrumpunt enim articulum, Credo remissionem peccatorum, quia addunt interpretationem, Credo remissionem aliis dari, non mihi. Item: Non credo remissionem, sed dubito. Non credo gra- tis dari propter filium Dei, sed dari propter me- rita sufficientia, propter sufficientem contritio- nem et alia opera. Item, propter satisfactiones. Hae additiones pugnant cum Evangelio enarrante totum articulum, Credo remissionem pecca- torum.

Alterius articuli de Ecclesia corruptelae etiam perniciosae sunt, quia fingunt Ecclesiam esse regnum politicum, in quo dominari oporteat Episcopos, et condere dogmata et cultus, et ho- rum decretorum observationem esse iusticiam co- ram Deo. Hac hypothesi posita procedunt Epi- scopi longius, constituunt idola, et ferunt leges suae potentiae, suis opibus accommodatas, ut legem de coniugio. Postea vi corporali cogunt homines, ut obtemperent, sicut Nabuchodonosor coëgit suas gentes, ut statuam colerent.

Ita utriusque articuli corruptelae abducunt mentes ab agnitione mediatoris, et extinguunt lucem Evangelii de remissione peccatorum, de fide, de interiore cultu, de vera invocatione, et abstrahunt homines ad idola. Manifestum est igitur, eos qui amplectuntur tales corruptelas, deficere a fide. Haec fiunt illustria consideratis exemplis omnium temporum.

Nego minorem, quia parere opus est, quod Deus et condidit et iuvat. Sed lapsus Evae est proprium opus mulieris, de hoc lapsu Christus loquebatur.

Haec exempla recitavi, ut iuniores conside- rent ludos sophismatum, et diabolicas praestigias, et se vera doctrina praemuniant: nam recte cogni- tis fontibus refutatio facilis est.

Semper cum discessum est a verbo Dei ini- tiis errorum, quae primum exigua videbantur, paulatim accesserunt tetra idola: ut in Israël pro- cessit impietas ad humanas hostias et ad obscoena idola, in Papatu manifesta idola sunt invocatio- nes mortuorum, concursus ad statuas, circum- gestatio panis, et multae prophanationes in coena Domini. Et manifesta turpitudo est in lege coe- libatus.

Quod autem dixit Paulus, creaturas esse res bonas, intellige quatenus sunt a Deo, et sicut usus ordinatus est: abusus autem vitium est in voluntate abutentium. Ideo mox addit Paulus sententiam plenam eruditionis, Sanctificetur per verbum et precationem, id est, usus coniugii, cibi, imperii, dominii, fit sanctus, concessus a Deo, et Deo placens per verbum et precationem, id est, cum utens sequitur verbum Dei, quod regit usum, et habet noticiam Evangelii, Ac scit has res externas non esse iusticiam aeternam, sed Deum sibi in hac vita mortali colligere aeternam Ecclesiam, ac tantisper velle, ut vita foveatur cibis, et maneat propagatio ordinata verbo Dei, et conservetur communis societas. Quanquam autem hae res non sunt iusticia aeterna, tamen lucent in eis bonitas et sapientia Dei, et vult Deus nos in earum usu exercere et ostendere obedientiam.

De his furoribus praemonet Ecclesiam Pau- lus, et duo signa expresse ponit, prohibitionem coniugii, et discrimina ciborum. Sciamus igitur non esse Ecclesiam Dei defensores talium erro- rum. Et hoc Pauli testimonio confirmemus nos, ut sciamus recte taxari errores illos, et Eccle- siam Dei esse coetum, qui vocem Evangelii in- corruptam amplectitur, et improbat illos errores. Caeterum de traditionibus et de coniugio alibi do- ctrina integre tradita est.

## 4:4
Every creature of God is good.

He opposes this rule to the fanatical spirits who condemn marriage, foods, political order, the distinction of dominions, and judgments. For there have always been, are, and will be such hypocrites, as once Marcion, Tatian, the Manichaeans, the Pope, the Monks, and now the Anabaptists, who argue about the distinction of dominions as follows: It is not permitted for anyone to desire what belongs to another. All things outside the spirit are alien; therefore, it is not permitted to desire any such things, such as property.

And Paul signifies a most ample wisdom when he says that the use is made holy by the Word of God, that is, by the acknowledgment of the whole doctrine of God concerning eternal righteousness and concerning bodily life, in which He wills the eternal Church to be begun.

Paul also commands that prayer be added, that is, the petition for help, confession, and thanksgiving: because God wills that this bodily life also be an occasion for exercising and showing obedience; wherefore, concerning marriage, chastity, the education and instruction of offspring, common society, the whole political order, and the avoiding of homicides and thefts, He has delivered to us the Word, and in this most beautiful order, in which His own wisdom and goodness shine, He wills that fear, faith, hope, invocation, love, chastity, beneficence, and other virtues be exercised.

I answer: The major premise is true concerning what is alien, which by the political distinction of dominions pertains to another's dominion, according to that: 'Do not covet another's wife, nor another's things.' The minor premise is false, as is manifest: one's own wife is a thing outside the spirit; she is not called an alien thing in that way; foods are things outside the spirit, and yet they are to be desired.

Thus Tatian used to argue. It is written in the Gospel according to the Egyptians that Christ said to Salome, 'I have come to destroy the works of the woman.' To bear children is the work of a woman; therefore, Christ abolishes marriage.

Necessary wisdom in the Church is to understand correctly the distinction between Law and Gospel, and between eternal righteousness in the hearts and the use of bodily things, which God has ordained in a certain way by His word: because in this mortal life He wills the Church to be gathered, and that in the use of these very things faith, invocation, and other virtues shine.

But the Manichaean and Anabaptist rabble, bewitched by the devil, displays a new holiness, as if they had left the earth and were flying in heaven outside this society of life, and meanwhile boasts that it possesses miraculous inspirations. And because this hypocrisy is a lie, and they are not lacking in things in this life, they subsequently create confusions of lusts, and stir up seditions, and wish to establish a new Jerusalem, as often happens. For even long ago a tragedy similar to the one at Münster occurred in Phrygia in the town of Pepuza, which they called the new Jerusalem, and they had fanatical prophets there.

This admonition against the Anabaptists and similar fanatical spirits must be diligently considered. And for this reason Paul says: Food is sanctified by the word of God, so that he may teach those who use it how they may use things with a good conscience, just as he says elsewhere: Whatever is not of faith is sin, Rom. 14. The native meaning of that statement must be rightly held. It is not merely a legal statement, as many interpret it in this way: Whatever is prohibited by divine commands pertaining to us is sin.

Although this legal understanding is true, yet it does not yet render the whole meaning of the Pauline statement: but because mention is made of faith, it is necessary to include the Gospel. Nor should faith be understood only as knowledge of history, as they say: The honest works of a pagan man do not please God, because he is not in the Christian profession: but true faith must be understood, which approaches God with trust in the Mediator, and invokes Him. Where such faith is not, but the heart acts against conscience, or remains in doubt, as one hanging a thief, and yet thinking that he is acting against God, he cannot invoke God, and acts with contempt for God.

Therefore, let this rule of Paul be known, and let it be rightly understood and shine forth in all actions, and let us do nothing against conscience, and let conscience be governed by the word of God, and let invocation be able to approach, namely, everything that is not of faith is sin.

Bodily exercise is profitable for a little, godliness for all things, etc.

There is a useful distinction between necessary and unnecessary works, chosen for the sake of our exercise, such as fasts or other labors undertaken to restrain the body. And external observances have always produced many disputes in the Church, because either for the sake of order or for the sake of exercises, some external observances are instituted or undertaken by human counsel, which are afterwards depraved by superstition, when an opinion of merit, worship, or necessity is attached to them. Therefore, antiquity also censured superstition, according to the memorable saying of Athanasius: Virtue is the exercise of true knowledge and symmetry.

But in order that one may judge rightly concerning human rites, the whole body of doctrine must be held, just as Paul here also makes an antithesis of necessary and unnecessary things. Godliness is profitable for all things. He names godliness, however, as both faith and all necessary virtues, or all works commanded to us divinely. And it is a very significant statement that he says the promises of the present and future life are proposed to godliness, and he adds an express assertion: The saying is certain and to be embraced with firm assent.

This sweetest and most necessary doctrine concerning the two kinds of promises must be most familiarly known. And first, as far as the Gospel is concerned, it contains the promise of the remission of sins and the restoration of eternal life through the Son of God, and on account of Him, which is most manifest. For it is certain that this is the principal voice of the Gospel, that the Son of God was sent to abolish sin and death and to restore eternal life.

But why does he say that the Gospel has the promise of the present life, when the Church is subject to the cross? Likewise, when the Lord says in Matt. 24: They will kill you and you will be hated by all men for my name's sake. And Luke 9: The Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head? Are these predictions of death, not of the present life? But I answer: Both propositions are very true, and the Church is subject to the cross, and yet it has the promise of bodily goods, just as the Lord joins these in Mark 10: He will receive a hundredfold, but with tribulation. And Isaiah 30: He will hear your cry, and will give you bread and water in anguish and pain.

For since God wishes the Church to be thus begun and gathered in this mortal life, He preserves it, provides it with hospitality, crops, economies, polities, the ability to propagate offspring, and the Church, just as the Lord Himself says in Matt. 6: Your heavenly Father knows that you have need of all these things, Seek first the kingdom of God, and the rest shall be added unto you. Likewise, Psalm 32: He shall nourish and feed them in famine: indeed, for the sake of the Church, God preserves both other nations and bodily goods. But after the whole Church shall have been gathered, and there shall be no more elect in the human race, this mortal life will soon cease, and the final judgment will take place.

Moreover, the promise of bodily goods is general, not tied to a certain place, as it was tied to a certain place for the Israelites, and it is always valid in this life for the whole congregation. Therefore, God always preserves some Church of His in this life, even if many members are killed, just as if victory were promised to an army, the promise is valid and true, even if some soldiers are killed.

Secondly, the bodily promise should always be understood with the exception of chastisement and the cross. God wills that both faith and obedience be exercised in the bodily goods requested. He wills to guard the life and family of Abraham, but in such a way that Abraham is guided not only by human counsels, but by faith, by the invocation of God, and that he seeks and expects help from God, according to the words of Jeremiah 17: Cursed is he who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm. Likewise, Zechariah 4: Not by might, not by an army, but by my spirit, says the Lord.

He also wills that men know this, that He is truly angry at sins, and horribly punishes lapses, so that we may be more diligent in restraining ourselves: just as the most sorrowful punishments followed the lapses of David, Solomon, etc. And yet, among these punishments, some seed of the Church has always been preserved, as in the Babylonian exile.

Thus we see that the bodily promise is likewise valid for the glory of God, so that the acknowledgment of God may not be extinguished in the human race, and in our petition we should keep this end in view, Psalm 114: Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory. Likewise: The dead shall not praise thee, O Lord. Let us therefore exercise both faith and obedience in the petition and expectation of bodily goods, just as the Lord commands us to seek our daily bread, and let us execrate those foolish superstitions of theirs who do not wish to interpret this petition as concerning bodily things.

But let these four causes always be in sight, for which God both delivered bodily promises and wills those goods to be sought. The first is, Because He wills it to be understood that these goods are not scattered by chance without the counsel and will of God, but that God, by His own counsel, either fosters the powers of nature, or abandons them, or gives faculties, or does not give them. Therefore, let this faith concerning providence be first in us, that these goods are not scattered by chance without the counsel of God. For this faith is the foundation of petition and thanksgiving. And let some testimonies be known: Deut. 8: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the divine mouth. Deut. 30: He is your life and the length of your days. Acts 17: In Him we live, and move, and have our being. Matt. 10: All the hairs of your head are numbered. Prov. 10: The blessing of the Lord makes rich. Prov. 3: Poverty is from the Lord in the house of the wicked. Jeremiah in Lamentations chapter 3: Who is he that says these things come to pass without the Lord commanding it? Shall not both good and evil proceed from the mouth of the Lord? It follows, therefore, then the second cause. Since it is most certain that these goods are given divinely, God wills that faith be exercised in both ways, by petition and by thanksgiving; He wills that He be acknowledged as the Creator and Giver of life and sustenance; He wills that this be celebrated in petition and thanksgiving. As Psalm 50 says: Call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me. The third cause is, These promises are testimonies concerning the preservation of the Church in this mortal life; for they are given for this reason, that the Church may not perish, according to that of Psalm 114: The dead shall not praise thee, O Lord. Likewise Matt. 6: Seek first the kingdom of God, and the rest shall be added unto you. Fourth, all bodily promises are reminders of the spiritual one, namely, of the Son of God, because we cannot even invoke God unless we first know that we are received and heard for the sake of the Mediator. Let this faith shine forth in every petition, even of bodily goods: thus it is clear that when faith seeks bodily things, it is necessary that spiritual petition be exercised at the same time. Let this whole doctrine concerning spiritual and bodily promises be most known to all, and let it be exercised daily in invocation, in which public and private goods are to be sought, wholesome governments, peace, sustenance, good health, and other goods. In these exercises, the doctrine will become more clear, and faith will grow, which will experience that this invocation is not in vain. Let us also know that God demands these exercises, and that this invocation is a worship pleasing to God in believers. As he says

Psalm 50: Call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you.

Be an example of the believers in word, etc.

Although examples are more conspicuous in those who govern, yet this sentence of Paul is a common rule, which individuals should keep in view in the governance of their whole life. He names these members in order. Be an example in word, that is, in doctrine; teach rightly, speak rightly and not sophistically about doctrine, and warn others to avoid curious questions, false, improperly and perplexedly stated things. Finally, let the doctrine be clear, necessary for the exercises of faith, and for invocation, and for good morals, as was said above, let doctrine be profitable for edification.

Secondly, he says, in conversation. Here he signifies universal justice, that is, honest actions according to all the commandments of God; do not be infamous for any cause.

In love. He adds something to the previous member: he not only wants the external conversation to be honest and not infamous, but he also wants there to be love in the heart toward God and toward men; he wants you to be a lover of the common association with a true heart, pleasant and beneficial. A thief is infamous, but Paul wants not only for thefts to be avoided, but moreover for you to be beneficial with a true heart.

In spirit, that is, in zeal; he wants you to be so pleasant that you nevertheless do not connive at crimes and pernicious dogmas. But you should rebuke those worthy of rebuke in a legitimate manner.

In faith, that is, in consolation; in all dangers, let others see you show patience and constancy by faith in persecution and other sorrows, not seeking unjust aids, but expecting the help of God, and let others be instructed and confirmed by your consolation, just as Jeremiah rules and consoles the Church of his time by his faith.

He also adds chastity by name, which is to avoid all prohibited unions, and it is a necessary virtue, according to this saying, 1 Corinthians 6: Do not err, fornicators and adulterers will not possess the kingdom of God, and they become dwellings of devils who pollute themselves with prohibited unions.

Be diligent in reading, consolation, and doctrine.

For many reasons let this saying be most familiarly known to all.
